Document: [S0] Brother Man ( 1954 ) is a novel by Jamaican Roger Mais , about a Messianic folk Rastafarian healer , ' Bra ' Man ' ( in dialect ) John Power . [S1] The book is significant as the first serious representation of the Rastafari movement in literature . [S2] Mais foresaw the defining power of the Rasta movement to Jamaican society 20 years before the era of Bob Marley and Reggae mainstream . [S3] It is also significant as an exploration of life in the ghetto of Kingston . [S4] It shows how the people relate to leaders , both making them deities and throwing them away when they fail to entertain them . [S5] The novel is written in prose with a layout that is seemingly cinematic and episodic ; little is done to describe the environment beyond the claustrophobic ghetto of ' The Lane ' in the slums of Kingston , Jamaica .

Document: [S0] Beyond Good & Evil is a 2003 action - adventure video game developed and published by Ubisoft for the PlayStation 2 , Microsoft Windows , Xbox and GameCube platforms . [S1] The story follows the adventures of Jade , an investigative reporter and martial artist , who works with a resistance movement to reveal a planet - wide alien conspiracy . [S2] The player controls Jade and allies , solving puzzles , fighting enemies , and obtaining photographic evidence . [S3] Michel Ancel , creator of the Rayman series , envisioned the game as the first part of a trilogy . [S4] The game was developed under the codename " Project BG&E ; " by 30 Ubisoft Pictures employees with production lasting more than three years . [S5] One of the main goals of the game is to create a meaningful story while giving players lots of freedom , though the game adopts a relatively linear structure . [S6] The game was received poorly when it was shown at E3 2002 , and it prompted the developers to change some of the game 's elements , including Jade 's design . [S7] Ancel also attempted to streamline the game in order to make the game more commercially appealing . [S8] Beyond Good & Evil was critically acclaimed . [S9] Critics praised the game 's animation , setting , story , and design , but criticized the game 's combat and technical issues . [S10] The game received a nomination for " Game of the Year " at the 2004 Game Developers Choice Awards . [S11] While the game had a cult following , it was considered a commercial failure at launch . [S12] A full HD re - mastered version of the game was released on Xbox Live Arcade in March 2011 and on PlayStation Network in June 2011 . [S13] A prequel , Beyond Good and Evil 2 , is in development and was announced at E3 2017 .

[S4] Bonatti 's astrological reputation was also criticised in Dante 's Divine Comedy , where he is depicted as residing in hell as punishment for his astrology . [S5] His most famous work was his Liber Astronomiae or ' Book of Astronomy ' , written around 1277 . [S6] This remained a classic astrology textbook for two centuries .

[S6] After redistricting , Finnegan 's district was merged with the neighboring 9th District of fellow Democrat Sidney Yates . [S8] Yates lost , and Chicago 's machine bosses persuaded Finnegan to stand down in 1964 and hand the 9th back to Yates . [S9] In return for his co - operation , Finnegan was appointed as a judge for the Circuit Court of Cook County . [S10] He resigned his seat in Congress on December 6 , 1964 and commenced his service on the bench the following day . [S11] He continued to serve until his death in 1971 .

Document: [S0] New Haven Harbor is an inlet on the north side of Long Island Sound in the state of Connecticut in the United States . [S1] The harbor area is an inlet carved by the retreat of the glaciers during the last ice age approximately 13,000 years ago . [S2] The city of New Haven and its neighborhoods of City Point , Long Wharf , The Annex , and East Shore lie on the northern and eastern sides . [S3] West Haven is on the west . [S4] The Quinnipiac and Mill rivers converge and empty into the inlet on its north end . [S5] The Pearl Harbor Memorial Bridge crosses here . [S6] The West River empties into the western end of the harbor ( also known as West Haven Harbor ) . [S7] The harbor is protected from Long Island Sound by a peninsula on its eastern side , once known as " Little Necke " but now called Lighthouse Point , because of the lighthouse that was constructed on its tip in 1805 . [S8] The original lighthouse was replaced in 1845 by the current structure , called the Five Mile Point Lighthouse . [S9] This lighthouse was replaced for navigation in 1877 by the offshore Southwest Ledge Light . [S10] Sperry Lighthouse ( 1899 – 1933 ) also served the harbor . [S11] In July 1779 , during the American Revolutionary War , the peninsula was the scene of an amphibious landing by British troops . [S12] The harbor is circumnavigable via the partially completed " Harborside Greenway " bicycle and pedestrian trail , which is part of the East Coast Greenway system .

Document: [S0] Antisemitic canards are unfounded rumors or false allegations which are defamatory towards Judaism as a religion , or defamatory towards Jews as an ethnic or religious group . [S1] They often form part of broader theories of Jewish conspiracies . [S2] According to defense attorney Kenneth Stern , " Historically , Jews have not fared well around conspiracy theories . [S3] Such ideas fuel anti - Semitism . [S4] The myths that all Jews are responsible for the death of Christ , or poisoned wells , or killed Christian children to bake matzos , or " made up " the Holocaust , or plot to control the world , do not succeed each other ; rather , the list of anti - Semitic canards gets longer . " [S5] Some antisemitic canards date back to the birth of Christianity , while some conspiracy theories are more recent . [S6] Since at least the Middle Ages , antisemitism has featured elements of conspiracy theory . [S7] In medieval Europe it was widely believed that Jews poisoned wells , had been responsible for the death of Jesus , and ritually consumed the blood of Christians . [S8] The second half of the 19th century saw the emergence of notions that Jews and/or Freemasons were plotting to establish control over the world . [S9] Forged evidence has been presented to spread the notion that Jews were responsible for the propagation of Communism , the most notorious example being The Protocols of the Elders of Zion ( 1903 ) . [S10] Such antisemitic conspiracy theories became central to the worldview of Adolf Hitler . [S11] Antisemitic theories persist today in notions concerning banking , Hollywood , the news media and a purported Zionist Occupation Government . [S12] Holocaust denial is also considered an antisemitic conspiracy theory because of its position that the Holocaust is a hoax designed to advance the interests of Jews and justify the creation of the State of Israel .

Document: [S0] Seth Gordon Persons ( February 5 , 1902 – May 29 , 1965 ) was an American Democratic politician who was the 43rd Governor of Alabama from 1951 to 1955 . [S1] He was born and died in Montgomery , Alabama . [S2] The Dauphin Island Bridge south of Mobile is formally named for him . [S3] Persons built a successful business running electrical lines in rural Alabama ( benefiting from Rural Electrification Administration contracts ) ; in addition to financial gain , he also won considerable popularity . [S4] When running for office in 1950 , Persons gained notoriety by touring the state in a helicopter ( prompting one opponent to dub him " the man from Mars " ) . [S5] He won the Democratic nomination by defeating a crowded field that included former governor Chauncey Sparks . [S6] In office , his notable accomplishments included abolishing flogging in Alabama 's prisons , advocating for the establishment of Alabama Public Television , and imposing speed limits on state highways . [S7] Persons largely accomplished his goal of having four years of " no fighting , " maintaining a truce among the various wings of the state Democratic Party . [S8] At the end of his term , Persons ordered the National Guard into Phenix City following the assassination of Attorney - General - elect Albert Patterson . [S9] After leaving office as governor , Persons never sought statewide public office again , although he did make an unsuccessful run for circuit judge late in life . [S10] Persons was an alumnus of Auburn University , though he attended for only one year . [S11] While at Auburn , Persons served as president of a student organization ( known as the " Boxcar Reds and Boxcar Blacks " ) that traveled to away football games .

Document: [S0] Between Five and Seven is as the name suggests , the sixth studio album by folk singer - songwriter John Gorka . [S1] It was released in August 1996 . [S2] It is the last of the five albums Gorka recorded for Windham Hill / High Street Records before returning to the smaller , Red House label . [S3] Gorka produced the album with John Jennings who also produced Gorka 's previous record , Out of the Valley . [S4] Unlike the previous record made in Nashville , Tennessee , the recording was done at Paisley Park Studios , Chanhassen , Minnesota and the instrumentation has been described as " more acoustic , less pop - oriented . " [S5] Paisley Park is southwest of Minneapolis and is the studio designed and owned by the artist , Prince . [S6] The album includes several lyrical portraits of Gorka 's misfit characters , love songs , and philosophical musings . [S7] The songs are also full of the wordplay for which Gorka has become known . [S8] The album features an impressive array of supporting musicians . [S9] Lucy Kaplansky and Jennifer Kimball add carefully placed harmony vocals to many tracks . [S10] John Jennings also brings along several other members of Mary Chapin Carpenter 's band including drummer Robbie Magruder , guitarist Dean Magraw , and pianist Jonathan Carroll . [S11] Gorka 's fellow Minnesotan Peter Ostroushko sits in on mandolin . [S12] As with many of Gorkas recordings Michael Manring plays fretless bass on nearly half of the songs . [S13] The tracks alternate between two different sets of instrumentalists which varies the pace of the music . [S14] The two bass players styles are distinct enough for the listener to recognize the difference .

Document: [S0] Vaanathaippola ( ) is a 2000 Indian Tamil - language drama film written and directed by Vikraman . [S1] The film features Vijayakanth in dual lead roles as well as Prabhu Deva , Meena , Livingston , Kausalya and Anju Aravind . [S2] Produced by Venu Ravichandran under Oscar Films , the film has a score and soundtrack composed by S. A. Rajkumar and cinematography handled by Arthur A. Wilson . [S3] The film tells the story of a caring brother who makes sacrifices to ensure his three younger brothers succeed in life . [S4] The film opened to positive reviews and box office success in January 2000 , and went on to win the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment the following year . [S5] Vaanathaipola subsequently went on to become the most commercially successful film in Tamil , running for over 250 days in theatres . [S6] Furthermore , the success of the film led to two Tamil Nadu State Film Awards , as well as several remakes in other Indian regional languages such as Telugu , Kannada and Bhojpuri . [S7] The film was remade in Telugu as Maa Annayya with Rajasekhar in the title role . [S8] The Kannada remake was titled Yajamana . [S9] The Bhojpuri remake was titled Pariwaar .

Document: [S0] Elizabeth II was Queen of Mauritius from 1968 to 1992 . [S1] Mauritius was a constitutional monarchy with Elizabeth as head of state . [S2] The Queen was also the monarch of the United Kingdom and the other Commonwealth realms . [S3] Her constitutional roles in Mauritius were delegated to a Governor - General . [S4] The Parliament of the United Kingdom 's Mauritius Independence Act 1968 transformed the British Crown Colony of Mauritius into an independent sovereign state . [S5] Unusually , no member of the British royal family attended the independence ceremony on the island because of security concerns . [S6] Princess Alexandra was due to attend but after communal violence the British Minister of State for the Commonwealth , Lord Shepherd , advised that her visit be cancelled . [S7] The Queen and her husband Prince Philip , Duke of Edinburgh , visited Mauritius for three days ( 24–26 March ) in 1972 , as part of a tour of Asia and Africa . [S8] They arrived in Port Louis on the royal yacht Britannia after visiting the Seychelles . [S9] They were met by a crowd of nearly a quarter of a million people , and rode through the city in an open - topped car . [S10] During the visit , the Queen opened the sixth session of the third Mauritius Parliament . [S11] The royal couple left Mauritius for Nairobi by air . [S12] It was the first ever visit to the island by a reigning monarch . [S13] Mauritius became a republic within the Commonwealth in 1992 with the President of Mauritius replacing the Queen as head of state . [S14] To date , Mauritius is the most recent of the Queen 's realms to become a republic .

Document: [S0] Durán , is a canton located in the province of Guayas , Ecuador , near the confluence of the Daule & Babahoyo rivers , where the Guayas River enters the ocean . [S1] Its township or capital is Eloy Alfaro . [S2] The canton was created in 1986 during the presidential period of Leon Febres Cordero through a presidential decree . [S3] The name " Eloy Alfaro " was chosen because of the Ecuadorian ex - president Eloy Alfaro Delgado . [S4] According to the National census in 2010 , there are 235,769 people residing within the canton limits . [S5] Many of its inhabitants commute to other places for work and it can be considered a " dormitory town " . [S6] However , many people who live in Durán find work within the canton by opening " comedores " or small restaurants , selling produce at the market , or even opening little stores with basic produce and house necessities . [S7] The towns Durán , Samborondón , and Guayaquil are connected by the bridge Rafael Mendoza Avilés . [S8] Durán is also well known for being the first railroad hub in Ecuador . [S9] Since July 2007 , a government program for the railroad reactivation began as well as the railroad connecting Duran with other cities located in the highlands of Ecuador .

Document: [S0] The National Integrated Ballistic Information Network or NIBIN is a specialized computer network in the United States . [S1] It contains digital images of recovered pieces of ballistic evidence . [S2] Running on the Integrated Ballistic Identification System or IBIS platform , NIBIN enables U.S. law enforcers to rapidly determine if a piece of recovered ballistic evidence came from a firearm that has been previously used in a crime . [S3] There are certain criteria that must be met prior to entering information into the NIBIN database . [S4] For instance , cartridge cases from a .22 caliber firearm or a revolver are normally not entered . [S5] Using NIBIN , law enforcement staff can identify firearms in new cases that were used in prior incidents . [S6] A series of seventeen different Washington state crime scenes involving seven firearms , and three different agencies in two counties , was identified using information provided by IBIS / NIBIN .

[S1] Godenzi was encouraged to join the Miss Hong Kong pageant by her modeling agency , which had groomed one of its models , Maggie Cheung , to compete the year before . [S2] Heavily favored , she won the title , in addition to the Miss Photogenic award . [S3] After her unsurprising victory , many expected her to do well in Miss Universe 1984 in Miami ( her father is Australian and her mother is ethnically Chinese ) . [S4] She was unplaced eventually , but did win third prize in the national costume competition . [S5] After her reign , Godenzi started a film career and was in several action films . [S6] She appeared in several films alongside kung fu film actor Sammo Hung before marrying him in 1995 . [S7] She was nominated for Best Supporting Actress at the 1988 Hong Kong Film Awards for her role in Eastern Condors . [S8] Godenzi has since retired from acting .

Document: [S0] Franz Wilhelm Seiwert ( March 9 , 1894 – July 3 , 1933 ) was a German painter and sculptor in a constructivist style . [S1] He was also politically active as a communist making significant contributions , both graphic and theoretical to Die Aktion . [S2] Seiwert was born in Cologne . [S3] He was seriously burned in 1901 , at the age of seven , in an experimental radiological treatment . [S4] As a result , he subsequently lived with the fear that his life would be short . [S5] He studied from 1910 to 1914 at the Cologne School of Arts and Crafts . [S6] In 1919 he met Max Ernst and took part in Dada activities . [S7] He was invited to exhibit in the large Dada exhibit in Cologne but withdrew at the last moment . [S8] In that same year he formed the Stupid group which included Heinrich Hoerle and Anton Räderscheidt . [S9] According to Ernst , " Stupid was a secession from Cologne Dada . [S10] As far as Hoerle and especially Seiwert were concerned , Dada 's activities were aesthetically too radical and socially not concrete enough " . [S11] His first large solo exhibition was in Cologne at the Kunstverein in 1923 , and by the mid-1920s he was a leader of the " Group of Progressive Artists " , who sought to reconcile constructivism with realism while expressing radical political views . [S12] In 1929 he founded the magazine " a - z " , a journal of progressive art . [S13] This became a vehicle for the exposition of Figurative Constructivism .

[S5] Bolivia 's state of instability , fraught with coups and international conflicts concerned him greatly .

Document: [S0] The Liverpool Neurological Infectious Diseases Course ( or NeuroID ) is an annual two - day course aimed at medical professionals and students with an interest in neurological infectious diseases . [S1] The course is organised by the Liverpool Brain Infections Group , a division of the Institute of Infection and Global Health at the University of Liverpool , in collaboration with the Walton Centre NHS Foundation Trust , Alder Hey Children ’s NHS Trust , Royal Liverpool University Hospital , and Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine , and is chaired by the neurologist Tom Solomon . [S2] It takes place during May at the historic Liverpool Medical Institution , in Liverpool , UK . [S3] A variety of both national and international speakers contribute to a programme which covers clinical aspects of common central nervous system infections such as meningitis and encephalitis , as well as rarer neurological infections and talks on recent advances in related research . [S4] The course is accredited by the UK Royal College of Physicians , and attracts delegates from many countries worldwide .

Document: [S0] The Battle of Chiari was fought on 1 September 1701 during the War of the Spanish Succession . [S1] The engagement was part of Prince Eugene of Savoy 's campaign to seize the Spanish controlled Duchy of Milan in the Italian peninsula , and had followed his victory over Marshal Catinat at the Battle of Carpi in July . [S2] Marshal Villeroi replaced Catinat as commander of the Franco – Spanish – Savoyard forces in the theatre , carrying with him orders from King Louis XIV to push the Imperialists out of Italy . [S3] Foreseeing Villeroi 's intention of attacking at any price , Eugene entrenched himself in front of the small fortress of Chiari , and waited for the attack . [S4] In a battle that lasted several hours the Austrians inflicted heavy casualties on Villeroi 's forces , gaining an overwhelming victory . [S5] The campaign established Eugene in Lombardy , and helped to persuade the Maritime Powers to come to the aid of the Emperor . [S6] Within a week of the battle England , the Dutch Republic , and Leopold I , had signed the second treaty of the Grand Alliance .

Document: [S0] Tomcats Screaming Outside is the first ( and to date only ) solo album from British musician Roland Orzabal of the group Tears for Fears , and was released on 2 April 2001 . [S1] Although Orzabal had effectively made two solo albums under the Tears for Fears moniker in the 1990s ( following the departure of bandmate Curt Smith ) , this was the first recording to be released under his own name . [S2] This album was Orzabal 's last to feature contributions from Alan Griffiths , who co - wrote most of the tracks on this album as well as the previous two Tears for Fears albums . [S3] The album was given a low - key release and did not chart , but earned some critical acclaim for its clever melding of pop songwriting and drum ' n bass , ambient techno and trip hop textures . [S4] Dan Gennoe claimed in Amazon.com 's editorial review : " Solo album or not , Tomcats Screaming Outside is the best Tears for Fears album in a decade . " [S5] In a 2000 interview Orzabal commented on his influences for the album : " I started out with an absolute concrete vision of where I wanted to go so I started with a very different rhythm approach , with drum and bass / jungle ... and I ended up with something that was n't the original plan . " [S6] The US release of the album ( on Gold Circle Records ) had the unfortunate coincidence to be released on September 11 , 2001 the same day the United States experienced its worst - ever terrorist attack , and drew little notice outside TFF 's core fan base .

Document: [S0] The Burseraceae are a moderate - sized family of 17 - 19 genera and about 540 species of flowering plants . [S1] The actual numbers differ according to the time period in which a given source is written describing this family . [S2] The Burseraceae are also known as the torchwood family , the frankincense and myrrh family , or simply the incense tree family . [S3] The family includes both trees and shrubs , and is native to tropical regions of Africa , Asia , and the Americas . [S4] Just as the family size ( in terms of genera and species ) differs according to the time period of the study , so , too , does its placement in the higher ranks . [S5] Nevertheless , the family is a genetically supported monophyletic group currently and frequently cited within the Sapindales and is recognized as a sister group to the Anacardiaceae . [S6] The Burseraceae are characterized by the nonallergenic resin they produce in virtually all plant tissue and the distinctive smooth , yet flaking , aromatic bark . [S7] The origins of the family can be traced to the Paleocene ( about 65 Mya ) when Beiselia mexicana first diverged in Mexico . [S8] The subsequent divergences in the family lineage and migration of the species in the Eocene ( 53 Mya ) from North America have led to the current distributions of the species that are primarily associated with the tropics . [S9] Though the family likely originated in North America , the greatest generic diversity presently is in the Southern Hemisphere . [S10] Tabonuco ( Dacryodes excelsa ) and gumbo limbo ( Bursera simaruba ) represent the economic , ethnobotanical , and ecological significance of the Burseraceae in the Western Hemisphere , while frankincense ( Boswellia sacra ) and myrrh ( Commiphora myrrha ) represent the same in the Eastern Hemisphere .

Document: [S0] The Pleistocene coyote ( Canis latrans orcutti ) , also known as the Ice Age coyote , is an extinct subspecies of coyote that lived in western North America during the Late Pleistocene era . [S1] Most remains of the subspecies were found in southern California , though at least one was discovered in Idaho . [S2] It was part of a carnivore guild that included other canids like foxes , gray wolves , and dire wolves . [S3] Compared to their modern Holocene counterparts , Pleistocene coyotes were larger and more robust , weighing , likely in response to larger competitors and prey rather than Bergmann 's rule . [S4] Their skulls and jaws were significantly thicker and deeper than in modern coyotes , with a shorter and broader rostrum and wider carnassial ( denoting the large upper premolar and lower molar teeth of a carnivore , adapted for shearing flesh ) teeth . [S5] These adaptions allowed it to cope with higher levels of stress , when it killed larger prey , compared to modern coyotes . [S6] Pleistocene coyotes were also likely more specialized carnivores than their descendants , as their teeth were more adapted to shearing meat , showing fewer grinding surfaces which were better suited for processing vegetation . [S7] The lower jaw was also deeper , and the molars showed more signs of wear and breakage than modern populations , thus indicating that the animals consumed more bone than today . [S8] Behaviorally , it is likely to have been more social than the modern coyote , as its remains are the third most common in the La Brea Tar Pits , after dire wolves and sabre - toothed cats , both thought to be gregarious species . [S9] Their reduction in size occurred within 1,000 years of the occurrence of the Quaternary extinction event , when the climate changed and the majority of their larger prey became extinct . [S10] Furthermore , Pleistocene coyotes were unable to successfully exploit the big game hunting niche left vacant after the extinction of the dire wolf , as that gap was rapidly filled by gray wolves . [S11] These gray wolves are likely to have actively killed off the larger - bodied coyotes , with natural selection favoring the modern gracile morph . [S12] Human predation on the Pleistocene coyote 's dwindling prey base may have also impacted the animal 's change in morphology .

[S5] An important feature of the site is the geology of the area . [S6] Originally a dome was created millions of years ago through tectonic uplifts . Document: [S0] George Washington 's resignation as commander - in - chief marked the end of Washington 's military service in the American Revolutionary War and his return to civilian life at Mount Vernon . [S1] His voluntary action has been described as " one of the nation 's great acts of statesmanship " and helped establish the precedent of civilian control of the military . [S2] After the Treaty of Paris ending the war had been signed on September 3 , 1783 , and after the last British troops left New York City on November 25 , Washington resigned his commission as commander - in - chief of the Continental Army to the Congress of the Confederation , then meeting in the Maryland State House at Annapolis , Maryland , on December 23 of the same year . [S3] This followed his farewell to the Continental Army , November 2 at Rockingham near Princeton , New Jersey , and his farewell to his officers , December 4 at Fraunces Tavern in New York City .

Document: [S0] Eivind Bolle ( 13 October 1923 – 10 June 2012 ) was a Norwegian politician for the Labour Party . [S1] He was born in Hol . [S2] He was elected to the Norwegian Parliament from Nordland in 1973 , and was re - elected on two occasions . [S3] He had previously served as a deputy representative during the term 1969 – 1973 . [S4] He was the Minister of Fisheries from 1973 to 1981 during three different cabinets : second cabinet Bratteli , cabinet Nordli and first cabinet Brundtland . [S5] During these three periods he was replaced in the Parliament by Eindride Sommerseth , Karl Ingebrigtsen and Finn Knutsen respectively . [S6] On the local level he was a member of Hol municipality council from 1959 to 1963 , and later in Hol 's successor municipality Vestvågøy . [S7] He served as mayor from 1971 to 1973 , during which term he was also a member of Nordland county council . [S8] Outside politics he worked as a fisher from 1938 to 1974 .

[S1] He was born in Rebola , Spanish Guinea and studied at the Escuela Superior de Santa Isabel and at La Escuela social de Granada . [S2] He was minister under Teodoro Obiang until he dissented with the dictatorship 's policies and went into exile in Valencia , Spain . [S3] Prior to his position in the Guinean government , he would live for over 15 years in Majorca ( where his daughter María Concepción , a flamenco singer best known as Concha Buika , was born ) . [S4] After his exile , he settled down in Valencia with his second wife and her family . [S5] Balboa Boneke died from renal problems , coupled with a three - year depression caused by the death of his wife , on 10 March 2014 in Valencia , Spain .

Document: [S0] " Direction of Endeavor for Chinese Christianity in the Construction of New China " , commonly known as " The Christian Manifesto " or " The Three - Self Manifesto " , was a political manifesto of Protestants in China whereby they backed the newly - founded People 's Republic of China ( PRC ) and the leadership of the Communist Party of China ( CPC ) . [S1] Published in 1950 , the manifesto paved the way for the government - controlled Three - Self Patriotic Movement ( TSPM ) of Protestants . [S2] This movement proclaimed the three principles of self - government , self - support , and self - propagation . [S3] The drafting and content of the manifesto was , and remains , controversial to this day . [S4] The manifesto was devised after Protestant leaders presented their concerns with religious freedom to Zhou Enlai , the Premier of China . [S5] Instead of receiving their report , Zhou demanded them to come up with a statement in support of the new communist leadership . [S6] Y. T. Wu and other leftist clergymen espoused the task and presented a draft manifesto that , after some opposition and changes , became a foundational text of Christianity in the new People 's Republic . [S7] It condemns missionary activities in China as a form of imperialism , pledges loyalty to the communist leadership , and encourages the Church to take up an indigenous Chinese stance toward Christianity . [S8] Published on the front page of the People 's Daily , the manifesto was accompanied by a campaign to gather signatures . [S9] Many Christian leaders and laymen signed , while others refused to do so . [S10] After the Korean War broke out , the campaign became an increasingly politicized test of loyalty that became merged with the Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries . [S11] Some view the manifesto as a betrayal of the Church , while others find sympathy for the position of Chinese Christians struggling to reconcile their faith with the changed political realities . [S12] The manifesto ended missionary activities in China and the separation of church and state . [S13] It led to the founding the TSPM and brought persecution to dissidents .

Document: [S0] Lake Hiawatha is located just north of Lake Nokomis in Minneapolis , Minnesota . [S1] It was purchased by the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board in 1922 for $ 550,000 . [S2] At that time the lake was a marsh known as Rice Lake , but over four years , the park system transformed the wetland into a lake surrounded by a park . [S3] The lake and park have a fishing dock , wading pool , tennis courts , and softball diamonds . [S4] There is a recreation center that hosts activities . [S5] The lake borders a municipal golf course . [S6] In the winter the park sets up ice and hockey rinks . [S7] There is a bike and walking path starting at Lake Hiawatha which veers onto Lake Nokomis or winds down the Minnehaha Creek right to the mouth of the Minnehaha Falls . [S8] Lake Hiawatha is one of the few lakes through which Minnehaha Creek flows , and the last one before it reaches Minnehaha Falls and then the Mississippi River . [S9] Friends of Lake Hiawatha is a community environmental action group that organizes volunteer efforts to clean the lake and park .

Document: [S0] The Scribe is a 1966 comedy film short starring Buster Keaton in his last film role before his death from lung cancer on February 1 , 1966 . [S1] It was produced by the Construction Safety Association of Ontario , Canada to promote Construction site safety , and was filmed where the Ontario Government Buildings were under construction in Toronto . [S2] The director was John Sebert . [S3] Keaton portrays the janitor at a newspaper who accidentally intercepts a call from the editor , ordering him to do a story about safety practices at a massive construction site . [S4] He sneaks onto the construction site and finds a list of 16 safety rules posted on a wall . [S5] He takes the list and attempts to confront workers when he sees them acting in an unsafe manner , often causing more accidents than he prevents . [S6] Keaton is silent throughout the film as he recreates several routines from his youth . [S7] Most notable was his recreation of a gag from his 1918 film The Bell Boy in which he mops the floor using only the tip of the mop , little by little while sitting on the floor .

Document: [S0] The Ninety - Two Resolutions were drafted by Louis - Joseph Papineau and other members of the Parti patriote of Lower Canada in 1834 . [S1] The resolutions were a long series of demands for political reforms in the British - governed colony . [S2] Papineau had been elected speaker of the legislative assembly of Lower Canada in 1815 . [S3] His party constantly opposed the unelected colonial government , and in 1828 he helped draft an early form of the resolutions , essentially a list of grievances against the colonial administration . [S4] To ensure that the views of the Legislative Assembly be understood by the British House of Commons , the Parti patriote had sent its own delegation to London in order to submit a memoir and a petition signed by 87,000 people . [S5] On February 28 , 1834 , Papineau presented the Ninety - Two Resolutions to the Legislative Assembly which were approved and sent to London . [S6] The resolutions included , among other things , demands for an elected Legislative Council and an Executive Council responsible before the house of representatives . [S7] Under the Constitutional Act of 1791 , the government of Lower Canada was given an elected legislative assembly , but members of the upper houses were appointed by the Governor of the colony . [S8] In the resolutions , the elected representatives once again reiterated their loyalty to the British Crown , but expressed frustration that the government of London had been unwilling to correct the injustices caused by the past governments of the colony . [S9] Papineau 's resolutions were ignored for almost three years ; meanwhile , the Legislative Assembly did all it could to oppose the un - elected upper houses while avoiding outright rebellion . [S10] British Colonial Secretary Lord Russell eventually responded to them by issuing ten resolutions of his own ( the Russell Resolutions ) . [S11] All of the Legislative Assembly 's demands were rejected . [S12] The ten resolutions reached Canada in 1837 , and many of Papineau 's reformists began to agitate for a rebellion . [S13] See the Lower Canada Rebellion .

Document: [S0] Cimatti was an Italian manufacturer of bicycles , motorcycles and mopeds active between 1937 and 1984 . [S1] In 1937 , the Olympic cyclist Marco Cimatti founded a small company in Bologna that originally produced bicycles . [S2] In 1950 , he changed to mopeds , and in the 1960s , started producing motorcycles , including the and Sport Luxury road and Kaiman Cross racing models with four - speed gearboxes . [S3] In 1972 – 77 , he introduced two models , one for motocross with a five - speed gearbox and the other for road . [S4] In those years Cimatti 's son Enrico expanded the business to export motorcycles to the United States , France , Norway and Tunisia . [S5] In the 1970s through early 1980s , Cimatti produced several moped lines including the City - Bike and the larger Town - Bike . [S6] Cimatti used two - stroke engines bought from both Moto Morini and Moto Minarelli . [S7] A recession in the early 1980s forced the company to close in 1984 .

[S1] Designed by McKim , Mead and White , it was built in 1900 for the Boston Symphony Orchestra , which continues to make the hall its home . [S2] The hall was designated a U.S. National Historic Landmark in 1999 and is a pending Boston Landmark . Document: [S0] The Hub is an American " computer network music " ensemble formed in 1986 consisting of John Bischoff , Tim Perkis , Chris Brown , Scot Gresham - Lancaster , Mark Trayle and Phil Stone . [S1] " The Hub was the first live computer music band whose members were all composers , as well as designers and builders of their own hardware and software . " [S2] The Hub grew from the League of Automatic Music Composers : John Bischoff , Tim Perkis , Jim Horton , and Rich Gold . [S3] Perkis and Bischoff modified their equipment for a performance at The Network Muse Festival in 1986 at The LAB in San Francisco . [S4] Instead of creating an ad - hoc wired connection of computer interaction , they decided to use a hub - a general purpose connection for network data . [S5] This was less failure - prone and enabled greater collaborations . [S6] The Hub was the first band to do a telematic performance in 1987 at the Clocktower in New York . [S7] Since this work represents some of the earliest work in the context of the new live music practice of Networked music performance , they have been cited as the archetypal network ensemble in computer music . [S8] The Hub 's best - known piece , Stuck Note by Scot Gresham - Lancaster has been covered by a number of network music bands , including MiLO- the Milwaukee Laptop Orchestra [S9] and BiLE- the Birmingham Laptop Ensemble . [S10] They have collaborated with Rova Saxophone Quartet , Nick Collins , Phill Niblock , and Alvin Curran . [S11] They currently perform around the world after a multi - year hiatus , ending in 2004 .

[S2] The initiator of the museum was the architect Hjalmar Welhaven . [S3] His private collection formed the foundation of the antique and historic skis on display at the museum . [S4] Until 1951 , the collection was housed in a building in the Oslo neighborhood of Frognerseteren . [S5] In connection with the rebuilding of Holmenkollbakken in 1951 , the museum collection was moved to new premises at Holmenkollbakken . [S8] Additionally it displays equipment used in the polar expeditions of both Fridtjof Nansen and Roald Amundsen . [S9] The Ski Museum is owned and operated by Skiforeningen . [S10] This association is responsible for the organization of sports , activities and events in Holmenkollen National Park .

[S4] The Philippine Organic Act was passed by the United States Congress in 1902 ; this enshrined into law the Commission 's legislative and executive authority . [S5] As stipulated in the Philippine Organic Act , the bicameral Philippine Legislature was established in 1907 , with the Commission as the upper house and the elected Philippine Assembly acting as lower house . [S6] The Jones Act of 1916 ended the Commission , replacing it with an elected Philippine Senate as the Legislature 's upper house .

Document: [S0] The policy of Russification of Finland ( Finnish : sortokaudet / sortovuodet - times / years of oppression ) was a governmental policy of the Russian Empire aimed at limiting the special status of the Grand Duchy of Finland and possibly the termination of its political autonomy and cultural uniqueness in 1899 – 1905 and in 1908 – 1917 . [S1] It was a part of a larger policy of Russification pursued by late 19th – early 20th century Russian governments which tried to abolish cultural and administrative autonomy of non - Russian minorities within the empire . [S2] The two Russification campaigns evoked widespread Finnish resistance , starting with petitions and escalating to strikes , passive resistance ( including draft resistance ) and eventually active resistance . [S3] Finnish opposition to Russification was one of the main factors that ultimately led to Finland 's declaration of independence in 1917 .

Document: [S0] Thirteens is an album by Leona Naess , released in the U.S. on 16 September 2008 by Verve Forecast Records , and released in the UK on 11 May 2009 by Polydor Records . [S1] The album was influenced by the death of Naess ’s father , Arne Næss , Jr. , in a mountaineering accident in January 2004 . [S2] Naess returned to London from New York City and eventually began writing and recording songs with music producer Samuel Dixon . [S3] Naess recorded with almost no budget , asking friends to contribute , and completed thirteen albums’ worth of material . [S4] Eleven songs were selected for the release , titled Thirteens . [S5] Described as " a sweet and poignant collection " by New York magazine , much of the album deals with the onset of maturity . [S6] The album consists of first takes , which were then overdubbed . [S7] A digital download of the album available on the iTunes Store includes a bonus track featuring singer - songwriter Ryan Adams ; an exclusive edition available through retailer Barnes & Noble includes two bonus tracks . [S8] The UK release includes two bonus tracks unavailable on previous releases of the album .

Document: [S0] The northern bald ibis , hermit ibis , or waldrapp ( Geronticus eremita ) is a migratory bird found in barren , semi - desert or rocky habitats , often close to running water . [S1] This glossy black ibis , which , unlike many members of the ibis family , is non - wading , has an unfeathered red face and head , and a long , curved red bill . [S2] It breeds colonially on coastal or mountain cliff ledges , where it typically lays two to three eggs in a stick nest , and feeds on lizards , insects , and other small animals . [S3] The northern bald ibis was once widespread across the Middle East , northern Africa , southern and central Europe , with a fossil record dating back at least 1.8   million years . [S4] It disappeared from Europe over 300 years ago , and is now considered critically endangered . [S5] There are believed to be about 500 wild birds remaining in southern Morocco , and fewer than 10 in Syria , where it was rediscovered in 2002 . [S6] To combat this ebb in numbers , recent reintroduction programs have been instituted internationally , with a semi - wild breeding colony in Turkey , as well as sites in Austria , Spain , and northern Morocco . [S7] The reasons for the species ' long - term decline are unclear , but hunting , loss of foraging habitat , and pesticide poisoning have been implicated in the rapid loss of colonies in recent decades .

Document: [S0] The O. W. Coburn School of Law was the law school of Oral Roberts University . [S1] The school was named after donor Orin Wesley Coburn , the founder of Coburn Optical Industries and the father of future US politician Tom Coburn . [S2] The school opened in 1979 . [S3] Its founding dean was Charles Kothe , a Tulsa , Oklahoma labor attorney . [S4] Other professors included Anita Hill , John Eidsmoe , Gary Lane , Herb Titus , and Rutherford Institute founder John W. Whitehead . [S5] In 1986 , the school closed , with its 190,000 volume law library , as well as 5 professors and 23 students , moving to CBN University ( now Regent University ) . [S6] Since the new CBN law school would not initially be accredited ( and in fact did not receive provisional accreditation until 1989 ) , students graduating in spring 1987 were allowed to state they graduated from Coburn , in order to be listed as graduating from an accredited school . [S7] U.S. Representative Michele Bachmann began attending Coburn the first year it opened , and graduated as part of its last class .

[S1] McLamore attended Northfield Mount Hermon School before matriculating at Cornell University . [S2] McLamore was an employee and also a businessman before . [S3] Edgerton originally opened Insta Burger King in Miami , Florida on March 1 , 1954 . [S4] Three months later , on June 1 , he met McLamore and they formed the Burger King Corporation . [S5] The corporation opened Burger King stores and went on to introduce the Whopper burger in 1957 , when it also dropped " Insta " from the name . [S6] The pair sold the business to Pillsbury in 1967 and McLamore served as Burger King 's president until 1970 , and was chairman to 1976 . [S7] McLamore died of cancer in Coral Gables , Florida on August 9 , 1996 , at the age of 70 .

Document: [S0] Emiliano Esono Michá is an Equatoguinean political activist currently imprisoned on weapons possession charges . [S1] His imprisonment drew protest from the US State Department and Amnesty International , the latter of which named him a prisoner of conscience . [S2] Michá was active with the Progress Party of Equatorial Guinea ( PPGE ) , a banned political party opposing the long - dominant Democratic Party of Equatorial Guinea . [S3] In late March 2008 , he was arrested without a warrant . [S4] Within a week , fellow PPGE activists Cruz Obiang Ebele , Gumersindo Ramírez Faustino , Juan Ecomo Ndong , Gerardo Angüe Mangue , and Bonifacio Nguema Ndong were also arrested . [S5] Michá was held for two months at the police station , turning which time he was allegedly tortured . [S6] In May 2008 , the six men were charged with knowledge of a weapons cache in the home of another PPGE activist , Saturnino Ncogo . [S7] Ncogo had died in prison on early March in suspicious circumstances . [S8] Authorities alleged he had thrown himself from the top bunk of his cell to commit suicide , but relatives received his body in an advanced state of decomposition , and no investigation was ever conducted . According to Amnesty International , the six men were given an unfair trial at which no evidence was presented save the weapons from Ncogo 's home and the statements the six had made under duress ; in addition , the six defendants alleged that police had altered their statements after the defendants had signed them . [S9] Despite being charged with unrelated crimes , the six were tried alongside Simon Mann , a UK national who had helped to organize a 2004 coup attempt . [S10] The six PPGE members were given sentences of one to five years apiece . [S11] The US State Department considers Michá a political prisoner , and has objected to his continued imprisonment . [S12] Amnesty International named him a prisoner of conscience , and has called for his immediate release .

Document: [S0] Elwood C. Buchanan , Sr was an American jazz trumpeter and teacher who became an early mentor of Miles Davis . [S1] Buchanan was born in St Louis , Missouri on January 26 , 1907 , and was trained in music by Joseph Gustat , the principal trumpeter with the St Louis Symphony Orchestra . [S2] He began his career playing in local dance bands , including Andy Kirk 's orchestra , and on the riverboats that travelled on the Mississippi River between St Louis and New Orleans . [S3] During the late 1930s and early 1940s , he taught music and directed the band at Lincoln High School in East St Louis , and also visited the local elementary schools to give weekly lessons . [S4] Buchanan was known for his strict and demanding teaching style , and for encouraging pupils to compete with one another . [S5] Buchanan was a patient of Miles Davis 's father , who told him of his son 's interest in music . [S6] Although Davis , at thirteen , was then too young to attend Buchanan 's school , Buchanan began giving him private lessons . [S7] Davis joined the school band when he began attending Lincoln . [S8] Although Buchanan had the band play mainly marches rather than jazz , the techniques he taught profoundly affected Davis ' jazz style . [S9] In particular , Buchanan went against the times by recommending to his students that they play without vibrato , and is said to have broken Davis of the habit by rapping his knuckles with a ruler and commanding : " Stop shakin ' that note . [S10] You 're going to shake enough when you get old " . [S11] Buchanan also encouraged Davis to study the lean , relaxed playing of Bobby Hackett ( then little known beyond the East Coast ) and Harold Shorty Baker . [S12] In this , too , Buchanan went against fashion ; the most popular trumpeter of the day was Louis Armstrong , whose hot playing style was very different from those of Hackett or Baker . [S13] Davis later credited Buchanan with persuading his parents to buy him a new trumpet , rather than a violin as his mother had preferred . [S14] Buchanan also introduced Davis to Clark Terry , who would become his recording partner . [S15] In his autobiography , Davis recalled : " Mr. Buchanan was the biggest influence on my life up until then . [S16] He was definitely the person who took me all the way into music at that time . "

Document: [S0] Frederick August Wenderoth or F. A. Wenderoth ( 1819 – 1884 ) was a German - born American painter and photographer . [S1] Born and educated in Cassel , where he first learned to paint from his father , he established a lifelong friendship with Charles Christian Nahl at school . [S2] During a period of political upheaval he left Germany for Paris where his was joined by Nahl and his half - brother Hugo Wilhelm Arthur Nahl . They then moved to the US , living first in New York , before traveling by sea to California to join the Gold Rush . [S3] Unsuccessful as miners , Wenderoth and Nahl opened art studios , first in Sacramento and later in San Francisco , collaborating as painters , engravers and photographers . [S4] After a trip to South Seas and Australia , Wenderoth married and moved to Philadelphia , where he established a photography studio . [S5] In the late 1850s he worked for a period in South Carolina , going into partnership with Jesse Bolles . [S6] There , and later when he returned to Philadelphia , he innovated a number of photographic techniques , such as the ivory - type and photozincography . [S7] Wenderoth died in 1884 of tuberculosis .

Document: [S0] Consort Mei ( died 755 ) was an imperial consort of the Chinese dynasty Tang Dynasty during the reign of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang . [S1] She was one of Emperor Xuanzong 's favorite concubine , often known as Mei fei ( with fei being a standard rank for imperial consorts during her lifetime ) . [S2] Her actual name was Jiang Caipin ( 江采蘋 ) , originally called Consort Jiang . [S3] After being told by her that she greatly favored Plum - Blossom flowers ( the flower is pronounced as mei in Chinese ) , Emperor Xuanzong began to fondly address her as Consort Mei . [S4] Consort Mei was initially selected by Gao Lishi , an eunuch official of Emperor Xuanzong , to become one of Emperor Xuanzong 's concubines in his harem . [S5] As Consort Mei was the most literate and talented concubines , she soon obtained Xuanzong 's favors . [S6] To express the favors towards Consort Mei , Xuanzong commanded servants to plant Plum - Blossom trees all around her palace to please her interest . [S7] Xuanzong even lovingly complimented her beauty as more adorable than Zhao Feiyan , and swore that he would never change his heart for her . [S8] However , in 737 , after the death of Consort Wu , another favorite concubine of Xuanzong , Xuanzong was deeply depressed until Gao Lishi convinced him to try looking at Yang Yuhuan - the wife of prince Li Mao , Xuanzong son with Consort Wu since her beauty was described as the most " irresistible " . [S9] Being curious , Xuanzong ordered Yang Yuhuan to come and subsequently fell in love with her beauty . [S10] Since Yuhuan was still literally his daughter - in - law ( as she was Li Mao 's wife ) , emperor Xuanzong then stealthily arranged Yuhuan to become a Taoist nun , after a brief moment , Xuanzong eventually offered Yuhuan honorable title as Yang Guifei ( with Guifei being the highest rank for imperial consorts ) after bestowing his son Li Mao a new wife . [S11] Yuhuan became Xuanzong 's most beloved consort as Xuanzong soon forgot about Consort Wu 's death . [S12] His favors towards Consort Mei also waned . [S13] In 755 , An Lushan began to create a rebellion ( known as An Lushan Rebellion ) in the palace . [S14] Emperor Xuanzong decided to bring Yang Guifei and his cortege along to flee from the capital Chang'an to Chengdu . [S15] Consort Mei was left behind then murdered during the rebellion .

Document: [S0] This is a list of United States ambassadors appointed by the 45th President of the United States , Donald Trump . [S1] Ambassadorships are often used as a form of political patronage to reward high - profile or important supporters of the President . [S2] The most visible ambassadorships are often distributed either in this way or to the President 's ideological or partisan confreres . [S3] Most ambassadorships , however , are assigned to Foreign Service Officers who have spent their career in the State Department . [S4] Regardless , all ambassadors must be formally appointed by the president and confirmed by the Senate . [S5] While all ambassadors serve at the president 's pleasure and may be dismissed at any time , career diplomats usually serve tours of roughly three years before receiving a new assignment , and political appointees customarily tender their resignations upon the inauguration of a new president .

[S1] He directed and produced films about the musics of Mozambique , Zimbabwe , Cape Verde , Lesotho , South Africa , and Brittany . [S2] He was the grandson of noted Philadelphia architect Clarence C. Zantzinger . [S3] He graduated from Westminster School in Connecticut and earned bachelor 's and master 's degrees in folklore and anthropology from the University of Pennsylvania . [S4] Zantzinger began making films in southern Africa in 1966 , while a Ph.D. candidate in the folklore / folklife program at the University of Pennsylvania . [S5] He studied film with Sol Worth at the University of Pennsylvania 's Annenberg School of Communications . [S6] Zantzinger also worked as a record producer . [S7] He lived in Devault , Chester County , Pennsylvania , where his production company , Constant Spring Productions , was based . [S8] He died of leukemia on February 16 , 2007 , at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania .

Document: [S0] Tyche (; from , Túkhē , meaning " luck " ; Roman equivalent : Fortuna ) was the presiding tutelary deity who governed the fortune and prosperity of a city , its destiny . [S1] In Classical Greek mythology , she is the daughter of Aphrodite and Zeus or Hermes . [S2] In literature , she might be given various genealogies , as a daughter of Hermes and Aphrodite , or considered as one of the Oceanids , daughters of Oceanus , and Tethys , or of Zeus . [S3] She was connected with Nemesis and Agathos Daimon ( " good spirit " ) . [S4] The Greek historian Polybius believed that when no cause can be discovered to events such as floods , droughts , frosts , or even in politics , then the cause of these events may be fairly attributed to Tyche .

[S1] The complex comprises the Ryan Brathwaite track , the Obadele Thompson stand and the Kirani James stand , all prominent Caribbean athletes . Document: [S0] Edmund Burke (; 12 January [ NS ] 17309 July 1797 ) was an Irish statesman born in Dublin , as well as an author , orator , political theorist and philosopher , who after moving to London in 1750 served as a member of parliament ( MP ) between 1766 and 1794 in the House of Commons with the Whig Party . [S1] Burke was a proponent of underpinning virtues with manners in society and of the importance of religious institutions for the moral stability and good of the state . [S2] These views were expressed in his A Vindication of Natural Society . [S3] Burke criticized British treatment of the American colonies , including through its taxation policies . [S4] He also supported the rights of the colonists to resist metropolitan authority , though he opposed the attempt to achieve independence . [S5] Burke is remembered for his support for Catholic emancipation , the impeachment of Warren Hastings from the East India Company and for his staunch opposition to the French Revolution . [S6] In his Reflections on the Revolution in France , Burke asserted that the revolution was destroying the fabric of good society , traditional institutions of state and society and condemned the persecution of the Catholic Church that resulted from it . [S7] This led to his becoming the leading figure within the conservative faction of the Whig Party , which he dubbed the " Old Whigs " , as opposed to the pro - French Revolution " New Whigs " , led by Charles James Fox . [S8] In the nineteenth century , Burke was praised by both conservatives and liberals . [S9] Subsequently , in the twentieth century he became widely regarded as the philosophical founder of modern conservatism .

Document: [S0] TMF ( The Music Factory ) was a music video and entertainment channel in the United Kingdom and Ireland . [S1] The channel was owned by Viacom International Media Networks and was originally a Dutch channel . [S2] Formed after the two other TMF stations , which are based in mainland Europe , the channel was created to counter against EMAP 's The Hits channel ( now 4Music ) on the new free - to - air digital terrestrial television service Freeview in 2002 . [S3] Upon launch , TMF 's description was " TMF is designed to replicate the rhythms of the whole family , playing the best pop videos with the biggest pop stars to become the sound track to the British family life . " [S4] However , it had since broadened its content to show programmes from its sister channels MTV , VH1 , Nick Jr. and Comedy Central , so no longer relied on just music videos . [S5] TMF broadcast on Freeview , Sky and Virgin Media and as well as in some Irish cable packages . [S6] The channel was the most viewed music video related station in the UK , according to BARB ratings . [S7] TMF had a new look on screen graphics in March 2008 to match the other British MTV channels . [S8] The previous on screen graphics were used since July 2005 and the original on screen graphics were used since October 2002 . [S9] The original DOG was on the top right of the screen , it has been moved to the top left of the screen since July 2005 . [S10] The new look TMF still used the old pre-2007 TMF logo whereas both the Dutch and Belgian TMF channels adapted the new logo . [S11] The DOG on music programmes was TMF : Music .

Document: [S0] Charles Paul Florimond Quef ( 1 November 1873 , Lille – 2 July 1931 , Paris ) was a French organist and composer . [S1] He studied at the conservatory in Lille , and later he attended the Paris Conservatory where he studied with Charles - Marie Widor , Louis Vierne and Alexandre Guilmant . [S2] From 1895 to 1898 , he was organist of the Église Sainte - Marie - des - Batignolles and in 1898 , organist of the Saint - Laurent church , Paris . [S3] In the same year , he was awarded the First prize for organ at the conservatory . [S4] Then he was appointed assistant organist and later , in November 1901 , titular organist of the Église de la Ste .- Trinité , Paris , due to resignation of his predecessor Guilmant . [S5] He retained this post until his death in 1931 .

[S2] He was also a contributor to the Iaşi periodical Zimbrul , in which he published one of his best - known works , Studie Moldovană ( " Moldovan Studies " ) , in 1851 - 1852 . [S3] He also wrote Iaşii şi locuitorii lui în 1840 " Iaşi and its inhabitants in 1840 " – a glimpse into Moldavian society during the Organic Statute administration , and two travel accounts ( better described as folklore studies ) , Piatra Teiului and Stânca Corbului . [S4] Russo is also notable for his Amintiri ( " Recollections " ) , a memoir .

Document: [S0] " Cry for Help " is the title of the first single taken from British dance - pop singer Rick Astley 's third studio album , Free . [S1] It was written by Rick Astley and Rob Fisher . [S2] The Andraé Crouch Choir provided backing vocals . [S3] Released as a single in January 1991 , " Cry for Help " reached number seven on both the UK Singles Chart and the US Billboard Hot 100 . [S4] It also reached number four in Canada and was a number - one hit on both the US and Canadian Adult Contemporary charts . [S5] The song 's number - seven UK chart placing meant that Astley became the first male solo artist to have his first eight singles reach the British top 10 . [S6] The song is a soul ballad , unlike Astley 's other more dance - oriented hit singles such as " Never Gon na Give You Up " . [S7] It was co - written by British singer Rob Fisher , formerly one half of the 1980s pop outfits Naked Eyes and Climie Fisher . [S8] To date , the song was Astley 's last appearance in the top 10 in either the US or UK . [S9] The song has been sung by Rick Astley in duet with Soren Sko and covered by Thomas Anders ( ex - Modern Talking ) .

Document: [S0] Marcial Maciel Degollado ( March 10 , 1920 – January 30 , 2008 ) was a Mexican Catholic priest who founded the Legion of Christ and the Regnum Christi movement , serving as general director of the legion from 1941 to 2005 . [S1] Throughout most of his career , he was respected within the church as " the greatest fundraiser of the modern Roman Catholic church " and as a prolific recruiter of new seminarians . [S2] Late in his life , Maciel was revealed to have sexually abused boys and young men . [S3] After his death , it came to light that he had also maintained relationships with at least two women , one of whom was a minor . [S4] He fathered as many as six children , and allegedly abused two of these children as well . [S5] In 2006 Pope Benedict XVI removed Maciel from active ministry based on the results of an investigation that he had started while head of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith , before his election as Pope in April 2005 . [S6] Maciel was ordered " to conduct a reserved life of prayer and penance , renouncing every public ministry " , and died in 2008 . [S7] On March 25 , 2010 , a communiqué on the legion 's website acknowledged as factual the " reprehensible actions " by Maciel , including sexual abuse of minor seminarians . [S8] In May 2010 the Vatican denounced Maciel 's actions and appointed a Papal Delegate to oversee the order and its governance .

Document: [S0] Jan Betley ( 1908 - 1980 ) was a Polish painter . [S1] Betley was born in Płock . [S2] Before the World War II , he was a student of two well known Polish painters , Tadeusz Pruszkowski and Felicjan Kowarski , at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw ( ASP ) . [S3] In 1936 , he graduated under the advisory of Pruszkowski and qualified himself as the assistant - professor in 1948 . [S4] Most of his early paintings were lost during the war time . [S5] After the war he taught at the ASP . [S6] He was a member of the Fourth Group advocating traditional subjects and perfectionism of technique . [S7] He is known for his portraits , landscapes , paintings of horses , battle scenes and genre pieces . [S8] He was closely related to Polish Colourism . [S9] His works can be found in Polish museums and in private collections in Poland and England . [S10] Betley died in Warsaw at age 72 .

Document: [S0] Lombardia ( Lombardy ) wine is the Italian wine produced in the Lombardy region of north central Italy . [S1] The region is known particularly for its sparkling wines made in the Franciacorta and Oltrepò Pavese areas . [S2] Lombardy also produces still red , white and rosé wines made from a variety of local and international grapes including Nebbiolo wines in the Valtellina region , Trebbiano di Lugana white wines produced with the Chiaretto style rosé along the shores of Lake Garda . [S3] The wine region currently has 15 Denominazione di origine controllata ( DOC ) , 3 Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita ( DOCG ) and 13 Indicazione Geografica Tipica ( IGT ) designations . [S4] The main cities of the region are Milan , Bergamo and Brescia . [S5] The region annually produces around 1.3 million hectolitres of wine , more than the regions of Friuli - Venezia Giulia , Marche , Trentino - Alto Adige / Südtirol and Umbria .

Document: [S0] Fatih Terim , Commendatore OSSI , T.C , ( born 4 September 1953 ) is a Turkish association football manager and former player . [S1] He is currently the manager of Galatasaray , a position he previously held three times . [S2] Terim has managed several clubs in Italy and Turkey , as well as the Turkish national football team , most recently from 2013 to 2017 . [S3] In a survey conducted by the International Federation of Football History & Statistics ( IFFHS ) in 80 countries , he was placed among the best eight managers in the world , receiving his award at a ceremony held in Rothenburg , Germany , on 8 January 2001 . [S4] Terim received a nomination for UEFA manager of the year 2008 , and Eurosport named him the best coach at UEFA Euro 2008 . [S5] In December 2008 , he was ranked the seventh - best football manager in the world by World Soccer Magazine in 2008 . [S6] His Turkish nickname is " İmparator " , and his Italian nickname is " Imperatore " . [S7] Both names mean " emperor " .

Document: [S0] Heinrich LXXII , Prince Reuss of Lobenstein and Ebersdorf ( 27 March 1797–17 February 1853 ) was the ruling prince of Reuss - Lobenstein from 7 May 1824 until his abdication on 1 October 1848 , and of Reuss - Ebersdorf from 1822 to 1848 . [S1] Unlike with most European monarchies , his large regnal number does not indicate that he was preceded by seventy - one previous rulers also named Heinrich . [S2] By tradition , all male members of the House of Reuss are named Heinrich , and are numbered by order of birth within the family in general . [S3] In the Reuss Younger Line , the numbering system was reset at the beginning of each century ; thus Heinrich LXXII 's high number is directly related to his having been born at the very end of the eighteenth century . [S4] Heinrich LXXII abdicated in 1848 , due to civil unrest in connection with the revolutions that spread through Germany and elsewhere in Europe that year . [S5] The last of his branch of the family , his principality passed to the Prince Reuss zu Schleiz , unifying the lands of the Reuss Younger Line .

[S1] He was the youngest son of Sabah bin Jaber , upon whose death he succeeded . [S2] He was elected to the position by chiefs and notables despite his standing as the youngest son . [S3] He is also the father of Jaber I Al - Sabah who succeeded him . [S4] Bin Sabah is credited with building the first defensive walls in Kuwait . [S5] During his reign , Kuwait also extended its commercial contacts into what is now India , Yemen , and Iraq . [S6] Also during this period , Kuwait established relations with the British East India Company .

Document: [S0] Microserfs , published by HarperCollins in 1995 , is an epistolary novel by Douglas Coupland . [S1] It first appeared in short story form as the cover article for the January 1994 issue of Wired magazine and was subsequently expanded to full novel length . [S2] Set in the early 1990s , it captures the state of the technology industry before Windows 95 , and anticipates the dot - com bubble of the late 1990s . [S3] The novel is presented in the form of diary entries maintained on a PowerBook by the narrator , Daniel . [S4] Because of this , as well as its formatting and usage of emoticons , this novel is similar to what emerged a decade later as the blog format . [S5] Coupland revisited many of the ideas in Microserfs in his 2006 novel JPod , which has been labeled " Microserfs for the Google generation " .

Document: [S0] The Frente de Libertação do Arquipélago da Madeira ( ) , or FLAMA ( which could be read as an archaic Portuguese word for " flame " , flama ) , was a right - wing terrorist paramilitary organisation from Madeira , whose main goal was to achieve Madeira 's independence from mainland Portugal . [S1] FLAMA carried out more than 70 armed and bomb attacks between 1974 - 1976 , during the revolutionary period that followed the Portuguese Carnation Revolution ( April 25 , 1974 ) . [S2] The Carnation Revolution effectively changed the Portuguese regime from an authoritarian dictatorship ( the Estado Novo ) to a democracy ( the Third Republic ) , but only after two years of a transitional period known as PREC ( Processo Revolucionário Em Curso , Portuguese for Ongoing Revolutionary Process ) , characterized by social turmoil and power dispute between left and right wing political forces . [S3] During this period the new government withdrew from Angola and Mozambique , the last Portuguese colonies on mainland Africa . [S4] Some in Madeira thought that their area should be the next to separate . [S5] FLAMA 's demands were more a right - wing political reaction by some of the regional elites to the left - wing nature of the Revolution and its main actors , than a truly ethnic or nationalist separatist goal . [S6] After the normalization of the Portuguese political system , early in 1976 , and the constitutional grant of autonomy to the Portuguese North Atlantic archipelagos of Madeira and Azores ( where a similar organization existed , the Frente de Libertação dos Açores ) , the organization vanished . [S7] Allegedly one of FLAMA 's most important activists was the controversial Alberto João Jardim , the former President of the regional government of Madeira , co - founder of the Madeiran branch of the popular centre - right - wing Portuguese party PSD and former Vice - president of the European People 's Party .

Document: [S0] University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust ( UCLH ) is an NHS foundation trust based in London , United Kingdom . [S2] The Trust has an annual turnover of around £ 940 million and employs approximately 8,180 staff . [S3] Each year its hospitals treat over 500,000 outpatients appointments and admit over 100,000 patients . [S4] In partnership with University College London , UCLH has major research activities is part of the UCLH / UCL Biomedical Research Centre and the UCL Partners academic health science centre . [S5] Its hospitals are also major teaching centres and offer training for nurses , doctors and other health care professionals in partnership with City , University of London , Kings College London , London South Bank University and UCL Medical School .

Document: [S0] The Metacomet Ridge , Metacomet Ridge Mountains , or Metacomet Range of southern New England is a narrow and steep fault - block mountain ridge known for its extensive cliff faces , scenic vistas , microclimate ecosystems , and rare or endangered plants . [S1] The ridge is an important recreation resource located within of more than 1.5 million people , offering four long - distance hiking trails and over a dozen parks and recreation areas , including several historic sites . [S2] It has been the focus of ongoing conservation efforts because of its natural , historic , and recreational value , involving municipal , state , and national agencies and nearly two dozen non - profit organizations . [S3] The Metacomet Ridge extends from New Haven and Branford , Connecticut on Long Island Sound , through the Connecticut River Valley region of Massachusetts , to northern Franklin County , Massachusetts , short of the Vermont and New Hampshire borders for a distance of . [S4] It is geologically distinct from the nearby Appalachian Mountains and surrounding uplands , and is composed of volcanic basalt ( also known as trap rock ) and sedimentary rock in faulted and tilted layers many hundreds of feet thick . [S5] In most cases , the basalt layers are dominant , prevalent , and exposed . [S6] The ridge rises dramatically from much lower valley elevations , although only above sea level at its highest , with an average summit elevation of .

Document: [S0] The Great South Australian Coastal Upwelling System is a seasonal upwelling system in the eastern Great Australian Bight , extending from Ceduna , South Australia , to Portland , Victoria , over a distance of about . [S1] Upwelling events occur in the austral summer ( from November to May ) when seasonal winds blow from the southeast . [S2] These winds blow parallel to the shoreline at certain areas of the coast , which forces coastal waters offshore via Ekman transport and draws up cold , nutrient - rich waters from the ocean floor . [S3] Because the deep water carries abundant nutrients up from the ocean floor , the upwelling area differs from the rest of the Great Australian Bight , especially the areas offshore of Western Australia and the Nullabor in South Australia , which are generally nutrient - poor . [S4] Every summer , the upwelling sustains a bountiful ecosystem that attracts blue whales and supports rich fisheries . [S5] The Great South Australian Coastal Upwelling System ( GSACUS ) is Australia 's only deep - reaching coastal upwelling system , with nutrient - enriched water stemming from depths exceeding . [S6] Recently , a new upwelling centre has been discovered on the western shelf of Tasmania . [S7] Since this new upwelling centre is located outside South Australian waters , the entire upwelling system should be rather called the Great Southern Australian Coastal Upwelling System .

Document: [S0] Brigden is a community in the township of St. Clair , Lambton County , Ontario , Canada . [S1] The community is located at the crossroads of Courtright Line and Brigden Road , between Kimball to the west and Oil City to the east , and about southeast of the city of Sarnia . [S2] Brigden has a population of about 500 and is the centre of a thriving agricultural district . [S3] The community is situated on the former Michigan Central Railroad line and thus is named after William Wharton Brigden , one of the engineers who surveyed the railway in 1936 . [S4] Brigden died of a heart attack on May 26 , 1939 in Battle Creek , Michigan , where he was the superintendent of the city waterworks . [S5] Brigden was a Police village governed by a Village Chairman and a Board of Trustees . [S6] The annual Brigden Fair is the last fair of the season in Lambton County occurring on Canadian Thanksgiving long weekend . [S7] Other annual events include the Brigden Community Fest . [S8] It is also the birthplace of businessman JR Shaw , founder and executive chairman of Shaw Communications .

Document: [S0] Cassin 's finch ( Haemorhous cassinii ) is a bird in the finch family , Fringillidae . [S1] This species and the other " American rosefinches " are placed in the genus Haemorhous . [S2] Adults have a short forked brown tail and brown wings . [S3] They have a longer bill than the purple finch . [S4] Adult males are raspberry red on the head , breast , back and rump ; their back and undertail are streaked . [S5] Adult females have light brown upperparts and light underparts with brown streaks throughout ; their facial markings are less distinct than those of the female purple finch . [S6] Their breeding habitat is coniferous forest in mountains of western North America as far south as northern New Mexico and Arizona ; also Southern California near Baja California . [S7] They nest in large conifers . [S8] They move to lower elevations in winter . [S9] Northernmost breeding birds migrate south , as do some birds throughout the range of the species ; many birds are permanent residents , however . [S10] Some non - breeding birds winter as far south as central interior Mexico . [S11] These birds forage in trees , sometimes in ground vegetation . [S12] They mainly eat seeds , buds and berries , some insects . [S13] When not nesting , they often feed in small flocks . [S14] This bird was named after John Cassin , who was a curator at the Philadelphia Academy of Natural Sciences .

Document: [S0] Muir Beach is a census designated place ( CDP ) , unincorporated community , and beach that is located northwest of San Francisco in western Marin County , California , United States . [S1] It is named for John Muir . [S2] The population was 310 at the 2010 census . [S3] The community itself flanks the northwest side of the beach . [S4] Located about 2 miles ( 3   km ) from the entrance to Muir Woods National Monument , the beach is about 1000 feet ( 305 m ) long and 200 feet ( 61 m ) wide , with coarse sand and several large boulders . [S5] Redwood Creek empties into the beach . [S6] There is a parking lot at the beach , which is accessible via a footbridge . [S7] The beach was formerly called Big Lagoon after a freshwater lagoon that was located where the parking lot is now . [S8] Damage from 20th century dairy farms interfered with the flow of the creek and the lagoon .

[S6] In the 1937 General Election , the party 's strength fell from 32 seats to 11 seats . [S4] The one - hour show was broadcast three times a day in some areas , and was seen all over the world on CNN International . [S6] The " final edition " of the program aired on December 16 , but a new episode on the war against cancer aired two days later on December 18 . [S7] Larry King Live was replaced by Piers Morgan Tonight , a talk show hosted by the British television personality and journalist Piers Morgan , that began airing January 17 , 2011 . [S1] It was located in the Heritage Range of the Ellsworth Mountains , next to the Patriot Hills that give it its name . [S2] The camp was run by the private company Adventure Network International ( now Antarctic Logistics & Expeditions LLC , known as ALE ) , [S3] a company that provides expedition support and tours to the interior of Antarctica . [S4] It was constructed in 1987 and used during the summer months of November to January . [S5] Patriot Hills was for many adventurers and explorers a stop on the way from Chile 's Punta Arenas into the interior of Antarctica . [S6] The flight time from Punta Arenas is about 4.5 hours . [S7] As of November 2010 ALE has moved operations . [S8] Union Glacier Camp is the new base of operations and Union Glacier Blue - Ice Runway SCGC is the new runway . [S9] Patriot Hills is being retained as a backup runway . [S10] In the summer months the temperature rises to −15   ° C . [S11] The temperature in the winter months is estimated to be about −40   ° C , but no one has yet overwintered in the Ellsworth Mountains .

[S6] On 27 February 2012 Lutsenko was sentenced to four years in jail for embezzlement and abuse of office . [S7] Lutsenko was held at the Lukyanivska Prison from 26 December 2010 until 7 April 2013 when he was released from prison because Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych pardoned him ( among others ) for health reasons . [S8] Both Lutsenko and his political allies regard his trial as an act of political persecution by the regime of Viktor Yanukovych . [S9] The European Union , the United States Department of State , Canada , human rights organizations , and other international organizations protested against the sentence and questioned whether it was a " fair , transparent and independent legal process " .
