Document: [S0] In English church history , a nonconformist was a Protestant who did not " conform " to the governance and usages of the established Church of England . [S1] Broad use of the term was precipitated after the Restoration of the British monarchy in 1660 , when the Act of Uniformity 1662 re - established the opponents of reform within the Church of England . [S2] By the late 19th century the term specifically included the Reformed Christians ( Presbyterians , Congregationalists and other Calvinist sects ) , plus the Baptists and Methodists . [S3] The English Dissenters such as the Puritans who violated the Act of Uniformity 1559—typically by practising radical , sometimes separatist , dissent — were retrospectively labelled as nonconformists . [S4] By law and social custom , nonconformists were restricted from many spheres of public life — not least , from access to public office , civil service careers , or degrees at university — and were referred to as suffering from civil disabilities . [S5] In England and Wales in the late 19th century the new terms " free churchman " and " Free Church " started to replace " dissenter " or " Nonconformist " . [S6] One influential nonconformist minister was Matthew Henry , who beginning in 1710 published his multi - volume Commentary that is still used and available in the 21st century . [S7] Isaac Watts is an equally recognized nonconformist minister whose hymns are still sung by Christians worldwide .

Document: [S0] The first Battle of Homs was fought on December 10 , 1260 , between the Ilkhanates of Persia and the forces of Egypt , in Syria . [S1] After the historic Mamluk victory over the Ilkhanates at the Battle of Ain Jalut in September 1260 , Hulagu Khan of the Ilkhanate had the Ayyubid Sultan of Damascus and other Ayyubid princes executed in revenge , thus effectively ending the dynasty in Syria . [S2] However , the defeat at Ain Jalut forced the Ilkhanate armies out of Syria and the Levant . [S3] The main cities of Syria , Aleppo and Damascus were thus left open to Mamluk occupation . [S4] But Homs and Hama remained in the possession of minor Ayyubid princes . [S5] These princes , rather than the Mamluks of Cairo themselves , actually fought and won the First Battle of Homs . [S6] Due to the open war between Hulagu and his cousin Berke of the Golden Horde during the civil war of the Mongol Empire , the Ilkhanate could only afford to send 6,000 troops back into Syria to retake control of the lands . [S7] This expedition was initiated by Ilkhanate generals such as Baidu who was forced to leave Gaza when the Mamluks advanced just before the battle of Ain Jalut . [S8] After quickly recapturing Aleppo , the force travelled southwards to Homs , but were decisively defeated . [S9] This ended the first campaign into Syria by the Ilkhanate , though there were several later incursions , none of which ended with conquests lasting more than a year .

Document: [S0] The Admission to the Union Clause of the United States Constitution , oftentimes called the New States Clause , and found at Article IV , Section 3 , , authorizes the Congress to admit new states into the United States beyond the thirteen already in existence at the time the Constitution went into effect . [S1] The Constitution went into effect on June 21 , 1788 , after ratification by 9 of the 13 states , and the federal government began operations under it on March 4 , 1789 . [S2] Since then , 37 additional states have been admitted into the Union . [S3] Each new state has been admitted on an equal footing with those already in existence . [S4] Of the 37 states admitted to the Union by Congress , all but six have been established within an existing U.S. organized incorporated territory . [S5] A state so created might encompass all or a portion of a territory . [S6] When the people of a territory or a region thereof would make their desire for statehood known to the federal government , in most cases Congress passed an enabling act authorizing the people of that territory or region to frame a proposed state constitution as a step toward admission to the Union . [S7] Although the use of an enabling act was a common historic practice , a number of states were admitted to the Union without one . [S8] In many instances , an enabling act would detail the mechanism by which the territory would be admitted as a state following ratification of their constitution and election of state officers . [S9] Although the use of such an act is a traditional historic practice , a number of territories have drafted constitutions for submission to Congress absent an enabling act and were subsequently admitted . [S10] The broad outline for this process was established by the Land Ordinance of 1784 and the 1787 Northwest Ordinance , both of which predate the present U.S. Constitution . [S11] The Admission to the Union Clause also forbids the creation of new states from parts of existing states without the consent of both the affected states and Congress . [S12] The primary intent of this caveat was to give Eastern states that still had western land claims ( there were four at that time ) a veto over whether their western counties could become states . [S13] This clause has served the same function since , each time a proposal to partition an existing state or states has arisen .

Document: [S0] The Railroad Revival Tour was an annual music tour that featured popular roots , folk , country , rock , bluegrass and Americana acts that began in 2011 . [S1] The musicians travel between shows across the American Southwest in a dozen or so vintage train cars from the 1950s and 1960s . [S2] The outdoor concert locations , sometimes attracting over 10,000 fans , are often a stone 's throw from the train . [S3] The bands eat , sleep and engage in impromptu jam sessions on the train between stops , giving them a chance to collaborate . [S4] On stage at night , they often join in on each other 's sets , sometimes bringing around 30 musicians up to create a rare and rowdy performance . [S5] The organic American roots feeling of the tour also prompts participating musicians to honor U.S. railway history , like Mumford & Sons ' tribute to Woody Guthrie in 2011 . [S6] The inaugural tour in 2011 included performances by Mumford & Sons , Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros , and Old Crow Medicine Show . [S7] A documentary of this first year , called Big Easy Express , directed by Emmett Malloy premiered at SXSW 2012 and won a Grammy Award in 2013 . [S8] The film is currently available on iTunes and DVD / Blu - ray Disc . [S9] In 2011 , Railroad Revival Tour bands Mumford & Sons , Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros , and Old Crow Medicine Show together closed their shows at every stop with " This Train . " [S10] The 2012 tour was slated to include performances by Willie Nelson , Band of Horses , Jamey Johnson , and John Reilly and Friends . [S11] However , the tour was cancelled for 2012 .

Document: [S0] Matagorda Bay ( ) is a large Gulf of Mexico estuary bay on the Texas coast , lying in Calhoun and Matagorda counties and located approximately northeast of Corpus Christi , east - southeast of San Antonio , south - southwest of Houston , and south - southeast of Austin . [S1] It is separated from the Gulf of Mexico by Matagorda Peninsula and serves as the mouth of numerous streams , most notably the Lavaca and Colorado Rivers . [S2] The Texas seaport of Port Lavaca is located on the system 's northwestern extension of Lavaca Bay . [S3] The city of Palacios is found on northeastern extension of Tres Palacios Bay , and Port O'Connor is located on the southwestern tip of the main bay 's shore . [S4] The ghost town of Indianola , which was a major port before it was destroyed by two hurricanes in the late 19th Century , is also found on the bay . [S5] The bay 's shore , especially near the Colorado River delta , provides a habitat for a wide variety of wildlife . [S6] The wildlife serves as a basis for the birding and fishing tourism , and is an essential component of the production of seafood , specifically shrimp and blue crab , which are the specialties of the area . [S7] The fertile land near the bay is ideal for farming , especially for the propagation of rice .

[S2] Mottoes are used by both military branches and smaller units . [S3] While some mottoes are official , others are unofficial . [S8] For the TV show itself the song was recorded live , but the album features a studio version recorded on June 24 . Document: [S0] Fyns Hoved is a bight of northeastern Funen , Denmark , curving south to form the approach to Odense Fjord . [S1] It is the northernmost point of Hindsholm and is thus Funen 's northernmost point , dividing the Kattegat and the Great Belt . [S2] The eastern side of the bight between Fyns Hoved and Skoven , to the south , is irregular , with a beach and hills behind it , and to the south of the bight is a small , shallow bay , Korshavn Bay , with the Korshavn Light in the vicinity . [S3] The bay is a natural harbour used by many yachtsmen . [S4] Fyns Hoved is located in the dry Great Belt region , where rainfall is about per year compared to the national average of per year . [S5] This makes it hospitable to plants that are more common in the dry areas of southern Europe . [S6] The area is frequented by many shore birds and is also a resting place for migrating birds , and harbour porpoises can be seen offshore . [S7] Numerous artists such as Theodor Philipsen , Johannes Larsen and Fritz Syberg have found inspiration in the light and the scenery . [S8] There are many stone walls in the area ; these date back to 1810 , when the seven farmers in the village of Nordskov decided to divide the area between them so that they would each have one northern and one southern strip of land . [S9] The seven cottagers had to content themselves with sharing one strip . [S10] During the German occupation , barracks , a radar installation and artillery on Fyns Hoved guarded the entrance to the Great Belt .

Document: [S0] The Orongorongo River runs for southwest through the Orongorongo Valley in the southern Rimutaka Ranges of the North Island of New Zealand . [S1] The river and its associated catchments lie within the bounds of the Rimutaka Forest Park , which is administered by the Department of Conservation . [S2] Orongorongo River is the main artery of the Rimutaka Range , draining an area with rainfall of up to a year , which is twice as much as the rainfall at the mouth of the river at Cook Strait . [S3] For much of its course the river is a braided river , with a wide bed of greywacke shingle and gravel and a number of streams of water . [S4] The gravel bed can be seen as light - coloured areas of varying width in the adjacent image . [S5] Because the rainfall in the Rimutaka Range often comes in high - intensity rainstorms , the river is prone to violent floods . [S6] The most severe of these floods sweep away most of the river 's vegetated islands every 15 to 20 years . [S7] Between these floods , the shingle islands are gradually colonised by various low growing plants , followed by a host of native shrubs such as tauhinu and manuka , and eventually small trees .

Document: [S0] Skylake is the codename used by Intel for a processor microarchitecture that was launched in August 2015 succeeding the Broadwell microarchitecture . [S1] Skylake is a microarchitecture redesign using the same 14   nm manufacturing process technology as its predecessor , serving as a " tock " in Intel 's " tick - tock " manufacturing and design model . [S2] According to Intel , the redesign brings greater CPU and GPU performance and reduced power consumption . [S3] Skylake CPUs share its microarchitecture with Kaby Lake , Coffee Lake and Cannon Lake CPUs . [S4] Skylake is the last Intel platform on which Windows earlier than Windows 10 will be officially supported by Microsoft , although enthusiast - created modifications exist that allow Windows 8.1 and earlier to continue to receive updates on later platforms . [S5] Some of the processors based on the Skylake microarchitecture are marketed as " 6th - generation Core " . [S6] On October 8 , 2018 , Intel announced new 9th gen Core X 98xx/99xx series CPUs , with the Core i9 - 9980XE Extreme Edition leading the launch .

Document: [S0] The Independent Democratic Action ( ) is a political party in São Tomé and Príncipe . [S1] It was established in 1994 by the then president Miguel Trovoada and is a politically centrist party . [S2] It took part in the 29 July 2001 presidential elections , in which its candidate , Fradique de Menezes , won 55.2 % of the vote and was elected president . [S3] After the elections Fradique de Menezes joined a new party - the Force for Change Democratic Movement - Liberal Party . [S4] In the legislative election held on 3 March 2002 , the Independent Democratic Action was the main party in the Uê Kédadji alliance , that won 16.2 % of the popular vote and 8 out of 55 seats . [S5] It left this alliance and won in the 2006 election 11 out of 55 seats . [S6] In the July 2006 presidential election , its leader Patrice Trovoada ran as the only major opposition candidate , but he was defeated by Menezes . [S7] Trovoada became Prime Minister in February 2008 , but was defeated in a May 2008 vote of confidence proposed by the Movement for the Liberation of São Tomé and Príncipe / Social Democratic Party ( MLSTP / PSD ) , and in June Menezes asked the MLSTP / PSD to form a new government . [S8] The ADI denounced Menezes ' designation of the MLSTP / PSD to form a government as unconstitutional , arguing that it was too late in the parliamentary term to do so , and it took the matter to the Supreme Tribunal of Justice .

Document: [S0] Yūsuf ibn Yaʿqūb ibn Is - ḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm ( ) is a Nabi ( , Prophet ) mentioned in the Qurʾān , the scripture of Islam , and corresponds to Joseph ( son of Jacob ) , a person from the Tanakh , the Jewish religious scripture , and the Christian Bible , who was estimated to have lived in the 16th century BCE . [S1] It is one of the common names in the Middle East and among Muslim nations . [S2] Of all of Jacob 's children , Joseph was the one given the gift of prophecy . [S3] Although the narratives of other prophets are mentioned in various Surahs , the complete narrative of Joseph is given only in one Surah , Yusuf , making it unique . [S4] It is said to be the most detailed narrative in the Qur'an and bears more details than the Biblical counterpart . [S5] Yusuf is believed to have been the eleventh son of Yaʿqūb ( , Jacob ) , and , according to many scholars , his favorite . [S6] According to Ibn Kathir , " Jacob had twelve sons who were the eponymous ancestors of the tribes of the Israelites . [S7] The noblest , the most exalted , the greatest of them was Joseph . " [S8] The story begins with Joseph revealing a ru'ya ( , ' dream ' or ' vision ' ) to his father , which Jacob recognizes . [S9] In addition to the role of God in his life , the story of Yusuf and Zulaikha ( Potiphar 's wife of the Old Testament ) became a popular subject in Persian literature , where it became considerably elaborated over the centuries . [S10] More recently , and relying on the Quran and Muslim , Christian and Jewish scholarly sources , Yusuf 's story has been depicted in a 45-part TV series ( originally in Persian but also dubbed in multiple other languages ) .

Document: [S0] American Theocracy : The Peril and Politics of Radical Religion , Oil , and Borrowed Money in the 21st Century ( ) is a 2005 political commentary book by American political writer Kevin Phillips . [S1] The book is a critique of the past forty years of the Republican coalition in United States politics . [S2] He " presents a nightmarish vision of ideological extremism , catastrophic fiscal irresponsibility , rampant greed , and dangerous shortsightedness . " [S3] Phillips points to three unifying themes holding this coalition together . [S4] First , its tie to oil and the role oil plays in American and world events . [S5] Second , to the coalition of social conservatives , Evangelicals and Pentecostals in this Republican coalition . [S6] Finally , he points to the " debt culture " of this coalition , and to a coming " debt bubble " related to the debt of the U.S. Government and U.S. consumers . [S7] He argues that similar issues have been prevalent in the past , when other world powers , such as the Roman Empire and the British Empire declined from their peaks and fell into disarray . [S8] While working as a strategist in the presidential campaign of Richard Nixon , Phillips wrote The Emerging Republican Majority . [S9] In that book , Phillips predicted the formation of this very coalition that he criticizes in his current book . [S10] In American Theocracy he admits that while these " mutations , " as he calls them , could have been predicted , he did not foresee the extent to which they would develop and dominate the coalition he helped put together . [S11] The last chapter of this book references his first work , and is called " The Erring Republican Majority . "

Document: [S0] John of Islay ( or John MacDonald ) ( 1434 – 1503 ) was a late medieval Scottish magnate . [S1] He was Earl of Ross and the 4th Lord of the Isles as well as being Mac Domhnaill , chief of Clan Donald . [S2] John would however prove to be the last of the Lords of the Isles , overmighty subjects of the Stewart Kings of Scotland and virtual kings in their own right in the Western Isles . [S3] His struggle for power with King James III of Scotland ended in humiliation , following which his illegitimate son Angus Óg rebelled against his rule . [S4] In a bitter civil war , John 's fleet of galleys met those of Angus sometime in the early 1480s off the coast of Mull at the Battle of Bloody Bay , in which John 's cause was defeated . [S5] After Bloody Bay he became an inconsequential figure ; and Angus continued to dominate the affairs of Clan Donald up until his murder in 1490 . [S6] In 1493 James IV brought the Lordship of the Isles to an end . [S7] John died unlamented in 1503 , having witnessed the almost complete destruction of his family inheritance .

Document: [S0] Ronald Leonard is an American cellist . [S1] He has had a distinguished career as a soloist , chamber musician , principal cellist and teacher . [S2] He is currently on the faculties of the USC Thornton School of Music and the Colburn School . [S3] He was a winner of the Walter Naumburg Competition while a student at the Curtis Institute of Music , where he studied with Leonard Rose and Orlando Cole . [S4] His first professional position was as a cellist in the Cleveland Orchestra , where he sat on the second stand . [S5] Two years later Mr. Leonard became principal cellist of the Rochester Philharmonic Orchestra and at that time began teaching at the Eastman School of Music . [S6] He taught at Eastman for 17 years , spent one year as cellist of the Vermeer Quartet , and then was appointed principal cellist of the Los Angeles Philharmonic , a post he held for 24 years . [S7] During this time , he soloed frequently with the orchestra . [S8] During this entire period he has been very active as a soloist , chamber musician and teacher . [S9] Conducting is his most recent activity ; Mr. Leonard is the conductor of the Colburn School Chamber Orchestra and he has been very involved at the USC Thornton School of Music , working with the string sections of both the USC Thornton Symphony and the USC Thornton Chamber Orchestra . [S10] From 1993 to 2003 , he held the prestigious post of " Gregor Piatigorsky Endowed Chair in Violoncello " at the USC Thornton School of Music . [S11] He was only third person to ever hold the position , following Piatigorsky himself and Lynn Harrell ( 1986 – 1993 ) . [S12] He is known internationally as " one of the better cellists originally from Rhode Island " .

Document: [S0] Cornelius Ryan 's A Bridge Too Far gives an account of Operation Market Garden , a failed Allied attempt to break through German lines at Arnhem in the occupied Netherlands during World War II . [S1] The title of the book comes from a comment made by British Lieutenant General Frederick Browning , deputy commander of the First Allied Airborne Army , who told Field Marshal Bernard Montgomery before the operation , " I think we may be going a bridge too far . " [S2] Drawing on a wide variety of sources , Ryan also documented his account of the 1944 battle with pictures and maps and included a section on the survivors , “ Soldiers and Civilians – What They Do Today ” . [S3] One particular focus was on the tactical mistakes made in planning the operation . [S4] Until Ryan 's book , Market Garden had been a classic example of victors writing the history . [S5] Popular accounts of World War II usually tended not to mention the battle at all or put Montgomery 's spin on it as being a " partial success " . [S6] The 1974 book was published by Simon & Schuster in New York and by Hamish Hamilton in London . [S7] There were frequent later editions , and a film based on it was released in 1977 .

Document: [S0] " Steam " is the second single from English rock musician Peter Gabriel 's 1992 album Us . [S1] Gabriel has said that the song is about a relationship in which the woman is sophisticated , bright , cultured , and knows everything about anything and that the man knows nothing about anything , except , he does know about the woman , and she does n't know much about herself . [S2] In certain countries , " Steam " was more successful than Gabriel 's previous single , " Digging in the Dirt " , but in others , it was not . [S3] It reached number 10 on the UK Singles Chart , number 32 on the US Billboard Hot 100 , and number one on the US Modern Rock Tracks chart . [S4] Elsewhere , the song was a number - one hit in Canada , topping the RPM Top Singles chart for the issue dated February 27 , 1993 , knocking Whitney Houston 's massive hit " I Will Always Love You " off the top spot after a 10-week run . [S5] It was also a top 10 hit in New Zealand and Ireland , peaking at number seven in both countries . [S6] An alternative version of this song called " Quiet Steam " was a B - side on the " Digging in the Dirt " single . [S7] It is a very lo - fi take on the popular version that appeared on the album . [S8] On Secret World Live , " Steam " is preceded for a minute or so by the " Quiet Steam " version .

Dearle ( 1859 in London – 15 January 1932 ) was a British textile and stained - glass designer trained by the artist and craftsman William Morris who was much influenced by the Pre - Raphaelite Brotherhood . [S1] Dearle designed many of the later wallpapers and textiles released by Morris & Co. , and contributed background and foliage patterns to tapestry designs featuring figures by Edward Burne - Jones and others . [S2] Beginning in his teens as a shop assistant and then design apprentice , Dearle rose to become Morris & Co. 's chief designer by 1890 , creating designs for tapestries , embroidery , wallpapers , woven and printed textiles , stained glass , and carpets . [S3] Following Morris 's death in 1896 , Dearle was appointed Art Director of the firm , and became its principal stained glass designer on the death of Burne - Jones in 1898 . [S4] Morris 's reputation overshadowed Dearle 's work throughout Dearle 's career : Dearle exhibited early patterns under Morris 's name and Dearle designs continue to be sold as Morris patterns . [S5] Critical assessment of Dearle 's work then underwent a significant change , during the final decades of the twentieth century , recognizing Dearle 's mature work as having a unique artistic vision of its own . [S6] Dearle always remained close to Morris 's esthetic , but from the 1890s onward he incorporated a distinctive set of Persian and Turkish influences .

Document: [S0] Raetia was the name of a canton of the Helvetic Republic from 1798 to 1803 , corresponding to modern Graubünden and composed of the Free State of the Three Leagues . [S1] Until 1799 , the canton was administered by the central government of the Helvetic Republic . [S2] The districts of Chiavenna , Valtellina and Bormio , previously dependencies of the Leagues , were never a part of the canton , having permanently been detached from the Leagues after Revolutionary France fomented revolt there , leading them to be annexed to the Cisalpine Republic on October 10 , 1797 . [S3] The districts subsequently joined the Austrian client kingdom of Lombardy - Venetia after the Congress of Vienna and eventually become the Italian province of Sondrio . [S4] The town of Campione , an imperial fief into the Landvogtei of Lugano at the same time , joined Lombardy leading to its current position as an Italian enclave within Ticino . [S5] With the Napoleonic Act of Mediation in 1803 , the canton was reestablished as Graubünden , finally incorporating the Three Leagues into a decentralized and federal Switzerland .

Document: [S0] The Wedding Dance ( sometimes known as The Dance Village ) is a 1566 oil - on - panel painting by Pieter Bruegel the Elder . [S1] Owned by the museum of the Detroit Institute of Arts in Detroit , Michigan , the work was discovered by its director in England in 1930 , and brought to Detroit . [S2] It is believed to be one of a set of three Bruegel works from around the same time , The Wedding Dance , The Peasant Wedding ( 1567 ) and The Peasant Dance ( 1569 ) . [S3] The painting depicts 125 wedding guests . [S4] As was customary in the Renaissance period , the brides wore black and men wore codpieces . [S5] Voyeurism is depicted throughout the entire art work ; dancing was disapproved of by the authorities and the church , and the painting can be seen as both a critique and comic depiction of a stereotypical oversexed , overindulgent , peasant class of the times .

[S3] Hardon 's Catholic Catechism remains a standard work on Catholic orthodoxy even to this day . [S4] The book is published with the nihil obstat and imprimatur .

Document: [S0] " Long Hard Road Out of Hell " is a song by American rock band Marilyn Manson and British trip hop band Sneaker Pimps , released as a single from the soundtrack to the 1997 motion picture Spawn . [S1] An arena rock and gothic rock song , " Long Hard Road Out of Hell " was written by Marilyn Manson and Twiggy Ramirez and produced by Manson and Sean Beavan . [S2] Its lyrics are about self - loathing and its title is derived from John Milton 's Paradise Lost ( 1667 ) . [S3] After the track was written , the Sneaker Pimps ' Kelli Ali was recruited to perform background vocals on it , as the Spawn soundtrack featured collaborations between hard rock artists and electronic music artists . [S4] The Sneaker Pimps were dissatisfied with the final track and wanted a remix of it to be released as a single instead ; conversely , Manson deemed it a personal favorite . [S5] " Long Hard Road Out of Hell " received mixed reviews from music critics ; some found it heartfelt while others felt it was too indistinct from other Marilyn Manson songs . [S6] Commentators noted that the track encapsulated the evolution of the band 's sound from the industrial music of Antichrist Superstar ( 1996 ) to the glam rock of Mechanical Animals ( 1998 ) . [S7] Manson initially approached Jonathan Glazer to direct the video for the track , but rejected his concept for it ; Glazer later used his concept for the video for Radiohead 's " Karma Police " ( 1997 ) . [S8] The music video for " Long Hard Road Out of Hell " was directed by Matthew Rolston . [S9] It depicts Manson in a dress and a group of models who initially appear to be female but are revealed to be male . [S10] The clip garnerd acclaim from critics for its imagery .

Document: [S0] Fatima Jinnah Park ( , Bagh - e - Fatima Jinnah ) , is a public recreational park situated within the Sector F-9 of Islamabad , Pakistan . [S1] It is named after Fatima Jinnah , the younger sister of Muhammad Ali Jinnah , the founder of Pakistan . [S2] Fatima Jinnah Park vast acreage is mostly covered by greenery , with a few man - made structures dotting the landscape . [S3] Most of the park area is effectively a wildlife sanctuary , except for a few areas of the park that are close to residential districts . [S4] The park is bounded by a steel fence with entrance doors placed at regular intervals , although only a few are routinely open and used . [S5] A further strip of land outside of the fence is lined with a footpath . [S6] A well laid network of footpaths lies inside the park , with neat grass and a few statues . [S7] The park is known for its wildlife , and the question of further development there divides people in the surrounding communities , many of whom worry that development would jeopardize its untamed feel .

Document: [S0] San Pablito is a small town located on the side of the Guajalote Mountain in the Sierra Norte de Puebla mountain region in central east Mexico . [S1] It belongs to the Pahuatlán municipality of the state of Puebla . [S2] Culturally it is dominated by the Otomi although it is part of the La Huasteca region . [S3] San Pablito is best known for the commercial production of a bark paper called amate as a handcraft . [S4] This paper is mostly sold to Nahua painters in Guerrero , but it is also sold nationally and internationally on its own . [S5] The paper is made much the way it was before the arrival of the Spanish . [S6] Originally , it was made only by the area 's shamans for ritual purpose but today commercial production is mostly done by the town 's women and children as many men have left to work in the United States .

Document: [S0] The North American Agreement on Environmental Cooperation ( NAAEC ) is an environmental agreement between the United States of America , Canada and Mexico as a side - treaty of the North American Free Trade Agreement . [S1] The agreement came into effect January 1 , 1994 . [S2] The agreement consists of a declaration of principles and objectives concerning conservation and the protection of the environment as well as concrete measures to further cooperation on these matters between the three countries . [S3] Part Three of the NAAEC establishes the Commission for Environmental Cooperation ( CEC ) , which was set up as part of the agreement . [S4] The structure of the CEC is composed of the Council , which is the governing body , a Secretariat based in Montreal and the Joint Public Advisory Committee .

Document: [S0] Jon A. Lund ( born November 6 , 1928 ) is an American attorney and politician from Maine . [S1] Lund , a Republican , served as Maine Attorney General from 1972 – 1975 . [S2] Prior to his time as the first full - time attorney general in Maine history , Lund was an assistant country attorney for Kennebec County , member of the Augusta City Council and two - time county attorney for Kennebec County . [S3] He was also elected to the Maine House of Representatives ( 1965 – 1966 ; 1969 – 1972 ) and Maine Senate ( 1967 – 1968 ) . [S4] During his time as attorney general , Lund took prominent stances on many controversial issues affecting Maine at the time , even though some were outside of the jurisdiction of his office . [S5] Among these stances included opposition to the proposed Dickey - Lincoln Dam in Northern Maine , which he opposed on environmental grounds . [S6] The project was eventually stopped in 1984 . [S7] Lund is a graduate of Bowdoin College and Harvard Law School .

Document: [S0] The 4th House of Orléans , sometimes called the House of Bourbon - Orléans ( ) to distinguish it , is the fourth holder of a surname previously used by several branches of the Royal House of France , all descended in the legitimate male line from the dynasty 's founder , Hugh Capet . [S1] The house was founded in 1661 by Prince Philippe , Duke of Anjou , younger son of king Louis XIII and younger brother of king Louis XIV , the " Sun King " . [S2] From 1709 until the French Revolution , the Orléans dukes were next in the order of succession to the French throne after members of the senior branch of the House of Bourbon , descended from king Louis XIV . [S3] Although Louis XIV 's direct descendants retained the throne , his brother Philippe 's descendants flourished until the end of the French monarchy . [S4] They held the Crown from 1830 to 1848 , and they still are pretenders to the French throne .

Document: [S0] Joshua Cushman ( April 11 , 1761 – January 27 , 1834 ) was a U.S. Representative from Massachusetts and from Maine . [S1] Born in Halifax , Massachusetts , Cushman served in the Continental Army from April 1 , 1777 , until March 1780 . [S2] He was graduated from Harvard University in 1787 , studied theology , was ordained to the ministry and licensed to preach . [S3] He was pastor of the Congregational Church in Winslow , Maine for nearly twenty years . [S4] He served in the Massachusetts State Senate , and served as member of the Massachusetts House of Representatives . [S5] Cushman was elected as Democratic - Republican from Massachusetts to the Sixteenth Congress ( March 4 , 1819 – March 3 , 1821 ) . [S1] Created by directors Ron Clements and John Musker and animated by Mark Henn , Tiana is voiced by Anika Noni Rose as an adult , while Elizabeth M. Dampier voices the character as a child . [S2] Tiana is loosely based on two princesses : Princess Emma , the heroine of E. D. Baker 's novel The Frog Princess , and the princess from the Brothers Grimm fairy tale " The Frog Prince " , which inspired Baker 's novel . [S3] A hardworking waitress who dreams of opening her own restaurant , Tiana finds her progress stalled when she transforms into a frog after desperately kissing a prince who has been turned into one by an evil witch doctor . [S4] The ninth Disney Princess , Tiana is the first to be of African - American heritage . [S5] Tiana has been mostly positively received , with critics praising her personality and values . [S6] However , the depiction of Tiana and her community has been criticized for lacking " emphasis on racial issues " . [S7] The decision to depict the two main characters , Tiana and Naveen , as frogs for the majority of the movie has also caused controversy , with some saying that it is equating people of color to animals .

Document: [S0] Liangzi Lake ( ) , originally Fan Lake ( 樊湖 ) , is a freshwater lake in China , it is located in the southeastern part of Hubei Province divided between the Liangzihu Scenic Spot Office of Jiangxia District , Wuhan and the Liangzihu District of Ezhou City ( both areas named after the lake ) . [S1] This rural area south of Wuhan ) , situated in the south bank of the middle reaches of Yangtze River . [S2] The lake is 370   km , with a drainage area of 3265   km , an elevation of 20 m , length 31.7   km and mean width 9.6   km ( max 12.3 m ) . [S3] The shoreline of lake is highly indented . [S4] Liangzi Lake appears to have two outlets . [S5] On the northers side of the lake , a small river or canal flows from Liangzi into Tangxun Lake ( ) , and urban lake on the south side of Wuhan , which eventually drains into the Yangtze . [S6] On the eastern side of the lake , another river flows from Liangzi Lake toward Ezhou , where it enters the Yangtze as well . [S7] On January 1 , 2018 , Ezhou officially implemented a new law called " Liangzihu District Marine Life Protection Zone Absolute Fishing Ban Work Implementation Plan"(《梁子湖区水生生物保护区全面禁捕工作实施方案 》 ) . [S8] The lake is rich in fish and it is the origin of Wuchang Bream . [S9] Analysis of core samples extracted from the bottom of the lake allows scientists to measure the presence of metals such as copper , lead , nickel and zinc in the environment over the last several thousand ages ; they provide evidence for the existence of mining and metal smelting in the region as early as 1500 BC , during the time of the State of Chu . [S10] ( The Huangshi / Daye region east of the lake continues to be a mining and metallurgical center to this day . ) [S11] " Sister Lakes " partnership has been established between Liangzi Lake and Lake Pepin in Minnesota .

Document: [S0] During the American Civil War , music played a prominent role on both sides of the conflict : Union and Confederate . [S1] On the American Civil War battlefield , different instruments including bugles , drums , and fifes were played to issue marching orders or sometimes simply to boost the morale of one 's fellow soldiers . [S2] Singing was also employed as a recreational activity but as a release from the inevitable tensions that come with fighting in a war , particularly a war in which the issue of freedom of a race is to be decided . [S3] In camp , music was a diversion away from the bloodshed , helping the soldiers deal with homesickness and boredom . [S4] Soldiers of both sides often engaged in recreation with musical instruments , and when the opposing armies were near each other , sometimes the bands from both sides of the conflict played against each other on the night before a battle . [S5] Each side had its particular favorite tunes , while some music was enjoyed by Northerners and Southerners alike , as exemplified by United States President Abraham Lincoln 's love of Dixie , the unofficial anthem of the Confederacy . [S6] To this day , many of the songs are sung when a patriotic piece is required . [S7] The war 's music also inspired music artists such as Lynyrd Skynyrd and Elvis Presley .

[S4] Other compositions included " Worry Worry Worry " , " The Old Chaperone " , " Take a Letter Miss Smith " , " I 'll Wait " , " Leave It to Joan " and " Something Old Something New . " [S5] George Tibbles who co - wrote the Woody Woodpecker Song with him remained friends for the next 23 years until Idriss ' death . [S6] Tibbles was a Producer and eventual Head Writer of the classic television series My Three Sons in the 1960s and gave Idriss music composing and script writing assignments on the show .

Document: [S0] Carol II ( 15 October 18934 April 1953 ) reigned as King of Romania from 8 June 1930 until his coerced abdication on 6 September 1940 . [S1] Carol was the eldest son of Ferdinand I and became crown prince upon the death of his grand - uncle , King Carol I in 1914 . [S2] He was the first of the Hohenzollern kings of Romania to be born in the country ( both of his predecessors were born and grew up in Germany and only came to Romania as adults ) . [S3] Carol , by contrast , spoke Romanian as his first language and was the first member of the Romanian royal family to be raised in the Orthodox faith . [S4] He possessed a hedonistic personality that contributed to the controversies marring his reign , and his life was marked by numerous scandals , among them marriages to Zizi Lambrino and Princess Helen of Greece and Denmark , daughter of King Constantine I of Greece . [S5] His continued affairs with Magda Lupescu obliged him to renounce his succession rights in 1925 and leave the country . [S6] Princess Helen eventually divorced him in 1928 . [S7] King Ferdinand died in 1927 and Carol 's five - year - old son ascended the throne as Michael I. Carol then returned to Romania in 1930 and replaced his son and the regency that had been in place . [S8] His reign was marked by re - alignment with Nazi Germany , adoption of anti - semitic laws and ultimately evolved into a personal dictatorship beginning in 1938 . [S9] On 6 September 1940 , he was forced by his Prime Minister Ion Antonescu to leave the country and withdraw abroad into exile . [S10] He was succeeded by his son Michael .

[S1] Fastow was one of the key figures behind the complex web of off - balance - sheet special purpose entities ( limited partnerships which Enron controlled ) used to conceal Enron 's massive losses in their quarterly balance sheets . [S2] By unlawfully maintaining personal stakes in these ostensibly independent ghost - entities , he was able to defraud Enron out of tens of millions of dollars . [S3] The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission subsequently opened an investigation into his and the company 's conduct in 2001 . [S4] Fastow served a six - year prison sentence for charges related to these acts . [S5] His wife , Lea Weingarten , also worked at Enron , where she was an assistant treasurer ; she pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud , money laundering conspiracy and filing fraudulent income tax returns , and served jail time before early release to a halfway house .

Document: [S0] Andrea Lilio ( 1555 - 1642 ) was an Italian painter born in Ancona , hence he also is known as L'Anconitano . [S1] He painted mainly in his native city , as well as in Rome , where he was active from the beginning of the 17th century until around 1640 . [S2] He was employed by Pope Sixtus V in the decoration of the library of the Vatican and in the decoration of the Scala Santa in San Giovanni Laterano . [S3] In the latter , he painted , Moses striking the Rock and Moses with the Brazen Serpent . [S4] Said to have been a pupil of Federico Barocci , Lilio created a popular niche for himself by painting allegories for aristocratic audiences . [S5] In fact , it is altogether possible that Lilio collaborated for the illustrations of Cesare Ripa 's Iconologia , which was a popular source for such motifs for a very long time . [S6] He died at Ascoli Piceno . [S7] In a chapel of the Chiesa Nuova , he painted The Archangel Michael driving fallen angels from Heaven . [S8] He continued to ornament churches and convents of Rome during the reign of Pope Clement VIII . [S9] One of his masterpieces , the Martyrdom of Saint Lawrence , was painted for Santa Caterina in Ancona . [S10] He painted the Christ Washing the Feet of His Disciples for the nave of Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome . [S11] He also was part of the team active in the painting of the Sistine chapel ( chapel of Nativity ) in Santa Maria Maggiore . [S12] For the cathedral of Fano , he painted a picture of All Saints . [S13] Four new allegorical paintings by Lilio were identified in Milan 's Bagatti Valsecchi Museum , Milan .

Document: [S0] Stars and Stripes Forever is a 1952 American Technicolor film biography of the late-19th-/early-20th - century composer and band leader John Philip Sousa . [S1] This 20th Century Fox feature was produced by Lamar Trotti , directed by Henry Koster , and stars Clifton Webb , Debra Paget , Robert Wagner , and Ruth Hussey . [S2] The film 's title is taken from Sousa 's " The Stars and Stripes Forever " , which has become the best known of his military marches . [S3] While the film 's storyline is loosely based on Sousa 's autobiography Marching Along , the film takes considerable liberties and dramatic license , often expanding and examining themes and passages from Sousa 's book . [S4] Two examples : In the film , Private Willie Little ( Robert Wagner ) , is credited with inventing the Sousaphone and naming it after his mentor , but in reality Sousa himself designed the instrument . [S5] The inspiration for the film 's title march is depicted in a scene with a voice over by Webb quoting Sousa 's actual description of its creation while he was aboard ship recovering from typhoid fever . [S6] In reality , having learned of the sudden death of his band 's manager , Sousa and his wife canceled their European vacation and were returning to the U.S. by steamship when the march came to him .

Document: [S0] Newell Convers Wyeth ( October 22 , 1882 – October 19 , 1945 ) , known as N. C. Wyeth , was an American artist and illustrator . [S1] He was the pupil of artist Howard Pyle and became one of America 's greatest illustrators . [S2] During his lifetime , Wyeth created over 3,000 paintings and illustrated 112 books , 25 of them for Scribner 's , the Scribner Classics , which is the work for which he is best known . [S3] The first of these , Treasure Island , was one of his masterpieces and the proceeds paid for his studio . [S4] Wyeth was a realist painter just as the camera and photography began to compete with his craft . [S5] Sometimes seen as melodramatic , his illustrations were designed to be understood quickly . [S6] Wyeth , who was both a painter and an illustrator , understood the difference , and said in 1908 , " Painting and illustration can not be mixed — one can not merge from one into the other . " [S7] He is the father of Andrew Wyeth and the grandfather of Jamie Wyeth , both known American painters .

Document: [S0] Historiographic metafiction is a term coined by Canadian literary theorist Linda Hutcheon in the late 1980s . [S1] The term is used for works of fiction which combine the literary devices of metafiction with historical fiction . [S2] Works regarded as historiographic metafiction are also distinguished by frequent allusions to other artistic , historical and literary texts ( i.e. [S3] intertextuality ) in order to show the extent to which works of both literature and historiography are dependent on the history of discourse . [S4] The term is closely associated with works of postmodern literature , usually novels . [S5] According to Hutcheon , in " A Poetics of Postmodernism " , works of historiographic metafiction are " those well - known and popular novels which are both intensely self - reflexive and yet paradoxically also lay claim to historical events and personages " . [S6] Works often described as examples of historiographical metafiction include : William Shakespeare 's Pericles , Prince of Tyre ( c.1608 ) , John Fowles ' The French Lieutenant 's Woman ( 1969 ) , E. L. Doctorow 's Ragtime ( 1975 ) , William Kennedy 's Legs ( 1975 ) , Salman Rushdie 's Midnight 's Children ( 1981 ) , A. S. Byatt 's Possession ( 1990 ) , Michael Ondaatje 's The English Patient ( 1992 ) , Thomas Pynchon 's Mason & Dixon ( 1997 ) and many others . [S7] By seeking to represent both actual historical events from World War Two while , at the same time , problematizing the very notion of doing exactly that , Kurt Vonnegut 's Slaughterhouse - Five ( 1969 ) features a metafictional , " Janus - headed " perspective .

Document: [S0] Greatest Hits is a compilation album by the British rock band Queen , released worldwide on 26 October 1981 . [S1] The album consisted of Queen 's best - selling singles since their first chart appearance in 1974 with " Seven Seas of Rhye " , up to their 1980 hit " Flash " ( though in some countries " Under Pressure " , the band 's 1981 chart - topper with David Bowie , was included ) . [S2] There was no universal track listing or cover art for the album , and each territory 's tracks were dependent on what singles had been released there and which were successful . [S3] Queen 's Greatest Hits was an instant success , peaking at number one on the UK Albums Chart for four weeks . [S4] It has spent 833 weeks in the UK Charts , and is the best - selling album of all time in the UK , selling over six million copies . [S5] It is certified eight times platinum in the United States , and is Queen 's most commercially successful album worldwide with over 25 million copies sold , making it one of the best - selling albums of all time . [S6] Radiohead guitarist Ed O'Brien hailed the UK edition of Greatest Hits as " impeccable " and " absolutely genius " , while British journalist Brian Viner called it the greatest album of all time .

Document: [S0] " The Murders in the Rue Morgue " is a short story by Edgar Allan Poe published in Graham 's Magazine in 1841 . [S1] It has been recognized as the first modern detective story ; Poe referred to it as one of his " tales of ratiocination " . [S2] C. Auguste Dupin is a man in Paris who solves the mystery of the brutal murder of two women . [S3] Numerous witnesses heard a suspect , though no one agrees on what language was spoken . [S4] At the murder scene , Dupin finds a hair that does not appear to be human . [S5] As the first fictional detective , Poe 's Dupin displays many traits which became literary conventions in subsequent fictional detectives , including Sherlock Holmes and Hercule Poirot . [S6] Many later characters , for example , follow Poe 's model of the brilliant detective , his personal friend who serves as narrator , and the final revelation being presented before the reasoning that leads up to it . [S7] Dupin himself reappears in " The Mystery of Marie Rogêt " and " The Purloined Letter " .

Document: [S0] Song of Freedom is a 1936 British film directed by J. [S1] Elder Wills and starring Paul Robeson . [S2] One of two elements pivotal to the plot is an opera composer named Gabriel Donizetti , presumably suggested by the historical opera composer Gaetano Donizetti . [S3] The other is a medallion that serves to identify Robeson 's character as a descendant of an African monarch . [S4] Song of Freedom may best represent the opportunity Robeson was looking for to " give a true picture of many aspects of the life of the coloured man in the West . [S5] Hitherto on the screen , he has been characterized or presented only as a comedy character . [S6] This film shows him as a real man . " [S7] Robeson was also given final cut approval on the film , an unprecedented option at the time for an actor of any race . [S8] As in Sanders of the River , the film called for documentary scenes of West African traditional dances and ceremonies , but this time Robeson obtained a contract giving him final cut , so that the film ’s message would not be changed behind the doors of the editing room . [S9] Robeson plays Zinga , a black dockworker in England with a great baritone singing voice . [S10] He is discovered by an opera impresario , and is catapulted into great fame as an international opera star . [S11] Yet he feels alienated from his African past , and out of place in England . [S12] By chance , he is informed that an ancestral medallion that he wears is proof of his lineage to African kings , and he leaves fame and fortune to take his rightful place of royalty . [S13] Reunited with his people , he plans to improve their lives by combining the best of western technology with the best of traditional African ways . [S14] Although the film was not a box office success in the US , it was notably chosen in 1950 to open the convention of Ghana 's Convention People 's Party . [S15] The ceremonies were presided over by the future first prime minister of independent Ghana , Kwame Nkrumah , Robeson 's friend from his London years .

[S1] Trump has proposed sizable income tax cuts and deregulation consistent with conservative ( Republican Party ) policies , along with significant infrastructure investment and protection for entitlements for the elderly , typically considered liberal ( Democratic Party ) policies . [S2] His anti - globalization policies of trade protectionism and immigration reduction cross party lines . [S3] Trump has said that he is " totally flexible on very , very many issues . " [S4] Trump 's signature issue is immigration , especially illegal immigration , and in particular building or expanding a border wall between the U.S. and Mexico . [S5] As of October 2016 , Trump 's campaign had posted fourteen categories of policy proposals on his website , which have been since removed . [S6] During October 2016 , Trump outlined a series of steps for his first 100 days in office . [S7] Trump 's political positions , and his descriptions of his beliefs , have frequently changed . [S8] Politico has described his positions as " eclectic , improvisational and often contradictory . " [S9] According to an NBC News count , over the course of his campaign Trump made " 141 distinct shifts on 23 major issues . " [S10] Fact - checking organizations reported that during the campaign , Trump made a record number of false statements and lies compared to other candidates , a pattern that continued once in office .

Document: [S0] Joseph Israel ( about 1780 – 4 September 1804 ) was an officer in the United States Navy during the Quasi - War with France and the First Barbary War . [S1] Israel entered the Navy as Midshipman 15 January 1801 . [S2] He served in Maryland during the Quasi - War with France and in Chesapeake , New York , and Constitution during operation in the Mediterranean against the Barbary pirates . [S3] Midshipman Israel was killed 4 September 1804 when ketch Intrepid exploded in the harbor of Tripoli during the night effort to destroy the enemy shipping led by Lieutenant Richard Somers . [S4] A monument to the memory of Israel and his fellow officers and men stands on the grounds of the United States Naval Academy at Annapolis . [S5] Israel was reported to be of the Jewish faith , although " there was no evidence that Israel is a Jew or of Jewish ancestry . " [S6] USS Israel ( DD-98 ) was named in honor of him .

Document: [S0] The is a subregion of the Chūbu region and Kansai region in Japan that runs along the Pacific Ocean . [S1] The name comes from the Tōkaidō , one of the Edo Five Routes . [S2] Because Tōkai is a sub - region and is not officially classified , there is some disagreement about where exactly the region begins and ends , however Japanese maps widely conclude that the region includes Shizuoka , Aichi , Gifu and Mie prefectures . [S3] The largest major city in the region is Nagoya and the Chūkyō Metropolitan Area ( Nagoya Metropolitan Area ) makes up a large portion of the region and has Japan 's third strongest economy . [S4] The business influence of this urban area sometimes extends out into the outlying areas of the three prefectures centered on Nagoya which are Aichi , Gifu , and Mie ; this area is sometimes referred to as the Chūkyō region . [S5] Tōkai is a heavy manufacturing area and is one of the most industrial regions in Japan . [S6] Its coast is lined with densely populated cities with economies that thrive on factories . [S7] The Tōkai region has experienced a number of large earthquakes in the past , including the two great earthquakes in 1944 ( also known as the " Tonankai earthquake " ) and 1945 ( also known as the " Mikawa earthquake " ) . [S8] Following the work of Kiyoo Mogi , it is predicted that there is a possibility that the area will be subject to a shallow magnitude 8.0 earthquake in the near future . [S9] Nagoya , Shizuoka , and other large cities would be greatly damaged , with potential casualties in the tens of thousands . [S10] The Coordinating Committee for Earthquake Prediction designated the region as an Area of Specific Observation in 1970 , and upgraded it to an Area of Intensified Observation in 1974 .

Document: [S0] Lough Owel ( ) is a mesotrophic lough in the Midlands of Ireland , situated north of Mullingar , the county town of Westmeath . [S1] It has a maximum depth of 22 m . [S2] Water from Lough Owel feeds the Royal Canal , a canal crossing Ireland from Dublin to the River Shannon . [S3] Access to the lake can be gained from a carpark and pier to the south of the N4 Mullingar to Longford route . [S4] Lough Owel and Lough Ennell are two of many lakes that form the River Brosna drainage basin . [S5] The Brosna is a tributary of the Shannon , flowing through Mullingar and Kilbeggan , both in Westmeath , and from there through the town of Clara ( County Offaly ) into the Shannon . [S6] The Viking chieftain Turgesius was drowned in Lough Owel by Máel Sechnaill mac Maíl Ruanaid in 845 . [S7] Since 1996 the lough has received international protection as a Ramsar site . [S8] It is noted for its birdlife and is also well known amongst anglers , and holds a few char along with brown trout .

[S1] He started playing professionally for Sportivo Dock Sud in 1938 . and he was sold in June 1939 to River Plate . [S2] He was part of the team known as La Máquina ( " the machine " ) which dominated Argentine football in the 1940s , and was also a member of the Argentine national team that won three South American Championships during the same decade . [S3] During his time at River Plate he won 4 titles and is considered one of their greatest ever players . [S4] After a very successful time at River Plate He moved to Platense , from 1951 to 1953 , where he played in 39 games making 3 goals . [S5] Muñoz played 11 times for the Argentina national team scoring two goals , he was part of the squad that won Copa América 1945 . [S6] He never played in the FIFA World Cup because the best part of his career coincided with the Second World War . [S7] After retiring as a player Muñoz went on to become the manager and then president of Club Atlético Platense .

Document: [S0] The Battle of Sio , fought between December 1943 and March 1944 , was the break - out and pursuit phase of General Douglas MacArthur 's Huon Peninsula campaign , part of the New Guinea campaign of World War II . [S1] After the defeat of the Japanese in the Battle of Sattelberg , Australian Army forces broke through the Japanese positions around Finschhafen . [S2] Constant pressure from US Navy PT boats , Australian land forces and Allied aircraft brought the Japanese logistical system to the brink of collapse , resulting in disease , malnutrition , and privation for the Japanese soldiers . [S3] Meanwhile , the Allied supply system grappled with the problems of terrain and climate , particularly inclement weather and rough monsoonal seas that hampered and occasionally prevented delivery of supplies by sea . [S4] Australian and Papuan troops advanced along the coast of the Huon Peninsula , using infantry , tanks , and air strikes against the Japanese positions , which were generally sited at creek crossings in the jungle . [S5] The advancing infantry kept strictly within range of the supporting artillery , which was liberally employed in the early stages of the operation . [S6] Using tactics that exploited the firepower of Australian artillery and armour , the Australian and Papuan troops inflicted heavy and disproportionate casualties on the Japanese as they advanced , ultimately linking up with the American forces at Saidor . [S7] Hundreds of Japanese soldiers were killed ; thousands more died from disease , malnutrition , exhaustion and suicide . [S8] The Allies failed to seize the opportunity to completely destroy the Japanese forces . [S9] During the advance , Australian troops captured Japanese cryptographic materials . [S10] This had an important effect on the subsequent course of the war against Japan in the South West Pacific , as it permitted codebreakers in Australia and the United States to read Japanese Army messages on a much greater scale than previously .

Document: [S0] Big Muddy Creek is a tributary of the Missouri River , approximately 191   mi ( 307   km ) long , in the Canadian province of Saskatchewan and the U.S. state of Montana . [S1] It flows through the Big Muddy Badlands . [S2] It rises in southern Saskatchewan at Willow Bunch Lake , on the plains north of the international border and approximately 20   mi ( 32   km ) northwest of Big Beaver . [S3] It flows southeast through the Big Muddy Badlands and through Big Muddy Lake , then south into Sheridan County , Montana , past Redstone , then east , past Plentywood , then south , forming the eastern border of Fort Peck Indian Reservation . [S4] It joins the Missouri west of Culbertson . [S5] It was explored in 1805 by the Lewis and Clark Expedition , who called it Martha 's River in their journals and noticed on their return voyage in 1806 that it had changed its mouth on the Missouri . [S6] Along with the Milk River and the Poplar River , it is one of three waterways in Canada that drain into the Gulf of Mexico .

Document: [S0] The six Cello Suites , BWV 1007 - 1012 , are suites for unaccompanied cello by Johann Sebastian Bach . [S1] They are some of the most frequently performed and recognizable solo compositions ever written for cello . [S2] Bach most likely composed them during the period 1717 – 23 , when he served as Kapellmeister in Köthen . [S3] The title given on the cover of the Anna Magdalena Bach manuscript was Suites à Violoncello Solo senza Basso ( Suites for cello solo without bass ) . [S4] These suites for unaccompanied cello are remarkable in that they achieve the effect of implied three- to four - voice contrapuntal and polyphonic music in a single musical line . [S5] As usual in a Baroque musical suite , after the prelude which begins each suite , all the other movements are based around baroque dance types ; the cello suites are structured in six movements each : prelude , allemande , courante , sarabande , two minuets or two bourrées or two gavottes , and a final gigue . [S6] The Bach cello suites are considered to be among the most profound of all classical music works . [S7] Wilfrid Mellers described them in 1980 as " Monophonic music wherein a man has created a dance of God . " [S8] Due to the works ' technical demands , étude - like nature , and difficulty in interpretation because of the non - annotated nature of the surviving copies , the cello suites were little known and rarely publicly performed until they were revived and recorded by Pablo Casals in the early 20th century . [S9] They have since been performed and recorded by many renowned cellists and have been transcribed for numerous other instruments ; they are considered some of Bach 's greatest musical achievements .

[S7] Hohenwald is also the home of the Elephant Sanctuary , the largest natural - habitat sanctuary for elephants in the United States . [S8] Hohenwald is one of only a few Mid - American towns that have met the Transition Towns criteria . [S9] The Buffalo Valley addiction extended care community is located there providing treatment and long - term housing for recovering persons . [S10] The Lewis County Courthouse and Hohenwald Rail Depot are listed on the National Register of Historic Places .

Document: [S0] Escuela Latinoamericana de Medicina ( ELAM ) , formerly Escuela Latinoamericana de Ciencias Médicas ( in Spanish ; in English : Latin American School of Medicine ( LASM ) , formerly Latin American School of Medical Sciences ) , is a major international medical school in Cuba and a prominent part of the Cuban healthcare system . [S1] Established in 1999 and operated by the Cuban government , ELAM has been described as possibly being the largest medical school in the world by enrollment with approximately 19,550 students from 110 countries reported as enrolled in 2013 . [S2] All those enrolled are international students from outside Cuba and mainly come from Latin America and the Caribbean as well as Africa and Asia . [S3] The school accepts students from the United States — 91 were reportedly enrolled as of January 2007 . [S4] Tuition , accommodation and board are free , and a small stipend is provided for students . [S5] An ELAM sister school operated by the Venezuela government and sited in Guri , Bolívar , Venezuela was scheduled to open in October 2006 . [S6] However , it was only half built as of November 2008 . [S7] The school is named Escuela Latinoamericana de Medicina A.P. [S8] Réverénd after French physician Alejandro Próspero Réverénd .

Document: [S0] Latourell Falls is a waterfall along the Columbia River Gorge in the U.S. state of Oregon , within Guy W. Talbot State Park . [S1] The Historic Columbia River Highway passes nearby , and at certain locations the Lower falls are visible from the road . [S2] Near the base of the falls , a parking lot and path were erected to assist visitors to the site . [S3] Visitors must hike along the loop trail to see the upper falls . [S4] Latourell is unique among the best - known Columbia Gorge waterfalls , in the way that it drops straight down from an overhanging basalt cliff . [S5] Most of those falls ( even the famous Multnomah Falls ) tumble to some degree . [S6] Latourell Falls is an excellent example of columnar basalt formations .

Document: [S0] " Portugal no coração " ( " Portugal in my heart " ) was the Portuguese entry in the Eurovision Song Contest 1977 , performed in Portuguese by Os Amigos . [S1] The song is a ballad in praise of Portugal itself . [S2] The song is about freedom , brotherhood and hope . [S3] Many of the verses of the lyrics are acclamations of the end of the Estado Novo dictatorship that lasted for 48 years , and the end of the wars that the Portuguese people had been forced to fight on the African colonies by that regime . [S4] It 's also a love hymn from Portuguese people to their ex - colonies people , whom they had fought . [S5] The song was performed eighth on the night , following Luxembourg 's Anne - Marie B. with " Frère Jacques " and preceding the United Kingdom 's Lynsey de Paul & Mike Moran with " Rock Bottom " . [S6] At the close of voting , it had received 18 points , placing 14th in a field of 18 . [S7] It was succeeded as Portuguese representative at the 1978 Contest by Gemini with " Dai li dou " .

[S1] Sadée started painting at the age of 20 . [S2] He studied in The Hague both at the Academy and in the studio of J E J van den Berg ( 1802 – 1861 ) . [S3] In 1866 with his fellow student Julius van de Sande Bakhuyzen . [S4] Sadée travelled to Düsseldorf where he studied for some months . [S5] He began painting biblical scenes and history paintings and later he focused on daily life . [S6] In Scheveningen he came into contact with the fisherman 's life . [S7] Here he was fascinated with the beach and the dunes , which were a source of inspiration for him . [S8] Typical of Sadée are the bright colors . [S9] Sadée travelled widely , he painted in the Pas de Calais and travelled in France , Germany , Belgium and Italy . [S10] Sadée exhibited in Amsterdam , Rotterdam and The Hague in the years 1853 – 1903 , and was elected to the Arte et Amicitiae in Amsterdam . [S11] He taught at the Academy in The Hague and numbered Hendrikus M. Horrix ( 1845 – 1923 ) amongst his pupils .

[S6] Fyllingen played in the First Division from 1994 to 1996 and in the Second Division from 1997 till 2009 . [S7] The last two seasons of its existence , the club played in the Third Division . Document: [S0] Across the Black Waters is an English novel by the Indian writer Mulk Raj Anand first published in 1939 . [S1] It describes the experience of Lalu , a sepoy in the Indian Army fighting on behalf of Britain against the Germans in France during World War I. [S2] He is portrayed by the author as an innocent peasant whose poor family was evicted from their land and who only vaguely understands what the war is about . [S3] The book has been described as Anand 's best work since the Untouchable . [S4] In Lalu 's tragedy lied the tragedy of the Indian village and Anand dramatizes a poignant truth : to disposses any one of land is to deny him an identity .— Basavaraj Naikar [S5] The book is part of a trilogy ( along with The Village and The Sword and the Sickle ) that chronicles the life of Lalu as he struggles to rise from the bottom of Indian society . [S6] In the background is India 's fight for independence . [S7] This book is the only Indian English novel that is set in World War I and portrays the experiences of Lalu , who only wants to reclaim the piece of land his family lost as a reward for serving . [S8] But when he returns from war , he finds his family destroyed and his parents dead . [S9] The novel 's larger themes are that of war and death Lalu encounters Western culture .

Document: [S0] William Harrison Frist Sr . ( born February 22 , 1952 ) is an American physician , businessman , and politician . [S1] He began his career as a heart and lung transplant surgeon . [S2] He later served two terms as a Republican United States Senator representing Tennessee . [S3] He was the Senate Majority Leader from 2003 to 2007 . [S4] Born in Nashville , Tennessee , Frist studied health care policy at Princeton University and interned for Congressman Joe L. Evins . [S5] Rather than going directly into politics , Frist earned a Doctor of Medicine degree from Harvard Medical School , becoming a surgeon at Massachusetts General Hospital and several other hospitals . [S6] In 1994 , he defeated incumbent Democratic Senator Jim Sasser , and pledged to only serve two terms . [S7] After serving as Chairman of the National Republican Senatorial Committee , Frist succeeded Tom Daschle as the Senate Majority Leader . [S8] Frist helped pass several parts of President George W. Bush 's domestic agenda , including the Jobs and Growth Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003 and PEPFAR . [S9] He was also a strong proponent of the Partial - Birth Abortion Ban Act and a prominent advocate of tort reform . [S10] Frist left the Senate in 2007 , honoring his commitment to serve no more than two terms . [S11] Since leaving Congress , he has remained active in public life and has taught at several universities .

[S5] According to Omar Noman , " as the famous story goes , " Nazar sustained the injury jumping out from the house window of the film actress Noor Jehan when her film producer husband Shaukat Hussain Rizvi returned home unexpectedly and surprised them . [S6] There were persistent rumors in the local newspapers , at the time , of a romantic affair going on between Noor Jehan and Nazar Mohammad . [S7] His son Mudassar Nazar also represented Pakistan in cricket for many years in the 1970s and 1980s .

Document: [S0] The Financial District of Lower Manhattan , also known as FiDi , is a neighborhood located on the southern tip of Manhattan Island , where the City of New York itself originated in 1624 . [S1] The district comprises the offices and headquarters of many of the city 's major financial institutions , including the New York Stock Exchange and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York . [S2] Anchored on Wall Street in the Financial District , New York City has been called both the most financially powerful city and the leading financial center of the world , and the New York Stock Exchange is the world 's largest stock exchange by total market capitalization . [S3] Several other major exchanges have or had headquarters in the Financial District , including the New York Mercantile Exchange , NASDAQ , the New York Board of Trade , and the former American Stock Exchange . [S4] The neighborhood roughly overlaps with the boundaries of the New Amsterdam settlement in the late 17th century . [S5] The population of the Financial District has grown to an estimated 61,000 residents as of 2018 , up from 43,000 as of 2014 , which in turn was nearly double the 23,000 recorded at the 2000 Census .

Document: [S0] The following list is composed of items , techniques and processes that were invented by or discovered by people from Spain . [S1] Spain was an important center of knowledge during the medieval era . [S2] While most of western and southern Europe suffered from the collapse of the Roman Empire , although declining , some regions of the former empire , Hispania ( the Iberian Peninsula ) , southern Italy , and the remainder of the Eastern Roman Empire or Byzantine Empire , did not to suffer from the full impact of the so - called Dark Ages when education collapsed with the collapse of the empire and most knowledge was lost . [S3] The Islamic conquests of places such as Egypt , which was a major part of the Byzantine Empire , and other places which were centers of knowledge in earlier times , gave the Muslims access to knowledge from many cultures which they translated into Arabic and recorded in books for the use of their own educated elites , who flourished in this period , and took with them to the Hispania after it fell under Muslim control . [S4] Much of this knowledge was later translated by Christian and Jewish scholars in the Christian kingdoms of the Reconquista from Arabic into Latin , and from there it spread through Europe .

Document: [S0] Michael John " Mike " Padden ( born November 13 , 1946 ) is a lawyer and politician from Spokane Valley , Washington . [S1] He is a member of the Washington State Senate representing Washington 's 4th Legislative District . [S2] Padden is well known as a " faithless elector " , a Presidential Elector who casts his vote for someone other than for whom he has pledged to vote . [S3] In the 1976 U.S. presidential election , Gerald Ford , the Republican candidate and incumbent , had lost the race to Democrat , and former Georgia Governor Jimmy Carter . [S4] Rather than vote as pledged , for President Ford , Padden instead cast his vote for Ronald Reagan , who had lost the Republican nomination to Ford earlier that year . [S5] He entered the Washington House of Representatives in January 1981 and served there until 1995 when he was appointed to serve as a district court judge in the Spokane County District Court . [S6] On June 13 , 2006 , Padden announced he would not run for re - election as judge . [S7] In 2007 , evidence surfaced that Padden used his influence as a judge to help direct more than $ 7.5 million in fees and interest payments to a former employer . [S8] At Padden ’s request , the state Commission on Judicial Conduct has issued a statement confirming that it examined complaints about Padden ’s 1999 selection of a former client as the official collection agency for District Court but found nothing to support an ethics violation . [S9] The commission typically acknowledges complaints only if it imposes discipline or sanctions . [S10] The agency , however , refused to disclose how it arrived at its conclusion or what the initial examination entailed . [S11] Padden was elected to the Washington Senate in November 2011 .

Document: [S0] John Richardson Thurman ( October 6 , 1814 – July 24 , 1854 ) was a U.S. Representative from New York . [S1] Born in New York City , Thurman graduated from Columbia University in 1835 . [S2] He moved to Chestertown , Warren County and engaged in agricultural pursuits . [S3] He was also involved in several businesses , including serving as a Director of the Sacket 's Harbor and Saratoga Railroad . [S4] He also speculated in land , as evidenced by the fact that his widow and children sold some of their holdings to the Delaware and Hudson Railroad during its construction . [S5] He held several local offices , including Associate Judge of the Warren County Court . [S6] Thurman was elected as a Whig to the Thirty - first Congress ( March 4 , 1849 – March 3 , 1851 ) . [S7] He declined to be a candidate for renomination in 1850 . [S8] After leaving Congress Thurman returned to managing his farm and other interests . [S9] He died at his home near Friends Lake in Chestertown on July 24 , 1854 . [S10] He was interred in the family cemetery . [S11] He was reinterred in Oakwood Cemetery , Troy , New York .

Document: [S0] Carl Gösta Björn Joachim von der Esch ( 11 January 1930 – 10 March 2010 ) was a Swedish Christian democratic politician , member of the Riksdag 1998 – 2006 . [S1] Esch had a farming business and did a Ph.D. in business administration at Uppsala University in 1972 . [S2] Before joining the Christian Democrats , he had previously represented Moderate Party in the Riksdag 1991 – 1994 , replacing Per Westerberg during his time as a minister . [S3] At the time of the Swedish 1994 referendum on membership in the European Union , Esch clashed with the Moderate Party as he campaigned on the " no " side . [S4] When he subsequently formed a list of EU critics that ran in the 1995 European Parliament election in Sweden , he was expelled from the party . [S5] This list was unsuccessful in the election , and von der Esch returned to parliamentary politics in 1998 as a Christian Democrat . [S6] In the 2003 referendum on joining the Economic and Monetary Union and the euro , he again campaigned on the " no " side . [S7] He later joined the June List , became its vice chairman in 2008 , and was on second place on the June List ballot in the 2009 European Parliament election in which the party lost its representation in the European Parliament .

Document: [S0] The first official National Football League ( NFL ) playoff game was the 1933 NFL Championship Game between the Chicago Bears and New York Giants . [S1] A " playoff " game was played in 1932 between the Chicago Bears and Portsmouth Spartans to break a regular season tie , but is recorded in the team record books as a regular season game . [S2] Since then there have been a total over 525 NFL playoff games including games from the AFL , but not the AAFC . [S3] The following list shows career postseason records for each starting quarterback in the NFL playoffs . [S4] Wins or losses are credited to the quarterback who started the game for each team , even if he was injured or failed to complete the game . [S5] While many players have won playoff games for two teams , only two have won a championship for different franchises . [S6] Tobin Rote was quarterback for the NFL champion 1957 Lions and the AFL champion 1963 Chargers . [S7] Peyton Manning was the quarterback for 2006 Colts and the 2015 Broncos . [S8] Note : from 1933–1949 some offenses did not employ a quarterback in the modern sense of the position . [S9] Listed below are the " primary passers " for those games , the players that passed the ball most in those games . [S10] They may not have actually started the game at quarterback . [S11] This format allows Hall of Fame quarterbacks like Sid Luckman and Sammy Baugh to maintain credit for their team 's playoff records since they were obviously the top passer for their team . [S12] The players involved in such games are marked with an asterisk ( * ) .

Document: [S0] The Orange Grove affair was a political scandal in Australia concerning the dealings of the New South Wales state Australian Labor Party government with multinational corporation The Westfield Group . [S1] It resulted from a court decision in 2004 to force the closure of the Orange Grove shopping centre after a zoning dispute , with the loss of approximately 200 jobs . [S2] Westfield , who owned a nearby shopping centre , had challenged the legitimacy of the Orange Grove centre , which was operating on land not zoned for this purpose . [S3] When the courts ruled in Westfield 's favor , Liverpool City Council sought State Government approval for a retrospective rezoning , to validate its earlier decision to approve the shopping centre . [S4] The State Government declined to intervene , despite a planning report suggesting that course of action , and the retail component of the Orange Grove centre was forced to close . [S5] The bulky goods component of the centre remained open , as the centre was legally zoned for bulky goods sales . [S6] However , the state Opposition subsequently unearthed information about a meeting between Premier Bob Carr 's chief of staff and a prominent Westfield employee , sparking allegations that interference from Westfield had played a role in the government 's decision not to intervene . [S7] As a result , a parliamentary inquiry was commissioned , and the Independent Commission Against Corruption announced an investigation . [S8] The investigation concluded in 2005 , with no findings of corruption against any person . [S9] However , the Commission recommended that the NSW Government strengthen guidelines for public servants dealing with corruption allegations by lobbyists . [S10] Unlike Nick Greiner in 1992 and Barry O'Farrell in 2014 , the Orange Grove affair marked the only time that a sitting Premier in Bob   Carr had survived appearing before ICAC although Carr did retire mere months after the conclusion of ICAC 's investigation of the Orange Grove affair .
