Document: [S0] The Prinzenpalais is a palace , now used as an art museum , in the city of Oldenburg , Lower Saxony , Germany . [S1] The museum houses the modern art collection of the State Museum for Art and Cultural History . [S2] The building dates from 1826 and is in the classical style . [S3] It was the residence of the Russian princes Alexander and Peter . [S4] Subsequently Grand Duke Niklaus Friedrich Peter occupied the building . [S5] In 2003 , it became part of the State Museum of Art and Cultural History ( with the Augusteum and Schloss Oldenburg ) and is an art gallery . [S6] The museum concentrates on German artists , ranging from neoclassicism and Romanticism in the mid-19th century to the post-1945 era . [S7] The Prinzenpalais building is near the northeast corner of the Schlossgarten Oldenburg . [S8] The Augusteum , Elisabeth - Anna - Palais , and Schloss Oldenburg are all close to the museum .

Document: [S0] Olympic Gold is the official video game of the XXV Olympic Summer Games , hosted by Barcelona , Spain in 1992 . [S1] It was released for the Sega consoles , Sega Genesis and Sega Master System , and Sega 's handheld , Sega Game Gear . [S2] Developed internally by Tiertex Design Studios , the game was sponsored by Coca - Cola and the game featured both the company logo on a zeppelin above the scoreboard , as well as the company jingle . [S3] The game uses button mashing as the main part of gameplay , but in three events it is n't used ( archery , diving ) or is slow - paced ( swimming ) . [S4] Each computer athlete has a fictional name and nationality ( choosing from UK , France , Germany , Italy , Spain , United States , Japan and the Unified Team , everyone with its own anthem snippet ) and actual strengths and weaknesses : J. Balen , for instance , is a frequent 100 m and 110 m hurdles record breaker but only an average hammer thrower . [S5] Also , each computer - controlled player seems better in a particular event depending on his country : Germans usually take the top spots in archery , Italians on swimming , Russians on pole vault , Americans on sprinting and so on .

[S3] Cleveland ( Northeast ) and Cincinnati ( Southwest ) are on opposite corners of Ohio , and essentially split Ohio . [S4] Both teams were founded by head coach Paul Brown , the namesake of the Browns franchise , who created the Bengals franchise in the American Football League ( AFL ) after he was fired from the Browns . [S5] The colors of each team are similar . [S6] The Bengals and Browns first played in 1970 . [S7] Previously , the Bengals were a part of the AFL . [S8] After the AFL – NFL merger the Bengals and Browns were placed in the AFC Central Division , where they remained until the Browns suspended operations after their relocation to Baltimore and a subsequent new Browns expansion team being awarded to Cleveland . [S9] The expansion Browns were also placed in the AFC Central . [S10] Both teams moved to the newly - formed AFC North division in 2002 as part of the NFL 's realignment . [S11] The Bengals lead the overall series , 50–39 . [S12] The two teams have never met in the postseason .

Document: [S0] The Togoland Campaign ( 9–26 August 1914 ) was a French and British invasion of the German colony of Togoland in west Africa , which began the West African Campaign of the First World War . [S1] German colonial forces withdrew from the capital Lomé and the coastal province , to fight delaying actions on the route north to Kamina , where the Kamina Funkstation ( wireless transmitter ) linked the government in Berlin to Togoland , the Atlantic and South America . [S2] The main British and French force from the neighbouring colonies of Gold Coast and Dahomey , advanced from the coast up the road and railway , as smaller forces converged on Kamina from the north . [S3] The German defenders were able to delay the invaders for several days at the battles of Agbeluvhoe and Chra but surrendered the colony on 26 August 1914 . [S4] In 1916 , Togoland was partitioned by the victors and in July 1922 , British Togoland and French Togoland were established as League of Nations mandates .

[S1] Many families of free people of color were formed in the colonial and early Federal period ; some attained education and property ; in addition there were many mixed - race slaves , who as freedmen after the war were part of the complex society of the South . [S2] Two of his books were adapted as silent films in 1926 and 1927 by the African - American director and producer Oscar Micheaux . [S3] Following the Civil Rights Movement during the 20th century , interest in the works of Chesnutt were revived . [S4] Several of his books were published in new editions , and he received formal recognition . [S5] A commemorative stamp was printed in 2008 . [S6] During the early 20th century in Cleveland , Chesnutt established what became a highly successful court reporting business , which provided his main income . [S7] He became active in the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People , writing articles supporting education as well as legal challenges to discriminatory laws .

Document: [S0] The Cranford Protocol or Cranford Agreement was an oral undertaking given in 1952 by the British Government to the residents of Cranford in London regarding the usage of the runways at London Heathrow Airport to reduce the impact of aircraft noise on local residents . [S1] Under normal operations the agreement prohibited take - off on the northern runway towards the east ( over London ) because of the proximity of Cranford to the east end of this runway ; however this runway could be used in exceptional cases , for example when the southern runway was not available for departures or when departure delays are excessive . [S2] Although no formal written agreement exists , the Government acknowledges that an oral undertaking was given by a senior government official at a meeting of the Cranford Residents ' and District Amenities Association on 31 July 1952 . [S3] The protocol is included in the Heathrow Manual of Air Traffic Services and the airport 's noise abatement notification , and thus is a part of the airport 's operating rules . [S4] On 15 January 2009 , the Labour Government announced that it was ending the Cranford Agreement as part of the controversial expansion of London Heathrow Airport . [S5] Although in May 2010 the Coalition Government cancelled the Heathrow expansion plans , in September 2010 it reaffirmed the decision to end the Cranford Agreement . [S6] This decision was welcomed by the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead , to the west . [S7] To the east , the London Borough of Hounslow called for mitigation or compensation to be offered by BAA to those affected by ending the Cranford Agreement . [S8] In May 2013 Heathrow Airport Holdings ( who own and operate the airport ) submitted planning permission to the London Borough of Hillingdon to build new access taxiways , which would allow the implementation of full runway alternation on easterly operations . [S9] This permission was rejected in March 2014 ; Heathrow Airport appealed with a planning enquiry in June 2015 . [S10] On 2 February 2017 the Planning Inspectorate recommended that the appeal be allowed and planning permission granted . [S11] The decision has not yet been implemented as the airport is considering the Governments airspace management proposals for London and their own plans for expansion .

[S3] Then , when the wall was destroyed , the street was widened and became a boulevard . [S4] Piet Mondrian 's little known story De groote boulevards ( Les Grands Boulevards ) , written in 1920 in Paris at the instance of Theo van Doesburg , was inspired by the Boulevard des Capucines .

Document: [S0] Pangaea Ultima ( also called Pangaea Proxima , Neopangaea , and Pangaea II ) is a possible future supercontinent configuration . [S1] Consistent with the supercontinent cycle , Pangaea Ultima could occur within the next 250 million years . [S2] This potential configuration , hypothesized by Christopher Scotese , earned its name from its similarity to the previous Pangaea supercontinent . [S3] Scotese later renamed Pangaea Ultima ( Last Pangaea ) to Pangaea Proxima ( Next Pangaea ) to alleviate confusion about the name Pangaea Ultima which could imply that it would be the last supercontinent . [S4] The concept was based on examination of past cycles of formation and breakup of supercontinents , not on current understanding of the mechanisms of tectonic change , which are too imprecise to project that far into the future . [S5] " It 's all pretty much fantasy to start with , " Scotese has said . [S6] " But it 's a fun exercise to think about what might happen . [S7] And you can only do it if you have a really clear idea of why things happen in the first place . " [S8] Supercontinents describe the merger of all , or nearly all , of the Earth 's landmass into a single contiguous continent . [S9] In the Pangaea Ultima scenario , subduction at the western Atlantic , east of the Americas , leads to the subduction of the Atlantic mid - ocean ridge followed by subduction destroying the Atlantic and Indian basin , causing the Atlantic and Indian Oceans to close , bringing the Americas back together with Africa and Europe . [S10] As with most supercontinents , the interior of Pangaea Proxima would probably become a semi - arid desert prone to extreme temperatures .

Document: [S0] Alice Bunker Stockham ( November 8 , 1833 in Cardington , Ohio – December 3 , 1912 in Alhambra , California ) was an obstetrician and gynecologist from Chicago and the fifth woman to become a doctor in the United States . [S1] She promoted gender equality , dress reform , birth control , and male and female sexual fulfillment for successful marriages . [S2] A well - traveled and well - read person who counted among her friends Leo Tolstoy and Havelock Ellis , she also visited Sweden and from her trips to schools there she brought back the idea of teaching children domestic crafts , thus single - handedly establishing shop and home economics classes in the United States . [S3] Stockham lectured against the use of corsets by women , made public endorsements of the healthiness of masturbation for both men and women ( still controversial when echoed by U.S. [S4] Surgeon General Joycelyn Elders more than 100 years later ) , advocated complete abstinence from alcohol and tobacco , and believed in women 's rights . [S5] Stockham was very concerned with the economic plight of divorced women with children and prostitutes who wanted to get off the street . [S6] She felt that these women had no marketable skills and would be unable to support themselves , so she had copies of her book Tokology , a layperson 's guide to gynecology and midwifery , privately printed and gave them to " unfortunate women " to sell door - to - door in Chicago . [S7] Each copy came with a bound - in certificate signed by Stockham and entitling the bearer to a free gynecological exam . [S8] In 1905 , a then 72-year old Stockham and her publisher were convicted of circulating improper literature under the Comstock laws .

[S6] In his preface Wittig writes : [S7] I 've often been asked how you go about it to invent a game . [S8] I want to add one answer now . [S9] Is perhaps the best answer possible to show the many different ways of designing a game . [S10] The answer is also a challenge : Invent rules of your own to my dice pyramid . [S11] The first edition of the game was a small version of the dice pyramid , without any rules . [S12] Over time , players contributed their own rules to a collection .

Document: [S0] The Trail Smelter dispute was a trans - boundary pollution case involving the federal governments of both Canada and the United States , which eventually contributed to establishing the Harm principle in the environmental law of transboundary pollution . [S1] The smelter in Trail , British Columbia was historically operated by the Consolidated Mining and Smelting Company ( COMINCO ) until COMINCO merged with Teck in 2001 , and has processed lead and zinc since 1896 . [S2] Smoke from the smelter caused damage to forests and crops in the surrounding area and also across the Canada – US border in Washington . [S3] The smoke from the smelter distressed residents , resulting in complaints to COMINCO and demands for compensation . [S4] The dispute between the smelter operators and affected landowners could not be resolved , resulting in the case being sent to an arbitration tribunal . [S5] Negotiation and resulting litigation and arbitration was settled in 1941 .

[S5] The Rohn Glacier and Regal Glacier head east and southeast to join the Nizina Glacier , while the Root Glacier flows south to join the Kennicott Glacier just above the town of McCarthy . [S6] Each of those large glaciers exceeds in width , but largest of all on Regal Mountain is a massive unnamed glacier , over across , which flows northwest just over to join the mighty Nabesna .

Document: [S0] … Nothing Like the Sun is the second solo studio album by English singer - songwriter Sting . [S1] The album was originally released on 13 October 1987 on A&M ; ( worldwide ) . [S2] The album explores the genres of pop rock , soft rock , jazz , reggae , world , acoustic rock , dance - rock , and funk rock . [S3] The songs were recorded during March – August in 1987 in sessions that took place at Air Studios , in Montserrat , assisted by record producers Hugh Padgham , Bryan Loren , and Neil Dorfsman . [S4] It features a number of high - profile guest guitarists , including former Police member Andy Summers , Eric Clapton , Mark Knopfler , and Hiram Bullock , and is generally regarded as the culmination of the smoother , more adult - oriented sound of Sting 's early work . [S5] On release , the album was received favorably by the majority of music critics and in 1989 , the album was ranked # 90 on Rolling Stone magazine 's list of the " 100 Best Albums of the Eighties " . [S6] " We 'll Be Together " , " Be Still My Beating Heart " , " Englishman in New York " , " Fragile " , and " They Dance Alone " were all released as singles . [S7] It won Best British Album at the 1988 Brit Awards . [S8] In 1989 the album received three Grammy nominations including Album of the Year while the album 's second single ( " Be Still My Beating Heart " ) was nominated for Song of the Year and Best Male Pop Vocal Performance .

[S3] It rises in Edison ( near Interstate 287 and County Route 501 ) and flows through the Dismal Swamp . [S4] It then flows through South Plainfield and the Cedar Brook joins it southwest of Spring Lake . [S5] It continues through Piscataway into New Market Pond , through Middlesex where it flows into the Green Brook at the northwest corner of Mountain View Park . [S6] It gives its name to the borough of Bound Brook , New Jersey .

[S1] The character arrived in early 2002 as the teenage sister of Geoff ( Andrew Laing ) and his adoptive sister , Anne Greenlaw ( Emmeline Hawthorne ) . [S2] The characters tomboy ways saw her favour rugby over fashion and as a result , she was isolated from her peers . [S3] The character participated in a hugely high profile storyline in 2003 where she fell for much older man , Dom ( Shane Cortese ) , who went on to murder Geoff . [S4] The character departed in 2004 following the death of both her siblings and intimidation from Dom . [S5] Delphi was highly praised throughout her two - year run , with Hutchison receiving numerous award nominations and winning the " Rising Star " prize in the 2004 TV Guide Best on the Box People 's Choice Awards . [S6] The characters romance with Dom and struggle with anorexia has seen the character 's storylines become iconic since her departure .

[S2] The treaty was signed in Edinburgh by Robert the Bruce , King of Scotland , on 17 March 1328 , and was ratified by the English Parliament at Northampton on 1 May. [S3] The document was written in French , and is held by the National Archives of Scotland in Edinburgh . [S4] The terms of the treaty stipulated that , in exchange for £ 100,000 sterling , the English Crown would recognise : [S5] The Kingdom of Scotland as fully independent ; [S6] Robert the Bruce , and his heirs and successors , as the rightful rulers of Scotland . [S7] The border between Scotland and England as that recognised under the reign of Alexander III ( 1249 - 1286 ) .

Document: [S0] Le Ventre de Paris ( 1873 ) is the third novel in Émile Zola 's twenty - volume series Les Rougon - Macquart . [S1] It is set in and around Les Halles , the enormous , busy central market of 19th - century Paris . [S2] Les Halles , rebuilt in cast iron and glass during the Second Empire was a landmark of modernity in the city , the wholesale and retail center of a thriving food industry . [S3] Le Ventre de Paris ( translated into English under many variant titles but literally meaning The Belly of Paris ) is Zola 's first novel entirely on the working class . [S4] The protagonist is Florent , an escaped political prisoner mistakenly arrested after the French coup of 1851 . [S5] He returns to his step - brother Quenu , a charcutier and his wife Lisa Quenu ( formerly Macquart ) , with whom he finds refuge . [S6] They get him a job in the market as a fish inspector . [S7] After getting mixed up in an ineffectual socialist plot against the Empire , Florent is arrested and deported again . [S8] Although Zola had yet to hone his mastery of working - class speech and idioms displayed to such good effect in L'Assommoir , the novel conveys a powerful atmosphere of life in the great market halls and of working class suffering . [S9] There are a number of vivid descriptive passages , the most famous of which , his description of the olfactory sensations experienced upon entering a cheese shop , has become known as the " Cheese Symphony " due to its ingenious orchestral metaphors . [S10] Throughout the book , the painter Claude Lantier , a relative of the Macquarts and later the protagonist of L'Œuvre ( 1886 ) - shows up to provide a semi - authorial commentary , playing the role of chorus . [S11] It is an interesting and often powerful work , though not usually considered as being on a par with the novelist 's achievements later in the Rougon - Macquart cycle .

Document: [S0] Tigran Vartanovich Petrosian ( June 17 , 1929   – August 13 , 1984 ) was a Soviet Armenian Grandmaster , and World Chess Champion from 1963 to 1969 . [S1] He was nicknamed " Iron Tigran " due to his almost impenetrable defensive playing style , which emphasised safety above all else . [S2] Petrosian was a Candidate for the World Championship on eight occasions ( 1953 , 1956 , 1959 , 1962 , 1971 , 1974 , 1977 and 1980 ) . [S3] He won the World Championship in 1963 ( against Mikhail Botvinnik ) , successfully defended it in 1966—against Boris Spassky — and lost it to Spassky in 1969 . [S4] Thus he was the defending World Champion or a World Championship Candidate in ten consecutive three - year cycles . [S5] He won the Soviet Championship four times ( 1959 , 1961 , 1969 , and 1975 ) . [S6] Petrosian is widely known for popularizing chess in Armenia .

Document: [S0] Oliver & Company is a 1988 American animated musical comedy - drama film produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation and released on November 18 , 1988 , by Walt Disney Pictures . [S1] The 27th Disney animated feature film , the film is based on the classic Charles Dickens novel Oliver Twist , which has been adapted many other times for the screen . [S2] In the film , Oliver is a homeless kitten who joins a gang of dogs to survive in the streets . [S3] Among other changes , the setting of the film was relocated from 19th century London to modern - day New York City , Fagin 's gang is made up of dogs ( one of which is Dodger ) , and Sykes is a loan shark . [S4] Following the release of The Black Cauldron , Michael Eisner and Jeffrey Katzenberg held a pitch meeting with the animation staff , in which story artist Pete Young pitched the idea to adapt Oliver Twist with dogs . [S5] The pitch was quickly approved , and the film quickly went into production under the working title Oliver and the Dodger . [S6] Released on the same day as The Land Before Time , Oliver & Company was a box office success , but it received mixed reviews from film critics . [S7] The film was re - released in the United States , Canada , and the United Kingdom on March 29 , 1996 . [S8] It was then released on home video later that same year , and again in 2002 and 2009 on DVD . [S9] The film was released on Blu - ray Disc in 2013 , commemorating its 25th Anniversary .

[S2] She has exhibited widely throughout the United States and internationally , including a solo exhibition at Yancey Richardson Gallery in 2015 , about which art critic Roberta Smith wrote , “ … obsessive delights await in this strange and beautiful show … ” [S3] She lives and works in Gloucester , Massachusetts and Brooklyn , New York .

Document: [S0] Nexus   Q is a discontinued digital media player developed by Google . [S1] Unveiled at the Google I / O developers ' conference on June 2012 , the device was expected to be released to the public in the United States shortly thereafter for US$ 300 . [S2] The Nexus Q was designed to leverage Google 's online media offerings , such as Google Play Music , Google Play Movies & TV , and YouTube , to provide a " shared " experience . [S3] Users could stream content from the supported services to a connected television , or speakers connected to an integrated amplifier , using their Android device and the services ' respective apps as a remote control for queueing content and controlling playback . [S4] The Nexus   Q received mixed reviews from critics following its unveiling . [S5] While its unique spherical design was praised , the Nexus Q was criticized for its lack of functionality in comparison to similar devices such as Apple TV , including a lack of third - party content services , no support for streaming content directly from other devices using the DLNA standard , as well as other software issues that affected the usability of the device . [S6] The unclear market positioning of the Nexus Q was also criticized , as it carried a significantly higher price than competing media players with wider capabilities ; The New York Times technology columnist David Pogue described the device as being ' wildly overbuilt ' for its limited functions . [S7] The Nexus   Q was given away at no cost to attendees of Google I / O 27 - 29 June 2012 , but the product 's consumer launch was postponed in July 2012 , purportedly to collect additional feedback . [S8] Those who had pre - ordered the Nexus   Q following its unveiling received the device at no cost . [S9] The Nexus   Q was quietly shelved in January 2013 , and support for the device in the Google Play apps was phased out beginning in May 2013 . [S10] Some of the Nexus   Q 's concepts were repurposed for a more - successful device known as Chromecast , which similarly allows users to wirelessly queue content for playback using functions found in supported apps , but is designed as a smaller HDMI dongle with support for third - party services .

Document: [S0] Zamoyski Palace ( Polish : Pałac Zamoyskich ) - a historical building , located by Nowy Świat Street in Warsaw , Poland . [S1] From 1667 the owner of the plot was Jan Wielopolski . [S2] Between 1744 and 1745 the inheritors of Wielopolski 's possessions reconstructed the palace following designs of architect Piotr Hiż . [S3] The owner of the building soon became Franciszek Ksawery Branicki , who commissioned renovation work under Szymon Bogumił Zug . [S4] In 1802 the palace was bought by Anna Jadwiga Sapieżyna . [S5] Stanisław Staszic would live in the palace until he died there in 1826 . [S6] In 1839 the palace became property of Andrzej Artur Zamoyski . [S7] The new owner commissioned reconstruction works headed by architect Enrico Marconi which gave the building 's present nature . [S8] During the January Uprising of 1863 , the house was plundered by the Imperial Army . [S9] During the interwar period the building housed the Ministry of Interior and Administration ( Poland ) . [S10] The palace was damaged during the Warsaw Uprising and rebuilt between 1948 and 1950 without modifying its architectural design . Document: [S0] The Waterloo Moraine is a landform and sediment body that was created as a moraine in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo , in Ontario , Canada . [S1] It covers a large portion of the cities of Waterloo and Kitchener and the township of Wilmot , and some parts of the townships of Wellesley and North Dumfries . [S2] About 90 % of the water supply of the Regional Municipality of Waterloo is derived from groundwater of the Waterloo Moraine aquifer system . [S3] During late 1989 and early 1990 , groundwater contamination in Elmira forced the Region to shut down some well fields . [S4] As a result , new land use management guidelines and water protection measures have been enacted . [S5] The Waterloo Moraine is the largest of fourteen moraines in the Region , spanning approximately 400 square kilometres . [S6] It is an interlobate moraine , consisting primarily of sand and gravel . [S7] It contains large aquifers , which discharge into the Grand River and its tributaries and maintain a base water flow rate into that system .

[S2] The Shire extends across the Peel Inlet and the Swan Coastal Plain into the Darling Scarp , including about of State forests . Document: [S0] The Virgin and Child with St Anne and St John the Baptist , sometimes called The Burlington House Cartoon , is a drawing by Leonardo da Vinci . [S1] The drawing is in charcoal and black and white chalk , on eight sheets of paper glued together . [S2] Because of its large size and format the drawing is presumed to be a cartoon for a painting . [S3] No painting by Leonardo exists that is based directly on this cartoon . [S4] The drawing depicts the Virgin Mary seated on the knees of her mother , St Anne , while holding the Child Jesus as Jesus ' young cousin , St. John the Baptist , stands to the right . [S5] It currently hangs in the National Gallery in London . [S6] It was either executed in around 1499 – 1500 , at the end of the artist 's first Milanese period , or around 1506 – 1508 , when he was shuttling between Florence and Milan . [S7] The majority of scholars prefer the latter date , although the National Gallery and others prefer the former .

[S5] He was assigned to his subsequent ministerial post after he supposedly did not comply . [S6] He was axed in the cabinet reshuffle of March 2017 , allegedly without being given reasons . [S7] His position was taken by a known Zuma ally , the then Free State economic development MEC Mosebenzi Zwane . [S8] In the same reshuffle , finance minister Pravin Gordhan and his deputy , Mcebisi Jonas , were also replaced .

Document: [S0] The is one of the active palaces of the Emperor of Japan and has the longest history as the capital of Japan . [S1] The Emperor declared Meiji Restoration and Charter Oath at this place in 1868 . [S2] The following year , the Emperor moved into Edo castle , currently Tokyo Imperial Palace , but he ordered the preservation of the Kyoto Imperial Palace in 1877 , which is still used as an active palace .. Today , the grounds are open to the public , and the Imperial Household Agency hosts public tours of the buildings several times a day . [S3] The Kyoto Imperial Palace is the latest of the imperial palaces built at or near its site in the northeastern part of the old capital of Heian - kyō after the abandonment of the larger original that was located to the west of the current palace during the Heian Period . [S4] The Palace lost much of its function at the time of the Meiji Restoration , when the capital functions were moved to Tokyo in 1869 . [S5] However , the Taishō and Shōwa Emperors still had their enthronement ceremonies at the palace .

Document: [S0] Anna Margaret Frances Caselberg ( née Woollaston , 1942 – 2004 ) was a New Zealand painter . [S1] Born in 1942 , Caselberg was the daughter of Edith Winifred Woollaston ( née Alexander ) and the painter Toss Woollaston . [S2] She studied at the University of Auckland , spending a year living with Colin McCahon and his family during this time . [S3] In 1960 she married poet John Caselberg , who—12 years older than her — was friends with both her father and McCahon . [S4] Anna Caselberg worked in oils and watercolour , mostly painting landscapes , and her style is said to show the influences of Colin McCahon and her father . [S5] Her work is held in public collections in New Zealand , including those of the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa and the Dunedin Public Art Gallery . [S6] Caselberg died of cancer in late 2004 , six months after her husband 's death , also from cancer . [S7] The Caselberg Trust , a charitable trust supporting artists , is named in honour of John and Anna Caselberg .

" [S1] Currently , 22 Partnerships exist " with former Soviet , Yugoslav and Warsaw Pact countries in the EUCOM Area of Responsibility . " [S2] Becoming independent on the dissolution of the Soviet Union on December 26 , 1991 , these countries shortly requested the advice and assistance of the United States in creating new self - defense forces . [S3] They had been acquired by the Soviet Union from the European Theatre of World War II . [S4] The requests began among the Baltic states , notably Latvia , which had approached NATO . [S5] It sent a delegation from five member countries , including the U.S. , which chose the National Guard Bureau as most appropriate spokesman , considering that Latvia could not afford a standing army . [S6] EUCOM thus became the first of the six geographic Combatant Commands that make up the [S7] " global SPP , " and the NG , which is divided into state - sized contingents , became the host of each state - sized new national force , typically , but not necessarily , one - to - one , totally voluntarily . [S6] The album entered the UK Albums Chart at number three , making it less successful than Disc - Overy . [S7] It was beaten to a top two chart position by The Marshall Mathers LP 2 and James Arthur . [S8] The album was certified gold by the British Phonographic Industry on 21 February 2014 .

Document: [S0] The Velislaus Bible or Velislav 's Bible ( Latin Velislai biblia picta ) is an illuminated manuscript of 1325 – 1349 , which is in effect a picture - book of the Bible , as the text is limited to brief titles or descriptions of the 747 pictures from the Old Testament and the New Testament , from the writings about the Antichrist and from the legends of the saints , especially St Wenceslas . [S1] It is therefore an example of a Biblia pauperum , though not in the typical form , having many more images . [S2] Most of the illuminations are only in ink , though some colour is used . [S3] The manuscript is of 188 folios on parchment , with a page size of 307 x 245 mm . [S4] It is in the Czech National Library ( Národní knihovna Ceské republiky ) , Prague . [S5] The codex was created by several artists probably for Velislav the Canon ( d. 1367 ) , the notary of John I of Bohemia and his son Charles IV , Holy Roman Emperor , who were both based in Prague .

Document: [S0] Kondor was the fifth of six Type 23 torpedo boats built for the German Navy ( initially called the Reichsmarine and then renamed as the Kriegsmarine in 1935 ) . [S1] The boat made multiple non - intervention patrols during the Spanish Civil War in the late 1930s . [S2] During World War II , she played a minor role in the attack on Oslo , the capital of Norway , during the Norwegian Campaign of 1940 . [S3] Kondor spent the next several months escorting minelayers as they laid minefields and damaged heavy ships back to Germany before she was transferred to France around September . [S4] She started laying minefields herself that month and continued to do so for the rest of the war . [S5] The boat returned to France in 1942 and helped to escort blockade runners , commerce raiders and submarines through the English Channel and the Bay of Biscay . [S6] Damaged by a mine shortly before the Allied Invasion of Normandy in June 1944 , Kondor was under repair on the day of the landings . [S7] Recognizing that she could not be repaired quickly , the boat was decommissioned later that month and was then further damaged by British bombers so that she was declared a constructive total loss .

Document: [S0] Suikoden Tactics , originally released in Japan as , is a tactical role - playing video game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 console as part of their Suikoden series . [S1] Initially released in Japan and North America in late 2005 , the game was later made available in Europe and the PAL region in early 2006 . [S2] It is the first strategy - based installment of the series , using tactical , grid - based combat instead of the turn - based battles employed by previous games in the series . [S3] The game 's music was composed by series veteran Norikazu Miura and features the opening theme " Another World " performed by Japanese vocalist yoshiko . [S4] The game 's fantasy story is told in two parts , taking place both before and after the events of Suikoden IV released one year earlier , and features appearances by characters from the title . [S5] Players assume the role of Kyril , a young man investigating the power of mysterious weapons called " Rune Cannons , " which hold strange powers of transformation .

[S8] He was an unsuccessful candidate for reelection in 1920 to the Sixty - seventh Congress . [S9] Maher entered the real estate business in Brooklyn , moved to Keansburg , New Jersey , and continued in real estate . [S10] He was elected mayor of Keansburg in 1926 . [S11] Maher died in Keansburg on July 31 , 1946 . [S12] He is buried in St. Joseph 's Cemetery , Keyport , New Jersey .

Document: [S0] Dom Afonso ( 23 February 1845   – 11 June 1847 ) was the Prince Imperial and heir apparent to the throne of the Empire of Brazil . [S1] Born in Rio de Janeiro , he was the eldest child of Emperor Dom Pedro   II and Dona Teresa Cristina of the Two Sicilies , and thus a member of the Brazilian branch of the House of Braganza . [S2] Afonso died from epilepsy at the age of two , devastating the emperor . [S3] The following year , Pedro and Teresa Cristina had another son , Pedro Afonso , but he too died in infancy . [S4] After the loss of his second son , doubts grew in Pedro   II 's mind that the imperial system could be viable . [S5] He still had an heir in his daughter Isabel , but he was unconvinced that a female would prove to be a suitable successor . [S6] He showed less concern about the effects his policies had on the monarchy , provided his daughter Isabel with no training for her role as potential empress , and failed to cultivate her acceptance within the country 's political class . [S7] Pedro   II 's lack of interest in protecting the imperial system ultimately led to its downfall .

Document: [S0] The United States Marine Band is the premier band of the United States Marine Corps . [S1] Established by act of Congress on July 11 , 1798 , it is the oldest of the United States military bands and the oldest professional musical organization in the United States . [S2] Today , the Marine Band also includes the Marine Chamber Orchestra and Marine Chamber Ensembles . [S3] The Marine Band is entirely separate from its sister military band , the United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps ( " The Commandant 's Own " ) and the 10 active duty Marine Corps field bands . [S4] The Marine Band has been uniquely known as " The President 's Own " since 1801 due to the historic connection to the President of the United States . [S5] The relationship between the Marine Band and the White House began on New Year 's Day 1801 , when President John Adams invited the band to perform at the Executive Mansion . [S6] Later that year , Thomas Jefferson initiated the tradition of Marine Band performances by requesting that it perform at his inauguration . [S7] The Marine Band has played at every United States presidential inauguration since . [S8] President Thomas Jefferson gave the title " The President 's Own " in 1801 . [S9] Today , the Marine Band performs in approximately 500 events every year including state funerals , state arrival ceremonies , state dinners , parades , concerts , and other social events . [S10] The Marine Band also travels across the country each October and November during its fall concert tour , a tradition that began in 1891 under its most famous director , composer John Philip Sousa .

[S6] The album reached the top spot in the music charts of Mexico , selling 550,000 copies there and gaining a diamond and gold certification by AMPROFON . [S7] As part of the album 's promotion , four singles were released . [S8] The first three , " Rebelde " , " Solo Quédate En Silencio " , and " Sálvame " , became number one hits in Mexico . Document: [S0] Greatest Hits is A - Teens ' last album . [S1] It is a compilation including their biggest worldwide hits , such as " Mamma Mia " , " Upside Down " , " Halfway Around the World " , " Floorfiller " , and many others . [S2] Every track included on the album ( except for the new tracks ) reached the Top 20 in at least one country . [S3] The album was planned to be released in early 2004 , but due to problems with Stockholm Records / Universal Music , A - Teens released the album on May 5 , 2004 . [S4] For the release of this album , the A - Teens called all their fans through their website asking for pictures , and they included the pictures on the booklet of the album . [S5] The tracks " The Final Cut " and " With or Without You " were written by the members of the band , giving messages of " goodbye " and " thanks " to their fans . [S6] This album was not released worldwide . [S7] Instead , it was released in selected territories where Universal thought it would do well . [S8] These included Mexico , Argentina , Germany , and some other European and Asian countries . [S9] The album went on to sell over 10,000 copies in Argentina and another 3,000 in Brazil ; overall , the album sold relatively well in Latin America and some parts of Europe , where " I Promised Myself " was a huge hit . [S10] An American edition was planned for this album , and it was going to be released through Interscope Records in late 2004 . [S11] However , the A - Teens were already finishing their Greatest Hits Tour in Sweden and they did n't want to promote in America as Dhani was about to release his first solo single there , so Interscope cancelled the release .

Document: [S0] Camp Caves was a US Army training camp north of the city of Rockhampton , Queensland , Australia . [S1] Built during World War Two , the camp was in use from September 1943 until early in 1944 . [S2] It was one of a number of US training camps in the area including Camp Nerimbera , Camp Thompson ’s Point , Camp Keppel Sands , Camp Yeppoon and Camp Wallaroo . [S3] Camp Caves was the camp for the 24th Infantry Division , which was also called the Hawaiian Division . [S4] It was called Camp Caves after the small town , The Caves , which was close to the campsite . [S5] The site was along the side of the Bruce Highway . [S6] It included medical services , warehouses , ammunition dumps , landing strips , and a small arms firing range . [S7] Work on building the camp began in November 1942 but was soon stopped . [S8] It started again in July 1943 . [S9] The camp was no longer used after March 1944 .

Document: [S0] Francesco De Masi ( 11 January 1930 – 6 November 2005 ) was an Italian conductor and film score composer . [S1] He studied composition at the San Pietro a Maiella Conservatory in Naples , under the guidance of Achille Longo , his uncle . [S2] De Masi became interested in film music when Longo was asked to compose a soundtrack for a film , and he asked De Masi to be his assistant . [S3] De Masi 's filmography includes scores for over 200 films and TV series , ranging from spaghetti westerns and sword and sandal epics to gialli and horror films , such as Lucio Fulci 's Lo squartatore di New York ( The New York Ripper ) . [S4] De Masi also scored several action films , such as Enzo G. Castellari 's Quel maledetto treno blindato ( The Inglorious Bastards ) , but he is best remembered for his work on spaghetti westerns . [S5] Unlike most other composers , De Masi started writing western scores slightly earlier than the genre 's most influential musician , Ennio Morricone . [S6] As De Masi 's music was less influenced by Morricone , his style had a distinctive sound . [S7] Many of his songs were performed by the low - voiced member of the I Cantori Moderni choir , Ettore " Raoul " Lovecchio . [S8] De Masi was also very interested in classical music . [S9] He taught at the Santa Cecilia Conservatory , also conducting the conservatory 's orchestra . [S10] In an interview , De Masi listed Palestrina , Karlheinz Stockhausen , Ravel and Shostakovich as his main classical influences . [S11] De Masi died of cancer at the age of 75 .

Document: [S0] Extreme Makeover : Home Edition ( EM : HE ; sometimes informally referred to as Extreme Home Makeover ) is an American reality television series providing home improvements for less fortunate families and community schools . [S1] The show was hosted by former model , carpenter and veteran television personality Ty Pennington . [S2] Each episode features a family that has faced some sort of recent or ongoing hardship such as a natural disaster or a family member with a life - threatening illness , in need of new hope . [S3] The show 's producers coordinate with a local construction contractor , which then coordinates with various companies in the building trades for a makeover of the family 's home . [S4] This includes interior , exterior and landscaping , performed in seven days while the family is on vacation ( paid for by the show 's producers ) and documented in the episode . [S5] If the house is beyond repair , they replace it entirely . [S6] The show 's producers and crew film set and perform the makeover but do not pay for it . [S7] The materials and labor are donated . [S8] Many skilled and unskilled volunteers assist in the rapid construction of the house . [S9] EM : HE is considered a spin - off of Extreme Makeover , an earlier series providing personal makeovers ( often including plastic surgery ) to selected individuals . [S10] Unusual for a spin - off , Home Edition outlasted its mother show by several seasons . [S11] This show displays extreme changes to help recreate someone 's space . [S12] However , the format differs considerably ; in the original Extreme Makeover , for instance , participants were not necessarily chosen based on any recent hardship , whereas the family 's backstory is an important component of Home Edition . [S13] EM : HE also has similarities to other home renovation series such as Trading Spaces , on which Pennington was previously a key personality . [S14] The series was produced by Endemol USA ( the people behind Big Brother , Fear Factor , Deal or No Deal , Wipeout , and other reality shows ) in association with Disney - ABC Television Group 's Greengrass Television . [S15] The Executive Producers were Brady Connell and George Verschoor . [S16] The program originally aired on Sunday evenings but was moved to Friday nights as of October 21 , 2011 . [S17] Upon the airing of its final episode in series form , and for the 2012 special holiday run , it remained ABC 's last series to air solely in standard definition and never converted to a high definition or widescreen presentation . [S18] On December 15 , 2011 , ABC announced that Extreme Makeover : Home Edition would end its run on January 13 , 2012 . [S19] It will , however , continue to air as a special on the network .

Document: [S0] The Committee against the Finnish White Terror ( ) was an organization in Sweden , formed at the end of the Finnish Civil War . [S1] The formation of the Committee was preceded by a call from the Social Democratic Left Party published in Politiken in February 1918 to mobilize protests around the country to counter the official Swedish government position on the Finnish question . [S2] The Committee sought to unite the Swedish labour movement for a common position against what they termed the ” White Terror ” in Finland . [S3] The Committee raised funds for humanitarian aid to the victims of the repression . [S4] The Committee also opposed denials of political asylum for Finnish refugees . [S5] Sven Linderot was one of the three members of the Committee . [S6] The Committee managed to gather 21,851.53 kronor , 14,518.73 for Finnish refugees in Sweden and 6,920 kronor for affected in Finland . [S7] The Committee published 100,000 leaflets titled ' Truth about Finland ' , and more than 100 public meetings were organized .

Document: [S0] Olympic National Park is an American national park located in the State of Washington , on the Olympic Peninsula . [S1] The park has four regions : the Pacific coastline , alpine areas , the west side temperate rainforest and the forests of the drier east side . [S2] Within the park there are three distinct ecosystems which are subalpine forest and wildflower meadow , temperate forest , and the rugged Pacific coast . [S3] President Theodore Roosevelt originally designated Mount Olympus National Monument on 2 March 1909 . [S4] The monument was redesignated as a national park by Congress and President Franklin Roosevelt on June 29 , 1938 . [S5] In 1976 , Olympic National Park was designated by UNESCO as an International Biosphere Reserve , and in 1981 as a World Heritage Site . [S6] In 1988 , Congress designated 95 percent of the park as the Olympic Wilderness .

[S1] The song was composed by Paulo Pereira and Pedro Marques . [S2] The song was the winner of the Festival da Canção contest on 28 February 2009 , receiving maximum votes from the juries , and coming second in the public televote . [S3] The song competed for Portugal in the first semi - final of Eurovision 2009 , where Flor - de - Lis performed 16th in the running order , following Finland 's Waldo 's People with " Lose Control " and preceding Malta 's Chiara with " What If We " . [S4] " Todas as ruas do amor " qualified for the final round , where they performed 6th in the running order preceding Iceland 's Yohanna with " Is It True ? " . [S5] The song finished 15th with 57 points .

Document: [S0] The Private Life of Helen of Troy is a 1927 American silent film about Helen of Troy based on the 1925 novel of the same name by John Erskine , and adapted to screen by Gerald Duffy . [S1] The film was directed by Alexander Korda and starred María Corda as Helen , Lewis Stone as Menelaus , and Ricardo Cortez as Paris . [S2] Coming at the end of the silent film era , it was nominated for an Academy Award in 1929 , the year of the Awards ' inception , in the category of Best Title Writing . [S3] Duffy died on 25 June 1928 , and was the first person to be posthumously nominated for an Academy Award . [S4] That same year , the first " talkie " , The Jazz Singer , received an honorary award for introducing sound to film , and the category for which The Private Life of Helen of Troy was nominated was dropped by the second Academy Awards . [S5] Two sections from the beginning and end , running about 27–30 minutes in total , are reportedly all that survive of The Private Life of Helen of Troy ; they are preserved by the British Film Institute .

Document: [S0] Schizoanalysis (; schizo- from Greek σχίζειν skhizein , meaning " to split " ) is a concept created by philosopher Gilles Deleuze and psychoanalyst Félix Guattari and first expounded in their book Anti - Oedipus ( 1972 ) . [S1] Its formulation was continued in their follow - up work , A Thousand Plateaus . [S2] Schizoanalysis acquires many different definitions during the course of its development in their collaborative work and individually in the work of Guattari . [S3] In Chaosmosis , Guattari explains that " rather than moving in the direction of reductionist modifications which simplify the complex " , schizoanalysis " will work towards its complexification , its processual enrichment , towards the consistency of its virtual lines of bifurcation and differentiation , in short towards its ontological heterogeneity " .

Document: [S0] The Contact Group is the name for an informal grouping of great powers that have a significant interest in policy developments in the Balkans . [S1] The Contact Group is composed of United States , United Kingdom , France , Germany , Italy , and Russia . [S2] It was first created in response to the war and the crisis in Bosnia in the early 1990s . [S3] The Contact Group includes four of the five Permanent Members of the UN Security Council and the countries that contribute the most in troops and assistance to peacebuilding efforts in the Balkans . [S4] Representatives of the EU Council , EU Presidency , European Commission and NATO generally attend Contact Group meetings . [S5] The Contact Group has taken a major interest in the UN - led process to determine the future political status of Kosovo and Metohija ( i.e. , whether it should be independent or remain a part of Serbia ) . [S6] The Contact Group meets regularly with UN Special Envoy Martti Ahtisaari , who has been charged with running the future status process . [S7] The Contact Group has no Secretariat or permanent staff — it is simply an informal grouping of countries that meets regularly at various levels to coordinate international policy initiatives in southeast Europe . [S8] Contact Group public statements , often negotiated to painstaking detail within the group , are considered to be significant statements of the international community 's policy and intentions in the region . [S9] The Contact Group usually meets at the level of Balkans director ( i.e. , the highest - ranking diplomats in charge of the Balkans in each foreign ministry ) . [S10] Occasionally , however , the Contact Group meets at the level of Political Director or even Foreign Minister .

Document: [S0] They Shoot Horses , Do n't They ? [S1] is a 1969 American depression - era melodrama film based on Horace McCoy 's 1935 novel of the same name and directed by Sydney Pollack . [S2] The screenplay was written by James Poe and Robert E. Thompson . [S3] The film focuses on a disparate group of characters desperate to win a Depression - era dance marathon and the opportunistic emcee ( MC ) who urges them on to victory . [S4] It stars Jane Fonda , Michael Sarrazin , Susannah York , Red Buttons , Bruce Dern , Bonnie Bedelia and Gig Young . [S5] The film premiered at the 23rd Cannes Film Festival and was released theatrically in the United States on December 10 , 1969 . [S6] The film upon release was a critical and commercial success , grossing $ 12.6 million on a budget of $ 4.86 million , becoming the sixteenth highest grossing film of 1969 . [S7] Critics praised its direction , screenplay , depiction of the depression - era and performances , most notably of Fonda 's which marked a significant turning point in her career . [S8] The film received nine nominations at the 42nd Academy Awards including Best Director , Best Actress ( for Fonda ) , Best Supporting Actress ( for York ) , Best Adapted Screenplay and winning Best Supporting Actor ( for Young ) . [S9] It is the most nominated film in the history of the aforementioned awards without a Best Picture nomination .

Document: [S0] The Merchants of Bollywood is an Australian musical written and directed by Toby Gough . [S1] The show is about the history of the Bollywood film industry , and it is named after Hiralalji Merchant and his grand daughter Vaibhavi Merchant , two notable Indian choreographers . [S2] The set and lighting design was by Liz Berry and the costumes were designed by Falguni Thakore and Bipin . [S3] The musical has been described as " an Indian version of the Billy Elliot story " and is choreographed by Vaibhavi Merchant . [S4] It was the first ever Bollywood production to tour straight from Film City in Mumbai . [S5] When the show reached Australia in February 2008 , there had been 400 performances seen by 500,000 patrons . [S6] The show toured the United Kingdom , various parts of Europe , the United States , Australia , Canada and various parts of Asia .

Document: [S0] Vineeth Sreenivasan ( born 1 October 1985 ) is an Indian playback singer , actor , director , producer and screenwriter , who works in Malayalam cinema . [S1] Vineeth is son of the actor and screenwriter Sreenivasan . [S2] He made his film debut in 2003 as a playback singer with the song " Kasavinte Thattamittu " from Kilichundan Mampazham , and later also worked in music albums . [S3] Vineeth made his acting debut in Cycle ( 2008 ) , and since then he has acted in numerous films . [S4] His directorial debut was in 2010 with Malarvaadi Arts Club , also written by him . [S6] Vineeth 's second directorial venture Thattathin Marayathu ( 2012 ) became one of the highest grossing films of 2012 . [S7] His first script for another director was Oru Vadakkan Selfie ( 2015 ) , directed by G. Pajith . [S8] His most recent directorial was Jacobinte Swargarajyam ( 2016 ) . [S9] Vineeth established the film production house named Habit of Life and produced its debut film Aanandam in 2017 .

Document: [S0] " How to Save a Life " is the twenty - first episode of the eleventh season of the American television medical drama Grey 's Anatomy , and is the 241st episode overall . [S1] It aired on April 23 , 2015 on ABC in the United States . [S2] The episode was written by showrunner Shonda Rhimes and directed by Rob Hardy , making it the first episode Rhimes has written since the season eight finale " Flight " . [S3] The installment marked the death and final appearance of the series’ male lead character , Derek Shepherd ( Patrick Dempsey ) , who had starred on the series since its inception . [S4] In this episode , Shepherd is involved in an accident while attempting to help the victims of a car accident . [S5] He is later pronounced brain dead , in part due to the surgeons not providing him with a timely CT scan . [S6] Only six regular cast membersEllen Pompeo , Patrick Dempsey , Chandra Wilson , Kevin McKidd , Sarah Drew and Caterina Scorsone appear in the episode . [S7] " How to Save a Life " also marks the first appearance of Dr. Penelope Blake ( Samantha Sloyan ) . [S8] The episode 's original broadcast was watched by 9.55 million viewers and registered the show as the week 's highest - rated drama and third - highest rated scripted series in the 18–49 demographic . [S9] It received mixed reviews from the critics who were divided on the show 's handling of Shepherd 's death . [S10] However , they were largely laudatory of Pompeo , with critic Rick Porter deeming it the best performance of her career .

[S2] His first LP , Feeler , reached number 1 a few months after its mid-2003 release , and his follow - up record , See The Sun , had a similar level of success , with all of the singles receiving widespread airplay . [S3] His third studio album , Summer At Eureka , was released in May 2008 . [S4] To date , Murray has sold over 1 million records . [S5] Some of the greatest influences on his career are Nick Drake , Neil Young and Bob Dylan . [S6] In November 2013 , Murray toured Canada with Paul Langlois and Rob Baker of The Tragically Hip .

Document: [S0] Berge Meere und Giganten ( Mountains Seas and Giants ) is a 1924 science fiction novel by German author Alfred Döblin . [S1] Stylistically and structurally experimental , the novel follows the development of human society into the 27th century and depicts global - scale conflicts between future polities , technologies , and natural forces , culminating in the catastrophic harvesting of Iceland 's volcanic energy in order to melt Greenland 's ice cap . [S2] Among critics , Berge Meere und Giganten has the reputation of being a difficult and polarizing novel , and has not received nearly as much attention as Döblin 's following novel , Berlin Alexanderplatz ( 1929 ) . [S3] Inspired by the mundane sight of pebbles rolling in the Baltic Sea surf in the summer of 1921 , Döblin began writing Berge Meere und Giganten that fall , conducting extensive research into various natural and human sciences in the process . [S4] Although he had originally conceived of it as a hymn to the city and technology , over the course of writing the novel it evolved into a tribute to the power of nature . [S5] He finished the manuscript in the summer of 1923 , and it was published by Fischer Verlag the following year .

Document: [S0] Howard the Duck is a 1986 American science fiction comedy film directed by Willard Huyck and starring Lea Thompson , Jeffrey Jones , and Tim Robbins . [S1] Produced by Gloria Katz and written by Huyck and Katz , with George Lucas as executive producer , the screenplay was originally intended to be an animated film based on the Marvel comic book of the same name , but the film adaptation became live - action because of a contractual obligation . [S2] Although several TV adaptations of Marvel characters had aired during the preceding 21 years , this was the first theatrically released feature film , coming after the serial Captain America . [S3] Lucas proposed adapting the comic book following the production of American Graffiti ( 1973 ) . [S4] Following multiple production difficulties and mixed response to test screenings , Howard the Duck was released in theaters on August 1 , 1986 . [S5] Upon its release , the film was a critical and commercial failure , and in the years since , was considered one of the worst films of all time . [S6] It was nominated for seven Razzie Awards , and made about $ 15 million domestically compared to its $ 30 million budget . [S7] Despite the criticism , it has gained a cult following among fans of the comic - book series .

Document: [S0] X - Men Legends II : Rise of Apocalypse is an action role - playing game developed primarily by Raven Software and published by Activision . [S1] It is the follow up to 2004 's X - Men Legends . [S2] It was released in September 2005 for the GameCube , Microsoft Windows , N - Gage , PlayStation 2 , PlayStation Portable and Xbox . [S3] It is set after the events of X - Men Legends and features the mutant supervillain Apocalypse as the primary antagonist . [S4] The developers intended the game to have a greater sense of scale than its predecessor , and writers created a story where the villains known as the Brotherhood of Mutants would need to ally themselves with the heroic X - Men to defeat a greater threat . [S5] High quality cinematics were created by Blur Studio . [S6] Online multiplayer was also added . [S7] The game was well received by gaming critics on all platforms . [S8] Critics felt that the inclusion of online play , additional mutant powers , and a larger cast made the game an improvement over its predecessor . [S9] Some reviewers were critical of the game 's voice acting and felt that the gameplay was repetitive . [S10] It sold enough copies to be added to the budget line known as PlayStation 2 's Greatest Hits .

[S1] The film was the third to be produced by Kardar 's United Players Pictures ( Playart Phototone ) , following Husn Ka Daku ( 1929 ) and Sarfarosh ( 1930 ) . [S5] For actor Gul Hamid , Safdar Jung was the first of seven silent films he worked in . [S6] A police officer in the British Police by profession , he was chosen by Kardar as a leading man due to Hamid 's " over - all persona " . [S7] Like the rest of the films produced earlier , Safdar Jung was also released at The Deepak cinema in Bhati Gate area of Lahore .

[S4] Released in March 1969 by Polydor Records in the UK and Atco Records in the US , it was the group 's fourth album released internationally , their sixth overall , and their only double album of original music . [S5] Odessa would be the final album for the band 's original incarnation , and this was the last album to include guitarist Vince Melouney . [S6] The album contains " First of May " , " Lamplight " , " Marley Purt Drive " and " Melody Fair " . [S7] The album was reissued as a single - disc in 1976 when interest was revived in the Bee Gees career , since then the album has gained increasing critical acclaim ; it was reissued again in 2009 as a deluxe 3 disc set , and is included in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die .

[S3] The single became one of Bowie 's best selling in his career , with total estimated sales over 400,000 in the UK alone . [S5] In 2008 , a rerecorded version by Aled Jones and Terry Wogan — under the name " Bandaged "— was released by Warner Home Music as part of BBC Children in Need Appeal 2008 . Document: [S0] In Christianity , worship is reverent honor and homage paid to God . [S1] In the New Testament various words are used for worship . [S2] The word proskuneo " to worship " means to bow down to God or kings . [S3] Throughout most of Christianity 's history , corporate Christian worship has been liturgical , characterized by prayers and hymns , with texts rooted in , or closely related to , the Scripture , particularly the Psalter ; this form of sacramental and ceremonial worship is still practiced by the Roman Catholic , Eastern Orthodox , and Anglican churches , as well as some Protestant denominations such as Lutheranism and Methodism . [S4] In Evangelicalism , worship is viewed like an act of adoration of God , with a more informal conception . [S5] The term liturgy is derived from the Greek leitourgia meaning " public service " and is formed by two words : " laos " ( people ) and " ergon " ( work ) , literally " work of the people " . [S6] Responsorial prayers are a series of petitions read or sung by a leader with responses made by the congregation . [S7] Set times for prayer during the day were established ( based substantially on Jewish models ) , and a festal cycle throughout the Church year governed the celebration of feasts and holy days pertaining to the events in the life of Jesus , the lives of the saints , and aspects of the Godhead . [S8] A great deal of emphasis was placed on the forms of worship , as they were seen in terms of the Latin phrase lex orandi , lex credendi ( " the rule of prayer is the rule of belief")—that is , the specifics of one 's worship express , teach , and govern the doctrinal beliefs of the community . [S9] According to this view , alterations in the patterns and content of worship would necessarily reflect a change in the faith itself . [S10] Each time a heresy arose in the Church , it was typically accompanied by a shift in worship for the heretical group . [S11] Orthodoxy in faith also meant orthodoxy in worship , and vice versa . [S12] Thus , unity in Christian worship was understood to be a fulfillment of Jesus ' words that the time was at hand when true worshipers would worship " in spirit and in truth " ( John 4:23 ) .

[S1] He was born on his grandfather 's rice farm near Eunice . [S2] His grandfather was a fiddler , who occasionally played with the legendary Dennis McGee , who was once a tenant farmer on his grandfather 's property . [S3] Marc Savoy began playing traditional music when he was 12 years old . [S4] Savoy holds a degree in chemical engineering but his primary income is derived from his accordion - making business , based at his Savoy Music Center in Eunice , Louisiana . [S5] His wife is the singer and guitarist Ann Savoy , whom he met in 1975 and married in 1977 . [S6] He has performed with Robert Bertrand , Dennis McGee , Rodney Balfa , Sady Courville , Dewey Balfa , D. L. Menard , and Michael Doucet , the latter of whom he plays with in the Savoy - Doucet Band . [S7] He also plays in the Savoy Family Band with his wife Ann and their sons Joel and Wilson . [S8] He hosts regular jam sessions and mini - festivals at the Savoy Music Center . [S9] Savoy is a recipient of a 1992 National Heritage Fellowship awarded by the National Endowment for the Arts , which is the United States government 's highest honor in the folk and traditional arts .

Document: [S0] Central Massachusetts is the geographically central region of Massachusetts . [S1] Though definitions vary , most include all of Worcester County and the northwest corner of Middlesex County . [S2] Worcester , the largest city in the area and the seat of Worcester County , is often considered the cultural capital of the region . [S3] Other populous cities include Fitchburg , Gardner , Leominster , and arguably Marlborough . [S4] The region is mostly wooded and hilly upland , in contrast to the Atlantic coastal plain to the east and the Connecticut River valley lowland to the west . [S5] The geographic center of Massachusetts is located in the town of Rutland . [S6] The term is seldom used in eastern Massachusetts , where Worcester and points west are instead regarded as part of Western Mass.

Document: [S0] The Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh is the chief executive of the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh . [S1] In accordance with the Constitution of India , the governor is a state 's de jure head , but de facto executive authority rests with the chief minister . [S2] Following elections to the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly , the state 's governor usually invites the party ( or coalition ) with a majority of seats to form the government . [S3] The governor appoints the chief minister , whose council of ministers are collectively responsible to the assembly . [S4] Given the confidence of the assembly , the chief minister 's term is for five years and is subject to no term limits . [S5] Following Madhya Pradesh 's reorganisation on 1 November 1956 , 17 people have served as its chief minister . [S6] Eleven of these belonged to the Indian National Congress , including the inaugural officeholder Ravishankar Shukla . [S7] The first non - Congress chief minister was Govind Narayan Singh who defected from the party and lead a Samyukta Vidhayak Dal government from 1967 to 1969 . [S8] Digvijaya Singh of the Congress became the first officeholder to serve two full five - year terms . [S9] He was succeeded by Uma Bharti of the Bharatiya Janata Party , Madhya Pradesh 's only woman chief minister . [S10] Her party - mate Shivraj Singh Chouhan is the current incumbent and the state 's longest - serving chief minister , having held office since November 2005 .

Document: [S0] In gridiron football , a triple - threat man is a player who excels at all three of the skills of running , passing , and kicking . [S1] In modern usage , such a player would be referred to as a utility player . [S2] Triple - threat men were the norm in the early days of football , as substitution rules were stringent . [S3] Thus , in addition to the need for passing , running , and kicking skills , they were also required to play defense . [S4] As injury awareness grew and substitution rules loosened , teams shifted to kicking specialists , which made the triple - threat man obsolete . [S5] One of the last triple - threat men in professional football was George Blanda , a quarterback and kicker who last played for the Oakland Raiders of the National Football League in 1975 . [S6] Danny White , a quarterback and punter , retired in 1989 . [S7] Since then , non - specialists have placekicked only extremely infrequently in the NFL . [S8] One instance occurred when Doug Flutie — also adept at both running and passing as a " scrambling " quarterback — drop kicked an extra point in 2006 during the last play of his career . [S9] Danny White of the Dallas Cowboys was the last non - specialist to kick on a regular basis , as he served as the team 's starting quarterback and punter from 1980 until 1984 , after several years as backup to Roger Staubach . [S10] There are , however , still dual - threat quarterbacks and wildcat halfbacks , who can both run and pass . [S11] A quarterback who played wide receiver in high school or college may sparingly catch passes or be converted into a wide receiver who occasionally passes . [S12] For over forty years the NFL single - season scoring record was held by a triple - threat man , Green Bay Packers Hall of Famer Paul Hornung . [S13] Hornung set a record of 176 points in 1960 by scoring fifteen touchdowns , kicking forty - one extra points , and also kicking fifteen field goals .

Document: [S0] Waldshut station ( ) is a railway station in the city of Waldshut - Tiengen in the German state of Baden - Württemberg . [S1] It was opened on 30 October 1856 . [S2] The station lies on the Upper Rhine Railway , which connects Basel and Singen along the northern and , mostly , German bank of the Rhine . [S3] It is the junction point for the Turgi – Koblenz – Waldshut line , which crosses the Rhine from Switzerland on the Waldshut to Koblenz railway bridge just to the south of the station . [S4] The Upper Rhine Railway is not electrified and most services are operated by diesel locomotives or railcars . [S5] The line from Switzerland is electrified using the Swiss standard of 15kV and 16.7Hz from an overhead line . [S6] Only one terminal platform in the station is electrified , and this is used by all trains from Switzerland .

[S8] Even historically Boltenhagen has been a popular holiday resort in Eastern Germany as being the second town , where bathing wagons have been placed . Document: [S0] The Winnebago War , also known as the Winnebago Uprising , was a brief conflict that took place in 1827 in the Upper Mississippi River region of the United States , primarily in what is now the state of Wisconsin . [S1] Not quite a war , the hostilities were limited to a few attacks on American civilians by a portion of the Winnebago ( or Ho - Chunk ) Native American tribe . [S2] The Ho - Chunks were reacting to a wave of lead miners trespassing on their lands , and to false rumors that the United States had sent two Ho - Chunk prisoners to a rival tribe for execution . [S3] Most Native Americans in the region decided against joining the uprising , and so the conflict ended after U.S. officials responded with a show of military force . [S4] Ho - Chunk chiefs surrendered eight men who had participated in the violence , including Red Bird , who American officials believed to be the ringleader . [S5] Red Bird died in prison in 1828 while awaiting trial ; two other men convicted of murder were pardoned by President John Quincy Adams and released . [S6] As a result of the war , the Ho - Chunk tribe was compelled to cede the lead mining region to the United States . [S7] The Americans also increased their military presence on the frontier , building Fort Winnebago and reoccupying two other abandoned forts . [S8] The conflict convinced some officials that Americans and Indians could not live peaceably together , and that the Natives should be compelled to move westward , a policy known as Indian removal . [S9] The Winnebago War preceded the larger Black Hawk War of 1832 , which involved many of the same people and concerned similar issues .

Document: [S0] The Georgian Foundation for Strategic and International Studies ( GFSIS ; ) is one of Georgia 's leading independent think tanks , based in Tbilisi . [S1] It was founded in 1998 with the declared aim of " helping improve public policy decision - making in Georgia through research and analysis , training of policymakers and policy analysts , and public education about the strategic issues , both domestic and international , facing Georgia and the Caucasus " . [S2] It has played an important role in training new public servants and scholars . [S3] The GFSIS includes several leading experts on politics , social studies , and economics in Georgia , many of them with experience as former high - ranking government officials and strong ties with the country 's top education institutions , such as Alexander Rondeli , Temuri Yakobashvili , Vladimer Papava , Merab Kakulia , and Archil Gegeshidze .

Document: [S0] Everard Burnside Butler ( December 28 , 1885 – November 23 , 1958 ) was a Canadian rower who won a bronze medal in the single sculls at the 1912 Summer Olympics . [S1] Butler started training in rowing in 1908 , and next year won his first junior race . [S2] By 1910 he rowed as a senior in the United States and Canada , and in 1911 won two US national titles , in the single sculls and quarter - mile dash . [S3] He defended those titles in 1912 , and won the quarter - mile dash again in 1914 . [S4] Butler fought in World War I with the 12th Artillery Brigade , and suffered extensive injuries in a mustard gas attack in France . [S5] Consequently , after the war he retired from major rowing competitions and worked as an accountant . [S6] He returned to the army during World War II and served with the 48th Highlanders and Royal Canadian Ordnance Corps .

Document: [S0] María de Buenos Aires is a tango operetta ( tango operita ) with music by Ástor Piazzolla and libretto by Horacio Ferrer that premiered at the Sala Planeta in Buenos Aires on 8 May 1968 . [S1] The first part of the surreal plot centers on the experiences of a prostitute in Buenos Aires , Argentina ; the second part takes place after her death . [S2] The characters include María ( and , after her death , the Shadow of María ) , a singer of payadas ; various members of the Buenos Aires underworld ; a payador who functions as a poet and narrator ; a goblin - like duende ; several marionettes under the control of the duende ; a circus of psychoanalysts ; pasta makers ; and construction workers . [S3] Many elements of the libretto suggest parallels between María and Mary , the mother of Jesus ( in Spanish , María ) or Jesus himself . [S4] While certainly not in the narrow sense an opera ballet , because the dance is tango rather than classical ballet , it falls within the tradition of having set dance pieces integral to an operatic work . [S5] The music draws on the nuevo tango idiom for which Piazzolla is famous . [S6] The original idea for the story was conceived by Piazzolla 's lover at the time of its composition , Egle Martin , who was married to Eduardo " Lalo " Palacios . [S7] The title role was originally conceived for Martin , but while Piazzolla was still composing the operita , he and Martin broke up after he asked her husband for her hand at Christmas in 1967 . [S8] According to Martin , Piazzolla said to Lalo , " She is music , she ca n't belong to anybody , no she is music , she is music , and that 's me . " [S9] After their rift , a replacement was desperately needed , but Piazzolla soon met folksinger Amelita Baltar at the Buenos Aires nightclub Nuestro Tiempo , formerly known as " 676 " and once Piazzolla 's home base in Argentina . [S10] Baltar 's identification with the character María , paired with her beauty and captivating stage presence , made her ideal for the role . [S11] The piece is written for at least three vocalists ( one of whom , the narrator , mainly speaks rather sings ) . [S12] For the orchestration Piazzolla augmented his current working quintet : Piazzolla ( bandoneón ) , Antonio Agri ( violin ) , Jamie " El Russo " Gosis ( piano ) , Oscar Lopez Ruiz ( guitar ) and Kicho Díaz ( double bass ) ; with viola , cello , flute , percussion , vibraphone and xylophone , and a second guitar . [S13] María de Buenos Aires has often been performed with dancers as well as musicians . [S14] There are several extant arrangements , including Piazzolla 's own and one by Pablo Ziegler .

[S1] He preferred to work collaboratively with liberal white groups in the South , quietly as a " sideline activist , " to get practical results . [S2] His position is often contrasted with that of W. E. B. [S3] Du Bois , who was a powerful and militant advocate for blacks and described Johnson as " too conservative . " [S4] During Johnson 's academic studies and leadership of Fisk University during the 1930s and 1940s , the South had legal racial segregation and Jim Crow discriminatory laws and practices , including having disfranchised most black voters in constitutions passed at the turn of the century . [S5] Johnson was unwavering in personal terms in his opposition to this oppressive system , yet worked hard to change race relations in terms of short - term practical gains . [S6] His grandson Jeh Johnson served as the United States Secretary of Homeland Security from 2013 to 2017 .

[S1] The battle of Samugarh was fought between his sons Dara Shikoh ( the eldest son and heir apparent ) and his two younger brothers Aurangzeb and Murad Baksh ( third and fourth sons of the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan ) . [S2] Dara Shikoh began to retreat towards Samugarh , about 10 miles ( 16   km ) east of Agra , India , south of the Yamuna River , after Aurangzeb had defeated Dara Shikoh 's forces during the Battle of Dharmat . [S3] Aurangzeb and his smaller but formidable army then flanked Dara ’s fortified line along the Chambal River by finding a little - known and unguarded ford . [S4] The battle was fought during northern India 's warmest season and Aurangzeb 's men were on the march for a very long while . [S5] The army of Aurangzeb arrived with yellow banners and flags and fortified their position in front of the heir apparent . [S6] Dara Shikoh then tried to protect his rear flank by erecting massive red tents and banners .

Document: [S0] The Sims class destroyers were built for the United States Navy , and commissioned in 1939 and 1940 . [S1] These twelve ships were the last United States destroyer class completed prior to the American entry into World War II . [S2] All Sims - class ships saw action in World War II , and seven survived the war . [S3] No ship of this class saw service after 1946 . [S4] They were built under the Second London Naval Treaty , in which the limit on destroyer standard displacement was lifted , but an overall limit remained . [S5] Thus , to maximize the number of destroyers and avoid developing an all - new design , the Sims class were only 70 tons larger as designed than previous destroyers . [S6] They are usually grouped with the 1500-ton classes and were the sixth destroyer class since production resumed with the Farragut class in 1932 . [S7] The class served extensively in World War II , and five of the class were lost in the war . [S8] Of the five ships lost , four were at the hands of the Japanese and one at the hands of the Germans . [S9] The class served on Neutrality Patrols in the Atlantic in 1940 - 41 . [S10] Except for Roe , Wainwright , and Buck , the class was transferred to the Pacific shortly after the attack on Pearl Harbor . [S11] All of the ships saw extensive combat service . [S12] At the war 's end in August 1945 , three of the seven survivors were undergoing overhauls that were left unfinished , and were ultimately scrapped . [S13] The remaining four seaworthy ships were used as targets during the 1946 Operation Crossroads atomic tests at Bikini Atoll . [S14] One was sunk by the first blast , while the other three were sunk as targets two years later after serving as experimental platforms .
