Document: [S0] Intelligent design ( ID ) is a pseudoscientific argument for the existence of God , presented by its proponents as " an evidence - based scientific theory about life 's origins " . [S1] Proponents claim that " certain features of the universe and of living things are best explained by an intelligent cause , not an undirected process such as natural selection . " [S2] ID is a form of creationism that lacks empirical support and offers no testable or tenable hypotheses , so it is not science . [S3] The leading proponents of ID are associated with the Discovery Institute , a fundamentalist Christian and politically conservative think tank based in the United States . [S4] Though the phrase " intelligent design " had featured previously in theological discussions of the design argument , the first publication of the term intelligent design in its present use as an alternative term for creationism was in Of Pandas and People , a 1989 creationist textbook intended for high school biology classes . [S5] The term was substituted into drafts of the book , directly replacing references to creation science and creationism , after the 1987 United States Supreme Court 's Edwards v. Aguillard decision , which barred the teaching of creation science in public schools on constitutional grounds . [S6] From the mid-1990s , the intelligent design movement ( IDM ) , supported by the Discovery Institute , advocated inclusion of intelligent design in public school biology curricula . [S7] This led to the 2005 Kitzmiller v. Dover Area School District trial in which U.S. District Judge John E. Jones III found that intelligent design was not science , that it " can not uncouple itself from its creationist , and thus religious , antecedents , " and that the school district 's promotion of it therefore violated the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment to the United States Constitution . [S8] ID presents two main arguments against evolutionary explanations : irreducible complexity and specified complexity . [S9] These arguments assert that certain features ( biological and informational , respectively ) are too complex to be the result of natural processes . [S10] As a positive argument against evolution , ID proposes an analogy between natural systems and human artifacts , a version of the theological argument from design for the existence of God . [S11] ID proponents then conclude by analogy that the complex features , as defined by ID , are evidence of design . [S12] Detailed scientific examination has rebutted the claims that evolutionary explanations are inadequate , and this premise of intelligent design — that evidence against evolution constitutes evidence for design — is a false dichotomy . [S13] It is asserted that ID challenges the methodological naturalism inherent in modern science though proponents concede that they have yet to produce a scientific theory .

[S4] However it has been proposed that it derives from " guduu+ga " , ' at the place of the Murray cod ' [ guduu ] , rather than " gudugaa " , a species of yam . [S5] At the 2006 census , Goodooga had a population of 265 , with 81 % of the population of Aboriginal descent . [S6] Goodooga 's newspaper is the Goodooga Flash . [S7] Goodooga 's main sport is Rugby league , the Goodooga Magpies or the Goodooga ' Newtown ' Jets . [S8] The other sports played in town are Netball , Bowls and Basketball .

Document: [S0] The Prime Minister of Thailand is the head of government of the Kingdom of Thailand . [S1] The prime minister is also the chairman of the cabinet of Thailand and represents the government at home and the country abroad . [S2] The post of prime minister has existed since 1932 , after a bloodless revolution forced the absolutist King Prajadhipok to grant for the people of Siam their first constitution . [S3] Under the newly established constitutional monarchy , the first prime minister of Siam was Phraya Manopakorn Nititada . [S4] At first , the office was called the President of the People 's Committee , it was later changed to Prime Minister of Siam when the king deemed it too communistic . [S5] Constitutionally the prime minister is required to be a member of the lower house of the National Assembly ( the House of Representatives ) . [S6] He must also gain their approval through a resolution before an official appointment by the king can take place . [S7] As a result , the prime minister might succumb to a vote of no confidence and removal in the House . [S8] However , this has never happened up to date . [S9] Throughout the post 's existence it has mostly been occupied by military leaders from the Royal Thai Army , three holding the rank of field marshal and seven the rank of general . [S10] The post of prime minister is currently held by General Prayut Chan - o - cha , who was formally appointed to the office on 24 August 2014 . [S11] Previously he was the de facto head of government as leader of the National Council for Peace and Order , since the coup d'état on 22 May 2014 . [S12] Note : The list includes leaders of military juntas and acting prime ministers . [S13] However , they are not counted in the official list as provided by the Royal Thai Government

Document: [S0] Bernard Joseph Cribbins , OBE ( born 29 December 1928 ) is an English character actor , voice - over artist and musical comedian with a career spanning over seventy years . [S1] He came to prominence in films of the 1960s , and has been in work consistently since his professional debut in the mid-1950s . [S2] Cribbins narrated The Wombles , a BBC children 's television programme that ran for 60 episodes between 1973 and 1975 , and played the pretentious guest Mr. Hutchinson in " The Hotel Inspectors " episode of Fawlty Towers ( 1975 ) , and the belligerent barman in Alfred Hitchcock 's Frenzy ( 1972 ) . [S3] He also recorded several successful novelty records in the early 1960s and was a regular and prolific performer on the BBC 's Jackanory from 1966 to 1991 . [S4] Having appeared as Tom Campbell , a companion to Dr. Who in the 1966 feature film Daleks ' Invasion Earth 2150 A.D. , Cribbins also appeared four decades later as Wilfred Mott , a companion to television 's Tenth Doctor .

Document: [S0] The Rhodesian Bush War — also called the Second Chimurenga and the Zimbabwe War of Liberation — was a civil conflict from July 1964 to December 1979 in the unrecognised country of Rhodesia ( later Zimbabwe - Rhodesia ) . [S1] The conflict pitted three forces against one another : the Rhodesian government , led by Ian Smith ( later the Zimbabwe - Rhodesian government of Bishop Abel Muzorewa ) ; the Zimbabwe African National Liberation Army , the military wing of Robert Mugabe 's Zimbabwe African National Union ; and the Zimbabwe People 's Revolutionary Army of Joshua Nkomo 's Zimbabwe African People 's Union . [S2] The war and its subsequent Internal Settlement , signed in 1978 by Smith and Muzorewa , led to the implementation of universal suffrage in June 1979 and the end of white minority rule in Rhodesia , which was renamed Zimbabwe Rhodesia under a black majority government . [S3] However , this new order failed to win international recognition and the war continued . [S4] Neither side achieved a military victory and a compromise was later reached . [S5] Negotiations between the government of Zimbabwe - Rhodesia , the UK Government and Mugabe and Nkomo 's united " Patriotic Front " took place at Lancaster House , London in December 1979 , and the Lancaster House Agreement was signed . [S6] The country returned temporarily to British control and new elections were held under British and Commonwealth supervision in March 1980 . [S7] ZANU won the election and Mugabe became the first Prime Minister of Zimbabwe on 18 April 1980 , when the country achieved internationally recognised independence .

[S1] It was founded in New York City in 1940 as the primary philanthropic vehicle for the five third - generation Rockefeller brothers : John D. Rockefeller III , Nelson , Laurance , Winthrop and David . [S2] It is distinct from the Rockefeller Foundation . [S3] The Rockefellers are an industrial , political , and banking family that made one of the world 's largest fortunes in the oil business during the late 19th and early 20th centuries . [S4] The Fund 's stated mission is to " advance social change that contributes to a more just , sustainable , and peaceful world . " [S5] The current president of RBF is Stephen Heintz , who was appointed to the post in 2000 . [S6] Valerie Rockefeller serves as RBF 's chairwoman . [S7] She succeeded Richard Rockefeller , the fifth child of David Rockefeller , who served as RBF 's chairman until 2013 .

Document: [S0] The Penn Line is a MARC commuter rail service running from Union Station in Washington , D.C. to Perryville , Maryland via Baltimore 's Penn Station on Amtrak 's Northeast Corridor . [S1] It is MARC 's busiest and only electric line . [S2] Currently the line is the fastest commuter rail line in the country , with trains running at speeds of up to . [S3] The service is operated under contract by Amtrak which supplies employees to operate trains , and maintains the right - of - way and MARC 's electric locomotives and passenger cars . [S4] The line is administered by MARC , a service of the Maryland Transit Administration ( MTA ) . [S5] The Penn Line is the successor to commuter services provided by the Pennsylvania Railroad ( PRR ) , Penn Central , and Conrail as long ago as the mid-19th century . [S6] Additionally , Amtrak operated a commuter service named the Chesapeake between 1978 – 1983 . [S7] In 1983 , Maryland , along with a number of other Northeastern states , took control of its commuter railroads and the " MARC " ( Maryland Area Regional Commuter ) service name was established . [S8] The Penn Line became the replacement for Amtrak 's Chesapeake as well as the minimal former PRR commuter service between Washington and Baltimore .

Document: [S0] Laytongku or Lay Tong Ku ( , ) in S'gaw Karen : Letawkho , is a Karen village on the south - western tip of Tambon Mae Chan Subdistrict of Umphang District in Thailand 's Tak Province and the extreme north - western tip of Kanchanaburi Province . [S1] It is located in a valley of the Dawna Range , within the area of Thungyai Naresuan Wildlife Sanctuary and Umphang Wildlife Sanctuary . [S3] Laytongku appeared in the news in 2017 because of an unauthorized removal of an ancient pair of elephant tusks held sacred by the villagers . [S4] The village is located on the Thai - Myanmar border along the border of the Karen State of Burma .

Document: [S0] Black Lake is located in Cheboygan and Presque Isle counties in northern Michigan , United States . [S1] With a surface area of , it is the seventh largest inland lake in Michigan . [S2] The largest body of water in the Black River watershed , it drains through the Lower Black and Cheboygan rivers into Lake Huron . [S3] Black Lake is a summer destination for many families from the suburban Detroit area and from other nearby states as well as residents of the neighboring town of Onaway . [S4] Onaway State Park , at the southeastern end of the lake , offers camping , swimming and fishing . [S5] Its buildings , built during the Great Depression by the Civilian Conservation Corps , have been deemed eligible for inclusion in the National Register of Historic Places . [S6] Businesses on or near the lake include the Black River Marina , The Bluffs Restaurant and the 211 Outpost . [S7] Since the late 1960s , the United Auto Workers Union has maintained the Walter and May Reuther Family Education Center on the site of a former private estate . [S8] Black Lake is noted for its unusual fishing season . [S9] A limited lake sturgeon ice fishing season is permitted in the winter . [S10] The fishery is limited to five total fish taken each year , each over 36 inches and taken through the ice with fishing spears . [S11] 25 anglers are chosen by lottery each day and given a flag to raise when they have caught a fish . [S12] When five flags have been raised the season is closed for the year . [S13] Seasons have lasted as little as a few hours .

Document: [S0] Osaka Bay ( 大阪湾 Ōsaka - wan ) is a bay in western Japan . [S1] As an eastern part of the Inland Sea , it is separated from the Pacific Ocean by the Kii Channel and from the neighbor western part of the Inland Sea by the Akashi Strait . [S2] Its western shore is formed by Awaji Island , and its northern and eastern shores are part of the Kansai metropolitan area . [S3] Major ports on Osaka Bay include Osaka , Kobe , Nishinomiya , Sakai , Amagasaki , and Hannan . [S4] A number of artificial islands have been created in Osaka Bay in past decades , including Kansai International Airport , Kobe Airport , Port Island , and Rokko Island . [S5] Several islands at the south end of Osaka Bay are part of the Seto Inland Sea National Park . [S6] Industries locate around Osaka Bay because there is a skilled and plentiful workforce , many port facilities , efficient linkages ( from small to medium to large firms ) . [S7] There are good transport links ( including the Shinkansen ) , room for expansion ( land reclaimed from the sea ) , and a large local market ( 9 million ) . [S8] In a recent economic change in Osaka Bay , older ' heavy ' industries such as Nippon Steel have declined , and ' new tech ' companies such as ICT have expanded . [S9] There has been a growth in the quaternary industries — research , development , and information . [S10] There has also been a development in the science parks and the building of new motorways ; this has meant the loss of the countryside . [S11] The Tempozan Ferris Wheel and Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan are both located in the Tempozan Harbor Village area of Osaka .

Document: [S0] Vladimir Mitrofanovich Orlov ( ) ( July 15 , 1895 - July 28 , 1938 ) was a Russian military leader and Commander - in - Chief of the Soviet Naval Forces from July 1931 to July 1937 . [S1] Orlov was born in Kherson and initially studied in the Legal faculty of St Petersburg University ( although he did not complete his studies ) . [S2] He joined the Baltic Fleet in 1916 and served as a navigating officer on the cruiser Bogatyr . [S3] In 1919 - 20 he was political officer of the Baltic Fleet and fought against the forces of the white General Nikolai Yudenich in the defence of Petrograd . [S4] In the 1920s he was commisar for water transport and in 1923 he became political commissar for all naval academies . [S5] Between 1926 and 1930 he commanded the Black Sea Fleet . [S6] In 1931 he was appointed commander of the Soviet Navy and in 1937 he was appointed deputy minister of defence . [S7] Orlov was arrested on 10 July 1937 and was sentenced to death on 28 July 1938 and executed . [S8] He was posthumously rehabilitated in 1956 .

[S1] He won two medals in the men 's skeleton event at the FIBT World Championships with a gold in 1998 and a bronze in 1999 . [S2] Schneider also finish ninth in the men 's skeleton event at the 2002 Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City . [S3] He won the men 's overall Skeleton World Cup title in 1997 - 8 . [S4] After retiring from competition Schneider became a coach , leading the Canadian skeleton team to three medals at the 2006 Winter Olympics in Turin ( a gold for Duff Gibson , a silver for Jeff Pain and a bronze for Melissa Hollingsworth ) , and coaching Jon Montgomery to victory in the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver , British Columbia , Canada . [S5] In July 2012 Schneider agreed a two - year contract to coach the Russian skeleton team .

[S4] The character of much of Barbieri ’s work is farcical , utilizing mistaken identity and other devices to entertain the audience . [S5] His themes deal largely with the ins and outs of love , and the relations between the upper and lower classes in nineteenth - century Spain , but there is also a distinct political character to much of his work . [S6] The zarzuelas El barberillo de Lavapiés and Pan y toros both contain plots to overthrow the government . [S7] In addition to his compositions , Barbieri was also an accomplished musician . [S3] In France , he collaborated with famous scientists Jean - Baptiste Lamarck ( 1744 – 1829 ) and Heinrich Christian Friedrich Schumacher ( 1757 – 1830 ) , a fellow Dane on a research trip in Paris during the 1780s . [S4] Hwass is remembered for amassing a large shell collection that included numerous rare specimens . [S5] Many European scientists used the collection as a reference work for their personal publications . [S6] Hwass 's best - known written work was the 1792 publication of Encyclopedie Methodique . [S7] Although his friend , Jean Guillaume Bruguière ( 1750 – 1798 ) , is often credited as author of the encyclopedia , the majority of the work was done by Hwass .

[S1] An active film - maker from 1970 , Kiarostami had been involved in over forty films , including shorts and documentaries . [S2] Kiarostami attained critical acclaim for directing the Koker trilogy ( 1987 – 94 ) , Close - Up ( 1990 ) , Taste of Cherry ( 1997 ) – which was awarded the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival that year – and The Wind Will Carry Us ( 1999 ) . [S3] In his later works , Certified Copy ( 2010 ) and Like Someone in Love ( 2012 ) , he filmed for the first time outside Iran : in Italy and Japan , respectively . [S4] Kiarostami had worked extensively as a screenwriter , film editor , art director and producer and had designed credit titles and publicity material . [S5] He was also a poet , photographer , painter , illustrator , and graphic designer . [S6] He was part of a generation of filmmakers in the Iranian New Wave , a Persian cinema movement that started in the late 1960s and includes pioneering directors such as Bahram Beyzai , Nasser Taghvai , Ali Hatami , Masoud Kimiai , Dariush Mehrjui , Sohrab Shahid - Saless and Parviz Kimiavi . [S7] These filmmakers share many common techniques including the use of poetic dialogue and allegorical storytelling dealing with political and philosophical issues . [S8] Kiarostami had a reputation for using child protagonists , for documentary - style narrative films , for stories that take place in rural villages , and for conversations that unfold inside cars , using stationary mounted cameras . [S9] He is also known for his use of Persian poetry in the dialogue , titles , and themes of his films . [S10] Kiarostami 's films contain a notable degree of ambiguity , an unusual mixture of simplicity and complexity , and often a mix of fictional and documentary elements . [S11] The concepts of change and continuity , in addition to the themes of life and death , play a major role in Kiarostami 's works .

Document: [S0] The genocide of indigenous peoples is the mass destruction of entire communities of indigenous peoples . [S1] Indigenous peoples are understood to be people whose historical and current territory has become occupied by colonial expansion , or the formation of a state by a dominant group such as a colonial power . [S2] While the concept of genocide was formulated by Raphael Lemkin in the mid-20th century , the earlier expansion of various European colonial powers such as the Spanish and British empires , and the subsequent establishment of colonies on indigenous territory , frequently involved acts of genocidal violence against indigenous groups in the Americas , Australia , Africa and Asia . [S3] According to Lemkin , colonization was in itself " intrinsically genocidal " . [S4] He saw this genocide as a two - stage process , the first being the destruction of the indigenous population 's way of life . [S5] In the second stage , the newcomers impose their way of life on the indigenous group . [S6] According to David Maybury - Lewis , imperial and colonial forms of genocide are enacted in two main ways , either through the deliberate clearing of territories of their original inhabitants in order to make them exploitable for purposes of resource extraction or colonial settlements , or through enlisting indigenous peoples as forced laborers in colonial or imperialist projects of resource extraction . [S7] The designation of specific events as genocidal is often controversial . [S8] Some scholars , among them Lemkin , have argued that cultural genocide , sometimes called ethnocide , should also be recognized . [S9] A people may continue to exist , but if they are prevented from perpetuating their group identity by prohibitions against cultural and religious practices that are the basis of that identity , this may also be considered a form of genocide . [S10] Examples include the treatment of Tibetans by the Chinese government and Native Americans by the US government .

Document: [S0] White Light Rock & Roll Review is Matthew Good 's second album as a solo artist , and was released on June 15 , 2004 . [S1] Though it was not as well - received as his previous solo effort , Avalanche , it quickly achieved Gold certification in Canada . [S2] Recording sessions for White Light Rock & Roll Review began less than a year after the release of Avalanche , making it the shortest time spent between records for Good . [S3] Having become disenchanted with the state of recorded music , Good became enamored with the techniques employed by classic artists like Led Zeppelin and The Who , who spent much of their careers perfecting their live shows and recording albums live off the floor . [S4] To this end , Good sought to write songs that could best be conveyed to live audiences . [S5] In fact , many of the record 's tracks ( including " Little Terror " , " North American for Life " , " Blue Skies Over Bad Lands " , " It 's Been A While Since I Was Your Man " , and " Ex - Pats of the Blue Mountain Symphony Orchestra " ) were written and performed live , well in advance of the album 's release .

Document: [S0] Pierre Seghers ( 5 January 1906 , Paris - 4 November 1987 , Créteil ) was a French poet and editor . [S1] During the Second World War he took part in the French Resistance movement . [S2] He founded , among other things , the famous line of books Poètes d’aujourd’hui ( Contemporary poets ) in 1944 , which published 270 books of poets both famous and unknown ( such as an anthology of modern accursed poets in 1972 , ) . [S3] Together François Lachenal , Paul Eluard and Jean Lescure , he gathers in 1943 .the texts of many poets of the French Resistance , which he published in Les Editions de Minuit under the title : L’honneur des poètes . [S4] Among the prizes and orders he received , he was made a commander of the Légion d'honneur and in 1976 Laureate Of The International Botev Prize . [S5] He was doctor honoris causa of Saint Andrews University , Scotland . [S6] He is buried at the Montparnasse Cemetery . [S7] An exhibition on his life and work took place in the Musée du Montparnasse in Paris in 2011 . [S8] A detailed catalogue was then published .

Document: [S0] Maggie Simpson in " The Longest Daycare " , or simply The Longest Daycare , is a 2012 American traditionally animated 3D comedy short film based on the animated television series The Simpsons . [S1] In the film , Maggie Simpson is enrolled at a new daycare facility where she squares off with the foul - tempered Baby Gerald when she befriends a caterpillar . [S2] The short originated with Simpsons producer James L. Brooks , who enlisted long - time veteran of the series , David Silverman , to direct the film . [S3] The picture was written by producers Brooks , Al Jean , David Mirkin , writers Michael Price and Joel H. Cohen , as well as show creator Matt Groening . [S4] The events of the short film take place between the twenty - third and twenty - fourth seasons of The Simpsons . [S5] The film premiered on July 13 , 2012 , where it was attached to screenings of the 20th Century Fox release . [S6] The film is the second Simpsons theatrical release . [S7] The short was re - released on February 15 , 2013 and played before the film Life of Pi in selected theaters in USA . [S8] Reception has been positive , praising the storytelling and animation . [S9] The film was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film in 2013 , losing to Paperman .

Document: [S0] Independence Pass , originally known as Hunter Pass , is a high mountain pass in the Rocky Mountains of central Colorado in the United States . [S1] It is at elevation on the Continental Divide in the Sawatch Range . [S2] The pass is midway between Aspen and Twin Lakes , on the border between Pitkin and Lake counties . [S3] State Highway 82 traverses it , in the process reaching the highest elevation of a paved Colorado state highway on a through road . [S4] After Cottonwood Pass to the south , it is the second - highest pass with an improved road in the state , the fourth - highest paved road in the state and the highest paved crossing of the Continental Divide in the U.S. Because of the heavy snowfall at its elevation , it is closed in wintertime , isolating Aspen from direct access from the east during the ski season . [S5] When the pass is open in warmer weather , it is a popular destination . [S6] A scenic overlook near the pass allows visitors to take in the alpine tundra environment above treeline , and offers excellent views to the east of Mount Elbert , Colorado 's highest peak and the second - highest mountain in the contiguous United States . [S7] Rock climbers are drawn to nearby bouldering opportunities , and informal paths lead to nearby mountain summits of even higher elevation . [S8] Backcountry skiers make use of the slopes during the late spring and early summer . [S9] Since 2011 the pass has been on the route of the USA Pro Cycling Challenge . [S10] The pass was formed by glacial action and erosion in the region , and its first recorded sighting was by Zebulon Pike in 1806 . [S11] Ferdinand Hayden surveyed it in 1873 . [S12] As part of the Continental Divide , it was the limit of European settlement in the region at the time , with the land to the west reserved for the Ute people . [S13] Prospectors who defied governor Frederick Walker Pitkin 's order crossed the pass on July 4 , 1879 , giving it its current name and setting up a similarly named village ( now a ghost town ) to its west . [S14] A toll road built across the pass was abandoned and neglected after a railroad connection was made to Aspen . [S15] A new road replaced it in the 1920s ; portions of the old route can still be seen along the western approach . [S16] The Independence Pass Foundation , based in Aspen , works to repair damage to the pass 's environment caused by both roads since 1984 .

Document: [S0] The Berlin - Hohenschönhausen Memorial ( ) is a museum and memorial located in Berlin 's north - eastern Lichtenberg district in the locality of Alt - Hohenschönhausen , part of the former borough of Hohenschönhausen . [S1] It was opened in 1994 on the site of the main political prison of the former East German Communist Ministry of State Security , the Stasi . [S2] Unlike many other government and military institutions in East Germany , Hohenschönhausen prison was not stormed by demonstrators after the fall of the Berlin Wall , allowing prison authorities to destroy evidence of the prison 's functions and history . [S3] Because of this , today 's knowledge of the functioning of the prison comes mainly from eye - witness accounts and documents sourced from other East German institutions . [S4] The prison was depicted in the 2006 film The Lives of Others , and in 2017 TV series The Same Sky . [S5] It is a member organisation of the Platform of European Memory and Conscience .

Document: [S0] The Shanghainese language , also known as the Shanghai dialect , Hu language or Hu dialect , is a variety of Wu Chinese spoken in the central districts of the City of Shanghai and its surrounding areas . [S1] It is classified as part of the Sino - Tibetan language family . [S2] Shanghainese , like other Wu variants , is mutually unintelligible with other varieties of Chinese , such as Mandarin . [S3] Shanghainese belongs to the Taihu Wu subgroup , and contains vocabulary and expressions from the entire Taihu Wu area of southern Jiangsu and northern Zhejiang . [S4] With nearly 14 million speakers , Shanghainese is also the largest single form of Wu Chinese . [S5] It serves as the lingua franca of the entire Yangtze River Delta region . [S6] Shanghainese is rich in vowels ( twelve of which are phonemic ) and in consonants . [S7] Like other Taihu Wu dialects , Shanghainese has voiced initials : neither Cantonese nor Mandarin has voiced initial stops or affricates . [S8] The Shanghainese tonal system is also significantly different from other Chinese varieties , sharing more similarities with the Japanese pitch accent , with two level tonal contrasts ( high and low ) , whereas Cantonese and Mandarin are typical of contour tonal languages .

Document: [S0] Booker Taliaferro Washington ( – November 14 , 1915 ) was an American educator , author , orator , and advisor to presidents of the United States . [S1] Between 1890 and 1915 , Washington was the dominant leader in the African - American community . [S2] Washington was from the last generation of black American leaders born into slavery and became the leading voice of the former slaves and their descendants . [S3] They were newly oppressed in the South by disenfranchisement and the Jim Crow discriminatory laws enacted in the post - Reconstruction Southern states in the late 19th and early 20th centuries . [S4] Washington was a key proponent of African - American businesses and one of the founders of the National Negro Business League . [S5] His base was the Tuskegee Institute , a historically black college in Alabama . [S6] As lynchings in the South reached a peak in 1895 , Washington gave a speech , known as the " Atlanta compromise " , which brought him national fame . [S7] He called for black progress through education and entrepreneurship , rather than trying to challenge directly the Jim Crow segregation and the disenfranchisement of black voters in the South . [S8] Washington mobilized a nationwide coalition of middle - class blacks , church leaders , and white philanthropists and politicians , with a long - term goal of building the community 's economic strength and pride by a focus on self - help and schooling . [S9] But , secretly , he also supported court challenges to segregation and restrictions on voter registration , passing on funds to the NAACP for this purpose . [S10] Black militants in the North , led by W.   E.   B. [S11] Du Bois , at first supported the Atlanta compromise but after 1909 , they set up the NAACP to work for political change . [S12] They tried with limited success to challenge Washington 's political machine for leadership in the black community but also built wider networks among white allies in the North . [S13] Decades after Washington 's death in 1915 , the civil rights movement of the 1950s took a more active and militant approach , which was also based on new grassroots organizations based in the South , such as CORE , SNCC and SCLC . [S14] Booker T. Washington mastered the nuances of the political arena in the late 19th century , which enabled him to manipulate the media , raise money , develop strategy , network , push , reward friends , and distribute funds , while punishing those who opposed his plans for uplifting blacks . [S15] His long - term goal was to end the disenfranchisement of the vast majority of African Americans , who then still lived in the South .

[S4] Although slightly damaged on the branches and the tip of the trunk , it was designated Natural Monument in 1956 . [S5] Another giant ginkgo tree of similar characteristics in Tokyo is located in the grounds of Oji Shrine .

Document: [S0] Mono is a free and open - source project to create an Ecma standard - compliant .NET Framework - compatible software framework , including a C # compiler and a Common Language Runtime . [S1] Originally by Ximian , it was later acquired by Novell , and is now being led by Xamarin , a subsidiary of Microsoft and the .NET Foundation . [S2] The stated purpose of Mono is not only to be able to run Microsoft .NET applications cross - platform , but also to bring better development tools to Linux developers . [S3] Mono can be run on many software systems including Android , most Linux distributions , BSD , macOS , Windows , Solaris , and even some game consoles such as PlayStation 3 , Wii , and Xbox 360 . [S4] The Mono project has been controversial within the open - source community , as it implements portions of .NET Framework that may be covered by Microsoft patents . [S5] Although standardized portions of .NET Framework are covered under Microsoft Open Specification Promise — a covenant stating that Microsoft will not assert its patents against implementations of its specifications under certain conditions — other portions are not , which led to concerns that the Mono project could become the target of patent infringement lawsuits . [S6] Following Microsoft 's open - sourcing of several core .NET technologies since 2014 and its acquisition of Xamarin in the beginning of 2016 , an updated patent promise has been issued for the Mono project ( ) . [S7] The logo of Mono is a stylized monkey 's face , mono being Spanish for monkey .

Document: [S0] Nishiyama Minako ( 西山 美なコ , born in Hyōgo prefecture , in 1965 ) is a Japanese contemporary artist whose works have dealt with cultures , customs , and the representations of young females in Japanese media and popular culture . [S1] Her work is identified with an initial stage of the artistic transformation of post - modern Japanese " cute culture " in which cute images were appropriated and used for critique . [S2] Nationally she has had many solo shows in Okayama , Tokyo , Kyoto , Osaka , Fukuoka , and Nishinomiya . [S3] In addition to a solo show at the Galerie Ghislaine Hussenot in Paris , France she has participated internationally in group shows in Beijing , China ; Madrid , Spain ; Rimini , Italy and Portland , Oregon , Minneapolis and Miami in the United States . [S4] Since the beginning of the 1990s she has been making sculptures , paintings and installations using a transient material such as sugar with a bright luscious pink red to pink color that evaporate and dissolve over time . [S5] Her used of sugar and bright pink color refer to the stereotypical representations or images of cuteness or kawaii of young Japanese female . Document: [S0] Lee Hall or Lee Hall Mansion is a historic brick plantation house that was built during the period from 1848 to 1859 . [S1] The community of Lee Hall , Virginia is named for it . [S2] The house and village are located near the junction of U.S. 60 and VA 238 , in Newport News , Virginia . [S3] The current property was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972 . [S4] The listed property includes two contributing buildings : The Main House ( open to the public ) and the former Kitchen ( closed to public , used as staff offices ) . [S5] The house as well as the nearby community of Lee Hall were named for Richard Decatur Lee the original owner and builder of Lee Hall Mansion . [S6] Lee was a prominent local planter . [S7] Despite having the same last name as Virginia native and Confederate general Robert E. Lee , a direct lineage to General Lee can not be traced . [S8] Lee Hall Mansion was used as headquarters for Confederate generals Joseph E. Johnston and John B. Magruder during the Peninsula Campaign of the American Civil War in 1862 . [S9] Nearby is Endview Plantation , a 238-year - old house . [S10] Endview was used as a hospital during the Civil War and as a campground during the Revolutionary War , the War of 1812 and the Civil War .

Document: [S0] Antioch on the Orontes (; ; also Syrian Antioch ) was an ancient Greek city on the eastern side of the Orontes River . [S1] Its ruins lie near the modern city of Antakya , Turkey , and lends the modern city its name . [S2] Antioch was founded near the end of the fourth century BC by Seleucus I Nicator , one of Alexander the Great 's generals . [S3] The city 's geographical , military , and economic location benefited its occupants , particularly such features as the spice trade , the Silk Road , and the Royal Road . [S4] It eventually rivaled Alexandria as the chief city of the Near East . [S5] It was also the main center of Hellenistic Judaism at the end of the Second Temple period . [S6] Most of the urban development of Antioch occurred during the Roman Empire , when the city was one of the most important in the eastern Mediterranean area of Rome 's dominions . [S7] Antioch was called " the cradle of Christianity " as a result of its longevity and the pivotal role that it played in the emergence of both Hellenistic Judaism and early Christianity . [S8] The Christian New Testament asserts that the name " Christian " first emerged in Antioch . [S9] It was one of the four cities of the Syrian tetrapolis , and its residents were known as Antiochenes . [S10] The city was a metropolis of half a million people during Augustan times , but it declined to relative insignificance during the Middle Ages because of warfare , repeated earthquakes , and a change in trade routes , which no longer passed through Antioch from the far east following the Mongol invasions and conquests .

Document: [S0] Derby ( ' dər - bē ) is a city in New Haven County , Connecticut , United States , approximately 8 miles west - northwest of New Haven , Connecticut . [S1] Derby is located in southwest Connecticut at the confluence of the Housatonic and Naugatuck Rivers . [S2] It borders the cities of Ansonia to the north and Shelton to the southwest , and the towns of Orange to the south , Seymour to the northwest , and Woodbridge to the east . [S3] The population was 12,903 at the 2010 census . [S4] It is the smallest consolidated city in Connecticut by area and population . [S5] Derby was settled in 1642 as an Indian trading post under the name Paugasset . [S6] It was named after Derby , England , in 1675 . [S7] It included what is now Ansonia , Seymour , and parts of Oxford and Beacon Falls . [S8] Derby is home to the first trolley system in New England and the first electric locomotive in U.S. history to be built and successfully used commercially for hauling freight . [S9] The locomotive , built in 1888 is still kept in running condition by the Shore Line Trolley Museum .

Document: [S0] Zevs ( born Christophe Aguirre Schwarz on 17 November 1977 in Saverne , France ) is a French street artist , best known for his trademark " liquidation " technique . [S1] He was an early and influential graffiti artist and active as a tagger in Paris in the 1990s . [S2] He is named after a regional train , Zeus , that almost ran him over one day he was down in the metro . [S3] Working with other French artists in the second half of the 1990s like André and Invader , Zevs has been among the prominent figures who pioneered the French street art scene . [S4] By the end of the 1990s he became known for his poetic drawings of shadows in Paris , shortly after the departure of Facundo Newbery from Paris . [S5] Later he ' bombed ' models on the billboards between the eyes . [S6] Though his interventions have been very popular , it has been discussed in France whether it is vandalism or art . [S7] In 2008 Zevs had his first major survey exhibition at the classical art museum the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek in Copenhagen , Denmark . [S8] His work , including selections of all of his major series to that point , was displayed alongside masterpieces in the museum 's permanent collections such as Édouard Manet 's The Absinthe Drinker and Auguste Rodin 's The Thinker .

Document: [S0] Glandularia , common name mock vervain or mock verbena , is a genus of annual and perennial herbaceous flowering plants in the family Verbenaceae . [S1] They are native to the Americas . [S2] Glandularia species are closely related to the true vervains and sometimes still included with them in Verbena . [S3] Horizontal chloroplast transfer occurred at least twice and possibly three times between these genera , which are otherwise too distinct to warrant unification . [S4] The discovery of the signal in the chloroplast genome was announced in 2008 by researchers from the University of Washington . [S5] Somehow , chloroplasts from V.   orcuttiana , swamp verbena ( V.   hastata ) or a close relative of these had admixed into the G.   bipinnatifida genome . [S6] Although hybridization runs rampant in the true and mock vervains – the ancestors of the well - known garden vervain are quite obscure – it does not seem to have been the cause of the cross - species gene transfer . [S7] In addition , the researchers discovered the signal of one more transfer event . [S8] This had introduced chloroplasts from an ancestral member of the Verbena lineage nowadays found in South America into Glandularia . [S9] Although all members of the present genus can be distinguished to have a chromosome count of five , the South American species are diploid , while polyploid hybrid Glandularia are very widespread from northern Central America northwards . [S10] The second genetic introgression must have occurred before the genus spread north , as species with the Verbena - like chloroplasts are found all over the Americas . [S11] Since the new chloroplast genes replaced the old ones , it may be that the possibly hybridogenic G.   bipinnatifida actually underwent horizontal chloroplast transfer twice in its evolutionary history .

Document: [S0] In a Silent Way is a studio album by American jazz trumpeter , composer , and bandleader Miles Davis , released on July 30 , 1969 , on Columbia Records . [S1] Produced by Teo Macero , the album was recorded in one session date on February 18 , 1969 , at CBS 30th Street Studio in New York City . [S2] Incorporating elements of classical sonata form , Macero edited and arranged Davis 's recordings from the session to produce the album . [S3] Marking the beginning of his , In a Silent Way has been regarded by music writers as Davis 's first fusion recording , following a stylistic shift toward the genre in his previous records and live performances . [S4] Upon its release , the album was met by controversy among music critics , particularly those of jazz and rock music , who were divided in their reaction to its experimental musical structure and Davis 's electric approach . [S5] Since its initial reception , it has been regarded by fans and critics as one of Davis 's greatest and most influential works . [S6] In 2001 , Columbia Legacy and Sony Music released the three - disc box set The Complete In a Silent Way Sessions , which includes the original album , additional tracks , and the unedited recordings utilized for production purposes .

Document: [S0] Kiirunavaara ( Northern Sami : Gironvárri , Meänkieli : Kierunavaara ) is a mountain in Kiruna , Sweden that contains one of the largest and richest bodies of iron ore in the world . [S1] The presence of iron in the area was known already in the mid-17th century , but at this early time communication lines to this northerly region were quite insufficient to permit any major exploitation . [S2] Only with the construction of a railway , the Iron Ore Line and the ports of Narvik and Luleå at the end of the 19th century did commercial mining become a realistic proposition . [S3] The Swedish mining company LKAB ( Luossavaara - Kiirunavaara Aktiebolag ) has been mining the mountain since the beginning of the 20th century . [S4] The mining area around Kiruna and Malmberget and the iron port and steelworks at Luleå made Norrbotten County one of the first , and most prominent , regions of heavy industry in Sweden , and the wider region has remained at the forefront of mining and steel smelting and alloying technology .

Document: [S0] " Rock n Roll " is a song by Canadian recording artist Avril Lavigne . [S1] It was released as the second single from her self - titled fifth studio album by Sony Music Entertainment on August 23 , 2013 . [S2] The song was written by Lavigne , David Hodges , Chad Kroeger , Jacob Kasher Hindlin , Rickard B. Göransson and Peter Svensson and was produced by Peter Svensson . [S3] " Rock n Roll " is an upbeat pop punk song , and lyrically it is a declaration of rebellion on which the singer puts up her " middle finger to the sky " to " let 'em know that she 's still rock and roll , " refusing to behave like an adult . [S4] The song received a critical praise from music critics , and was highlighted as one of the standout tracks on the album . [S5] " Rock n Roll " performed moderately on the charts , reaching number one in South Korea and Taiwan , and number five in Japan , respectively . [S6] The song failed to make impact elsewhere , peaking at number 37 in Canada and number 91 on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart . [S7] The music video directed by Chris Marrs Piliero shows Lavigne in full combat mode , conspiring with Danica McKellar ( playing a character called Winnie Cooperre ) in an attempt to " save rock and roll " .

Document: [S0] Watts Station is a train station built in 1904 in Watts , Los Angeles , California . [S1] It was one of the first buildings in Watts , and for many years , it was a major stop for the Pacific Electric Railway 's " Red Car " service between Los Angeles and Long Beach . [S2] It was the only structure that remained intact when stores along 103rd Street in Watts were burned in the 1965 Watts Riots . [S3] Remaining untouched in the middle of the stretch of street that came to be known as " Charcoal Alley " , the station became a symbol of continuity , hope , and renewal for the Watts community . [S4] It has since been declared a Historic - Cultural Monument and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places .

Document: [S0] Luis Roche was an important Venezuelan urbanist and was the Venezuelan ambassador to Argentina . [S1] He was also an amateur film director . [S2] In the 1930s , Roche advocated for the redesign of Caracas , to include developed corridors to a multi - purpose center . [S3] His suggestion involved a 36-meter - wide avenue based on Avenue des Champs - Élysées . [S4] He was responsible in great measure for the development of Caracas ' east side during the 1940s . [S5] He contributed to the development of neighborhoods such as La Castellana , Altamira and La Florida . [S6] Roche was a relevant diplomatic figure as well , being appointed as Venezuela 's ambassador to Argentina . [S7] He married a Colombian / French lady by the name of Beatrice Dugand , with whom he had four children , Beatrice Roche , Lilianne Roche , Marcel Roche and Luis Armando Roche . [S8] An important avenue in Altamira ( Caracas ) bears the name Luis Roche in his honor .

Document: [S0] Jirō Shiizaki ( 椎崎二郎,Shiizaki Jirō ) ( 30 September 1911 – 15 August 1945 ) was a lieutenant colonel in the Imperial Japanese Army in World War II . [S1] He served as a member of the staff of the domestic affairs section of the Military Affairs Bureau 's War Affairs Section . [S2] Shiizaki was one of several members of that staff to participate in a coup ( the Kyūjō incident ) in the early morning of August 15 , 1945 , the day the Emperor would declare Japan 's surrender . [S3] The coup was organized primarily by Major Kenji Hatanaka , and though quite a number of men were involved in the plot at one point or another , Shiizaki was one of the few to be involved in the climactic action ; the rebels , with the help of the First Imperial Guard Division , seized the Imperial Palace , held Emperor Hirohito under , essentially , house arrest , and sought to destroy the phonographic recordings which had been made of the Emperor 's surrender speech . [S4] Sometime around seven o'clock on the morning of August 15 , the plot began to fall apart . [S5] General Shizuichi Tanaka , commander of the Eastern District Army , arrived at the Palace and harangued the conspirators on their duty to their country , and demanding that the dishonor brought by their treason could only be absolved through seppuku . [S6] Shiizaki , along with a number of others , committed ritual suicide that morning , on the grounds of the Imperial Palace .

Document: [S0] Breakout is an arcade game developed and published by Atari , Inc. , released on May 13 , 1976 . [S1] It was conceptualized by Nolan Bushnell and Steve Bristow , influenced by the 1972 Atari arcade game Pong , and built by Steve Wozniak aided by Steve Jobs . [S2] Breakout was the basis and inspiration for certain aspects of the Apple II personal computer . [S3] The game was ported to the Atari 2600 and was followed by a 1978 sequel , Super Breakout , which four years later became the pack - in game for the Atari 5200 console . [S4] Breakout spawned an entire genre of Breakout clones , and the concept found new legs with Taito 's 1986 Arkanoid which itself found dozens of imitators . [S5] In Breakout , a layer of bricks lines the top third of the screen . [S6] A ball travels across the screen , bouncing off the top and side walls of the screen . [S7] When a brick is hit , the ball bounces away and the brick is destroyed . [S8] The player loses a turn when the ball touches the bottom of the screen . [S9] To prevent this from happening , the player has a movable paddle to bounce the ball upward , keeping it in play .

Document: [S0] Operator Toll Dialing was a project and method used by the Bell System in the USA and Canada to automate the switching and billing of long distance calls in the public switched telephone network ( PSTN ) . [S1] The program was initiated by 1945 , at which time ca . [S2] 5 % of the 2.7 million toll board calls per day were handled by this method . [S3] Operator Toll Dialing eliminated the need for intermediate and inward operators to complete toll calls to distant central offices . [S4] Initially this system involved step - by - step routings to set up each circuit , but later was improved by the development of area codes with machine translation which helped to standardize dialing across the network . [S5] The system was implemented in the USA beginning in 1946 . [S6] In 1947 , the North American Numbering Plan for area codes was set up . [S7] Operator Toll DIaling was gradually superseded by Direct Distance Dialing ( DDD ) , in which the customer dialed the area code as well as the number . [S8] Beginning in 1951 on a limited basis , it was not fully implemented until the 1970s . [S9] Telephone administrations in other countries implemented similar programs , such as in the United Kingdom , which led to Subscriber Trunk Dialling ( STD ) .

Document: [S0] Mola di Bari , commonly referred to simply as Mola ( Barese : ) , is a town and comune of the Metropolitan City of Bari , in the region of Apulia , in Southern Italy , on the Adriatic Sea . [S1] In recent times , the town was best known for having primarily whitewashed buildings , however , growth , modern construction , and building design have changed the image significantly , particularly in the northern ( and more modern ) part of the town . [S2] Mola 's city center is its main piazza , Piazza XX Settembre near the port and it also boasts a church ( Chiesa Matrice , i.e. [S3] Mother Church ) dating back to the 13thcentury . [S4] Bakeries in Mola are known for their focaccia food . [S5] Until the early 1990s , there were two privately owned public firewood ovens available to the inhabitants of Mola , one located on Via Nino Bixio , on the southern part of the town , and the other located on Via Pesce , on the opposite side of the main Piazza . [S6] These businesses served the local residents by providing a place to cook baked goods , primarily focaccia and breads . [S7] Typically , focaccia pans were quite large ( some approaching half a meter in diameter ) and were difficult to cook in one ’s home . [S8] The tradition of sending items to be baked by the local oven has passed . [S9] Mola is also home to a large fishing industry that supplies fresh fish throughout the southern Italian region .

Document: [S0] Carl Buchheister ( 17 October 1890 – 2 February 1964 ) was a German constructivist artist noted for his multiple series of " model paintings " at Galerie Lambert Weyl , Paris . [S1] which he began in 1925 . [S2] He was born in Hanover , Germany . [S3] Although he was not officially part of the Bauhaus movement , Buchheister was a close friend of Wassily Kandinsky and paralleled many of the social and artistic goals of the Bauhaus school . [S4] With regard to constructivism , Buchheister was typically more playful and improvisational than his contemporaries , becoming interested in the Dada movement after a collaboration with Kurt Schwitters in the late 1920s which led him to incorporate more varied materials such as acrylic glass , aluminum , wood , and twine into his compositions . [S5] This direction was given much freer rein after World War II and the end of Nazism . [S6] He died in Hanover in 1964 .

[S3] However , some analysts considered the project unrealistic and doomed to fail due to the poor conditions of the infrastructure in the area . [S4] Eventually those plans were abandoned and all low - cost flights were moved in March 2012 at Bucharest main airport Henri Coandă International Airport .

Document: [S0] Paradise Cracked ( ) is a cyberpunk single - player turn - based strategy video game . [S1] It was created by MiST Land South ( renamed as GFI Russia in 2006 ) for Microsoft Windows and released in 2002 . [S2] It has several translation problems that make the game difficult to understand in English . [S3] The player starts as a character named " Hacker " who is just as the name implies . [S4] The player starts with a pistol and the ability to hack certain objects ( ATM 's , Trade Robots , etc . ) [S5] as well as a journal which gives maps of the area and tells them missions both current and completed . [S6] As certain missions are completed , the character 's level will increase and skills can have points added to them increasing areas like strength , aim , hacking skill , health points and so forth . [S7] The game offers the option to play solo or to join with other characters or groups ( such as the mob ) . [S8] Hacker is constantly hunted by the law making teaming up with someone in the best interest of the player 's survival . [S9] Teaming up will also add new missions to Hacker 's journal . [S10] Additional weapons , items , and body armor can be acquired by purchase or by killing another player . [S11] The character 's strength determines what weight of weapons , items etc . [S12] he can carry while certain clothing will increase or decrease the number of items they can carry . [S13] The heavier the weight , the less distance the character can move in a given turn . [S14] As strength and level increase , so will a character 's distance he can travel . [S15] The game never really gained much ground in terms of commercial success .

Document: [S0] Eleonora Vallone ( born 1 February 1955 ) is an Italian actress , model and TV - personality . [S1] Born in Rome , the daughter of actors Raf Vallone and Elena Varzi , she made her film debut in 1979 in the " poliziottesco " Gardenia , and later starred in several genre films , also in the more ambitious Alberto Bevilacqua drama film Le rose di Danzica . [S2] In 1981 she hosted the Sanremo Music Festival alongside Claudio Cecchetto . [S3] In the same years she appeared nude in several men 's magazines such as Playmen and the Italian edition of Playboy . [S4] A pioneer and teacher of water gymnastics , Eleonora Vallone founded the first Italian school for water aerobics instructors , and she patented the method " GymNuoto " . [S5] She also wrote three books about waterobics , " GymNuoto " , " GymVasca " and " GymSwim " .

Document: [S0] This is a list of the operating Victorian regional railway stations serviced by V / Line operated trains . [S1] The stations make up seven radial passenger train lines , which all operate from Southern Cross station in Melbourne , Australia , with two further lines proposed to be reopened to V / Line passenger rail services . [S2] Stations listed in bold are terminus stations . [S3] Frequent services operate to the major regional cities of Ballarat , Bendigo , Geelong , Seymour , and the Latrobe Valley ; with a smaller number of services continuing to the end of their respective lines . [S4] Services to Ballarat , Bendigo , Geelong , and the Latrobe Valley were upgraded as part of the Regional Fast Rail project completed in 2006 . [S5] Four lines previously closed to passenger services - those to Ararat , Bairnsdale , Leongatha and Mildura were proposed to be refurbished as part of the Linking Victoria project . [S6] While all were expected to reopen during 2004 , only the Ararat and Bairnsdale lines have been reopened , with the Leongatha and Mildura projects delayed .

Document: [S0] Cesare Mori ( Pavia , December 22 , 1871 – Udine , July 6 , 1942 ) was a prefect ( prefetto ) before and during the Fascist period in Italy . [S1] He is known in Italy as the " Iron Prefect " ( Prefetto di Ferro ) because of his iron - fisted campaigns against the Mafia in Sicily in the second half of the 1920s . [S2] He is widely regarded as a fascist , even though at the beginning of Italy 's fascist dictatorship he arrested both fascists and socialists when he was prefect of Bologna . [S3] He officially joined the Fascist National Party only in 1926 . [S4] He was probably an officer who did n't have any strong political beliefs and who exhibited courage , dedication and integrity in the defense of the state and its institutions especially in combating the Mafia in Sicily . [S5] Nonetheless , the fight against the Mafia carried out by Cesare Mori proved to be effective mainly due to the special powers granted to him by Benito Mussolini when he was prefect in Sicily . [S6] Italian film director Pasquale Squitieri made a movie in 1977 --- Il prefetto di ferro --- about his fight against the Mafia when he was prefect in Sicily .

Document: [S0] " In the Mood " is a popular big band - era # 1 hit recorded by American bandleader Glenn Miller . [S1] It topped the charts for 13 straight weeks in 1940 in the U.S. and one year later was featured in the movie Sun Valley Serenade . [S2] " In the Mood " is based on the composition " Tar Paper Stomp " by Wingy Manone . [S3] The first recording under the name " In the Mood " was released by Edgar Hayes & His Orchestra in 1938 ( see " Origins " below ) . [S4] In 1983 , the Glenn Miller recording from 1939 was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame . [S5] In 1999 , National Public Radio ( NPR ) included the 1939 Glenn Miller recording on RCA Bluebird on the NPR 100 , the list of " The 100 most important American musical works of the 20th century " . [S6] In 2004 , the 1939 Glenn Miller recording on RCA Victor was inducted into the Library of Congress National Recording Registry which consists of recordings that are " culturally , historically , or aesthetically significant . "

Document: [S0] The Navy , Army and Air Force Institutes ( NAAFI ) is an organisation created by the British government in 1921 to run recreational establishments needed by the British Armed Forces , and to sell goods to servicemen and their families . [S1] It runs clubs , bars , shops , supermarkets , launderettes , restaurants , cafés and other facilities on most British military bases and also canteens on board Royal Navy ships . [S2] Commissioned officers are not usually supposed to use the NAAFI clubs and bars , since their messes provide these facilities and their entry , except on official business , is considered to be an intrusion into junior ranks ' private lives . [S3] NAAFI personnel serving aboard ship are part of the Naval Canteen Service ( NCS ) , wear naval uniform and have action stations , but remain ordinary civilians . [S4] NAAFI personnel can also join the Expeditionary Force Institutes ( EFI ) , which provides NAAFI facilities in war zones . [S5] EFI personnel are members of the Territorial Army serving on special engagements , bear ranks and wear uniform . [S6] NCS personnel can similarly volunteer to join the Royal Navy when it goes on active service . [S7] Petty Officer John Leake , NCS canteen manager in HMS Ardent , was awarded the Distinguished Service Medal ( DSM ) in the 1982 Falklands War for his courage while manning a machine gun .

Document: [S0] The Treaty of Ghent ( ) was the peace treaty that ended the War of 1812 between the United States of America and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland . [S1] Both sides signed it on December 24 , 1814 , in the city of Ghent , United Netherlands . [S2] The treaty restored relations between the two nations to status quo ante bellum , restoring the borders of the two countries to the lines before the war started in June 1812 . [S3] The treaty was approved by the UK parliament and signed into law by the Prince Regent ( the future King George IV ) on December 30 , 1814 . [S4] It took a month for news of the peace treaty to reach the United States , and in the meantime American forces under Andrew Jackson won the Battle of New Orleans on January 8 , 1815 . [S5] The Treaty of Ghent was not fully in effect until it was ratified by the U.S. Senate unanimously on February 17 , 1815 . [S6] It began two centuries and more of peaceful relations between the U.S. and Britain , although there were a few tense moments such as the Trent Affair in 1861 .

Document: [S0] Microsoft Sync Framework is a data synchronization platform from Microsoft that can be used to synchronize data across multiple data stores . [S1] Sync Framework includes a transport - agnostic architecture , into which data store - specific synchronization providers , modelled on the ADO.NET data provider API , can be plugged in . [S2] Sync Framework can be used for offline access to data , by working against a cached set of data and submitting the changes to a master database in a batch , as well as to synchronize changes to a data source across all consumers ( publish / subscribe sync ) and peer - to - peer synchronization of multiple data sources . [S3] Sync Framework features built - in capabilities for conflict detection – whether data to be changed has already been updated – and can flag them for manual inspection or use defined policies to try to resolve the conflict . [S4] Sync Services includes an embedded SQL Server Compact database to store metadata about the synchronization relationships as well as about each sync attempt . [S5] The Sync Framework API is surfaced both in managed code , for use with .NET Framework applications , as well as unmanaged code , for use with COM applications . [S6] It was scheduled to ship with Visual Studio 2008 in late November 2007 .

Document: [S0] The Museum of Army Flying is a British military aviation museum about the history of flying in the British Army . [S1] It is located beside the Army Air Corps Centre in Middle Wallop , close to Andover in Hampshire , England . [S2] The Museum covers the history of Army aviation from the Balloon sections of the Royal Engineers , through the establishment of the Royal Flying Corps in 1912 and Air Observation Post ( AOP)Squadrons . [S3] It brings the story up to date with the establishment of the Army Air Corps in 1957 , from the merger of the Glider Pilot Regiment and the AOP Squadrons . [S4] The Museum also contains multiple flight simulators that anyone can use for a small fee . [S5] Outside the museum is a play park featuring aviation themed play pieces that kids can climb on , including a control tower based on the Middle Wallop control tower .

Document: [S0] The Tule Lake camp was a federal work facility and WRA isolation center located in Siskiyou County , five miles west of Tulelake , California . [S1] It was established by the United States government in 1935 during the Great Depression for vocational training and work relief for young men , in a program known as the Civilian Conservation Corps . [S2] The camp was established initially for CCC enrollees to work on the Klamath Reclamation Project . [S3] During World War II , in 1942 the Tule Lake War Relocation Center was built next to the camp as one of ten concentration camps in the interior of the US for the incarceration of Japanese Americans who had been forcibly relocated from the West Coast , which was defined as an Exclusion Zone by the US military . [S4] Two - thirds of the 120,000 incarcerated individuals were United States citizens . [S5] Renamed the Tule Lake Isolation Center , this facility was adapted in the wartime years to shelter Japanese - American strikebreakers used against resisters at the main segregation camp , imprison Japanese - American dissidents , and house Italian and German prisoners of war ( POWs ) who were assigned to work as farm laborers in the region . [S6] After the war , on 25 April 1946 , the camp was transferred from the Army to the Fish and Wildlife Service , which had managed it just prior to the establishment of the segregation camp . [S7] The four remaining buildings are being restored in a project to return the camp to its 1940s appearance .

Document: [S0] Rage Against the Machine is an American rap metal band from Los Angeles , California . [S1] Formed in 1991 , the group consists of vocalist Zack de la Rocha , guitarist Tom Morello , bassist Tim Commerford and drummer Brad Wilk . [S2] After a self - issued demo , the band signed with Epic Records and released its self - titled debut album Rage Against the Machine in 1992 , the material for which was written by all four members of the group . [S3] After contributing the single " Year of tha Boomerang " to the Higher Learning soundtrack in 1995 , the band released its second studio album Evil Empire in 1996 , on which " Year of tha Boomerang " was featured as the closing track . [S4] In 1997 the band released a cover version of Bruce Springsteen 's " The Ghost of Tom Joad " , and the following year contributed " No Shelter " to the soundtrack to the film Godzilla , as well as releasing it as a single . [S5] In 1999 the band released its final album of original material , The Battle of Los Angeles , which again credited all four members equally for songwriting . [S6] The group disbanded in October 2000 , after de la Rocha departed to focus on producing his first solo album . [S7] After the group 's breakup , Epic released Renegades in December 2000 , which featured cover versions of songs originally recorded by several hip hop artists , rock bands and other artists .

Document: [S0] Goght (; formerly Goghot ) is a village in the Kotayk Province of Armenia , located on the right bank of the upper - Azat River . [S1] It is known from 13th - century manuscripts as Goghot . [S2] It is located near Garni and sits along the road leading to Geghard Monastery . [S3] The village has a small ruined basilica from the 17th or 18th century located straight down a dirt road from the main square . [S4] Some khachkars are built into the exterior walls of the church , as well as at its altar . [S5] Goght sits overlooking a large gorge and upon a promontory on the other side is the 11th- to 13th - century monastery of Havuts Tar . [S6] It may be reached by foot from the town , but more easily from Garni via the Garni Gorge . [S7] The community has a school , kindergarten , house of culture , and a library . [S8] The local economy is heavily dependent on agriculture , based primarily on grain farming , orchard cultivation , and cattle - breeding .

Document: [S0] Saint Malo (; also known as Maclou or Mac'h Low , or in Latin as Maclovius or Machutus , born 27 March 520 – died 15 November 621 ) was a mid - sixth century founder of Saint - Malo , a commune in Brittany , France . [S1] He was one of the seven founding saints of Brittany . [S2] Saint Malo of Aleth was baptized as an adult by Saint Brendan the Navigator . [S3] He became a student of Saint Brendan . [S4] As a monk at Llancarfan Abbey in Wales , Saint Malo was known for his participation in the famous Voyage of Saint Brendan . [S5] As an Immigrant to Brittany , he helped in the missionary work of Saint Aaron of Brittany , was the first bishop of Aleth ( modern Saint - Servan , France ) and established churches in the area of Brittany now named Saint - Malo in his honor . [S6] Saint Malo of Aleth was later driven from the area to Saintes , France by opponents of his mission . [S7] Details of Malo 's career have been preserved in three medieval ' Lives ' that seem to include incidents associated with multiple people bearing a similar name . [S8] It appears that Saint Malo of Aleth was probably born in Wales in approximately 520 . [S9] Malo 's name may derive from the Old Breton machlou , a compound of mach " warrant , hostage " and lou ( or loh ) " brilliant , bright , beautiful " .

Document: [S0] Major League Baseball ( MLB ) is the highest level of play in North American professional baseball , and is the organization that operates the National League and the American League . [S1] In 2000 , the two leagues were officially disbanded as separate legal entities , and all of their rights and functions were consolidated in the commissioner 's office . [S2] Since that time , MLB has operated as a single league , and constitutes one of the major professional sports leagues of the United States . [S3] It is composed of 30 teams . [S4] The First - Year Player Draft , also known as the Rule 4 Draft , is MLB primary mechanism for assigning amateur baseball players from high schools , colleges , and other amateur baseball clubs to its teams . [S5] The first draft took place in 1965 ; it was introduced to prevent richer teams from negotiating wealthier contracts with top - level prospects and therefore , monopolizing the player market . [S6] Originally , three drafts were held each year . [S7] The first draft took place in June and involved high - school graduates and college seniors who had just finished their seasons . [S8] The second draft took place in January for high school and college players who had graduated in December . [S9] The third draft took place in August and was for players who participated in American amateur summer leagues . [S10] The August draft was eliminated after two years , and the January draft lasted until 1986 . [S11] The draft order is determined based on the previous season 's standings , with the team possessing the worst record receiving the first pick . [S12] In addition , teams that lost free agents in the previous off - season may be awarded " compensatory " picks .

Document: [S0] The Pittsburgh Catholic is the weekly Catholic newspaper for the Roman Catholic Diocese of Pittsburgh , published for lay people and priests . [S1] It labels itself as the oldest Catholic newspaper in continuous publication . [S2] The newspaper was established in 1844 by Pittsburgh 's first bishop , Michael O'Connor . [S3] According to its website , the Catholic has a total market of 111,250 Catholics . [S4] The Catholic is available for free at most churches and Catholic outlets or centers in the Diocese of Pittsburgh , as churches purchase the newspaper in bulk for 21 cents per copy . [S5] Articles include news about events occurring throughout the diocese , articles on local diocesan schools , features on community and charity programs orchestrated by local Catholic organizations , reviews and commentary on contemporary media , question - and - answer forums by priests to explain church doctrine , and editorials on Church issues . [S6] The former Bishop of Pittsburgh , Donald Wuerl , was generally seen as a conservative bishop . [S7] As a result , the Pittsburgh Catholic is a conservative publication as well . [S8] However , because the newspaper is oriented towards the local region , it rarely contains extensive commentary on national issues . [S9] According to the Pittsburgh Business Times Book of Lists , the Pittsburgh Catholic is the largest weekly publication in western Pennsylvania and the second - largest newspaper in western Pennsylvania . [S10] The Pittsburgh Catholic is a member of the Catholic Press Association . [S11] Its general manager , Robert P. Lockwood , was nominated as finalist for the association 's annual St. Francis de Sales Award .

Document: [S0] Malay houses ( Malay : Rumah Melayu ; Jawi : رومه ملايو ) are traditional dwellings , originating before the arrival of foreign or modern influences , and constructed by the indigenous ethnic Malay of the Malay Peninsula , Sumatra and Borneo . [S1] Traditional architectural forms , such as tropically - suited roofs and harmonious proportions with decorative elements are considered by traditionalists to still have relevance . [S2] However traditional buildings require significant maintenance compared to modern construction ; how to preserve wooden materials from the decaying effect of tropical weather as well as termite problems . [S3] These traditional skills are gradually being lost as Malaysia continues its process of industrialisation , while in Indonesia traditional houses have still survived in rural areas . [S4] The effort to preserve indigenous architectural styles of Indonesian archipelago has been conducted through documentation and create replicas in provinces pavilions in Taman Mini Indonesia Indah , Jakarta .

Document: [S0] Justinian Tamusuza ( born 1951 ) is a Ugandan composer of contemporary classical music . [S1] His music combines elements of traditional Ugandan music and Western music . [S2] He is best known for his first string quartet , which was included by the Kronos Quartet on their 1992 CD Pieces of Africa , which contains music by seven African composers . [S3] His music has also been performed by the Imani Winds . [S4] Tamusuza was born in Kibisi . [S5] His early training was in Baganda traditional music . [S6] His early instructors included the Reverend Anthony Okelo and Kevin Volans at Queen 's University Belfast in Belfast , Northern Ireland . [S7] He received his doctorate in composition at Northwestern University , where he studied with Alan Stout . [S8] He has taught at Makerere University in Kampala , Uganda , as well as at Northwestern University . [S9] His music is published by International Opus .

Document: [S0] Aspren or Asprenas ( ) was a 1st - century Christian saint and venerated as the first Bishop of Naples . [S1] Aspren lived at the end of the 1st century and in the early 2nd century , as confirmed by archaeological studies regarding the early Neapolitan Church as well as the fact that " Aspren " was a common name during the days of the Roman Republic and the early years of the Roman Empire and afterwards fell into disuse . [S2] The Marble Calendar of Naples ( Calendario Marmoreo di Napoli ) attests to Aspren 's existence and the fact that he lived during the reigns of Trajan and Hadrian ; Aspren 's episcopate is stated as lasting twenty - three years . [S3] Nothing is known of his life , but an ancient legend holds that Saint Peter , on his way to Rome , stopped at Naples and converted an old woman ( identified as Candida the Elder ) after he cured her of an illness . [S4] Numerous other converts to Christianity were made during this time in Naples , including Aspren , who was converted either by Peter or Candida herself and who had also been ill . [S5] The legend holds that Peter consecrated Aspren as bishop of Naples and asked him to construct the oratory of Santa Maria del Principio , which would form the basis for the basilica of Santa Restituta ; San Pietro ad Aram was also said to have been built during this time .

Document: [S0] The Vätsäri Wilderness Area ( , ) is located along the northeastern shore of Lake Inari in Inari , northern Finland , stretching all the way to the Finland – Norway border . [S1] The landscape is dominated by taiga forests of Scots pine , bog and bodies of water . [S2] The northeastern part rises as a treeless fell ridge . [S3] Vätsäri is one of twelve wilderness areas in Lapland and covers an area of . [S4] The wilderness has one marked trail and a few cabins . [S5] The reserve is under the management of Metsähallitus ( Administration of Forests ) and was established with the other wilderness reserves in 1991 . [S6] It is part of Pasvik – Inari Trilateral Park along with Øvre Pasvik National Park and Øvre Pasvik Landscape Protection Area in Norway , and the joint Norwegian – Russian Pasvik Nature Reserve . [S7] The area has a short growing season , cold winters , little precipitation and poor soil quality created by the gneiss bedrock . [S8] Lake Inari has been affected by acid rain and loss of fish from the Paatsjoki River Hydroelectric Plants . [S9] The reserve is an important habitat of the brown bear and also has a large moose population ; reindeer husbandry is practiced by the Samis . [S10] Whitefish and vendace are the most common species of fish , the latter being an introduced species .

Document: [S0] The List of diplomats of Norway to China began when diplomatic relations were established in 1851 . [S1] The establishment of diplomatic relations took place during the union between Sweden and Norway , and a Norwegian - Swedish consulate general was established in Guangzhou . [S2] A vice consulate was set up in Shanghai in 1853 . [S3] When the vice consulate in Shanghai became the consulate general in 1863 , and the consulate general in Guangzhou was upgraded to a vice consulate . [S4] When the union of Norway and Sweden was ended in 1905 , Norway sent the consul - general , Thorvald Hansen , to Shanghai . [S5] And there was a vice consulate , Jørgen Jacob Eitzen , in Hong Kong . [S6] The Norwegian legation in Beijing was established in 1919 . [S7] It was merged with the consulate general in Shanghai in 1930 ( after the Nationalist Government moved to Nanjing in 1928 ) and remained until 1954 . [S8] And there was an embassy in Chongqing from 1943 to 1945 during the war time .

Document: [S0] The Corps Hubertia Freiburg is a fraternity ( Studentenverbindung ) in Freiburg , Germany . [S1] It was founded on October 29 , 1868 and is one of 162 German Student Corps in Europe today . [S2] The Corps is a member of the Kösener Senioren - Convents - Verband ( KSCV ) , the oldest federation of classical European fraternal corporations with roots dating back to the 15th century and member fraternities across Austria , Belgium , Germany , Hungary , Latvia and Switzerland . [S3] Membership to the fraternity is open to honorable men studying at one of Freiburg 's universities and based exclusively on personality , good moral standing , and strength of character . [S4] Members of the Corps Hubertia value and engage in the tradition of academic fencing duels as a way to sharpen and prove their character under pressure . [S5] Continuing a practice dating back into the 1700s , Hubertia 's members wear the traditional Couleur , colored stripes , in green - gold - black . [S6] The fraternity teaches and expects tolerance from its members , stemming from diverse ethnic , national , religious and political backgrounds . [S7] Hubertia 's members are often referred to as Huberten . [S8] Members of the fraternity controlled the forestry departments of Baden , the south - west of Germany , in a de facto monopoly from the late 1800s to the early 20th century . [S9] Many of the members today practice this heritage as passionate hunters in private and fraternity events .
