Document: [S0] In music , a fugue ( ) is a contrapuntal compositional technique in two or more voices , built on a subject ( a musical theme ) that is introduced at the beginning in imitation ( repetition at different pitches ) and which recurs frequently in the course of the composition . [S1] It is not to be confused with a fuguing tune , which is a style of song popularized by and mostly limited to early American ( i.e. [S2] shape note or " Sacred Harp " ) music and West Gallery music . [S3] A fugue usually has three main sections : an exposition , a development and a final entry that contains the return of the subject in the fugue 's tonic key . [S4] Some fugues have a recapitulation . [S5] In the Middle Ages , the term was widely used to denote any works in canonic style ; by the Renaissance , it had come to denote specifically imitative works . [S6] Since the 17th century , the term fugue has described what is commonly regarded as the most fully developed procedure of imitative counterpoint . [S7] Most fugues open with a short main theme , the subject , which then sounds successively in each voice ( after the first voice is finished stating the subject , a second voice repeats the subject at a different pitch , and other voices repeat in the same way ) ; when each voice has entered , the exposition is complete . [S8] This is often followed by a connecting passage , or episode , developed from previously heard material ; further " entries " of the subject then are heard in related keys . [S9] Episodes ( if applicable ) and entries are usually alternated until the " final entry " of the subject , by which point the music has returned to the opening key , or tonic , which is often followed by closing material , the coda . [S10] In this sense , a fugue is a style of composition , rather than a fixed structure . [S11] The form evolved during the 18th century from several earlier types of contrapuntal compositions , such as imitative ricercars , capriccios , canzonas , and fantasias . [S12] The famous fugue composer Johann Sebastian Bach ( 1685–1750 ) shaped his own works after those of Johann Jakob Froberger ( 1616 – 1667 ) , Johann Pachelbel ( 1653 – 1706 ) , Girolamo Frescobaldi ( 1583 – 1643 ) , Dieterich Buxtehude ( c. 1637–1707 ) and others . [S13] With the decline of sophisticated styles at the end of the baroque period , the fugue 's central role waned , eventually giving way as sonata form and the symphony orchestra rose to a dominant position . [S14] Nevertheless , composers continued to write and study fugues for various purposes ; they appear in the works of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart ( 1756 – 1791 ) and Ludwig van Beethoven ( 1770 – 1827 ) , as well as modern composers such as Dmitri Shostakovich ( 1906 – 1975 ) .

Document: [S0] The Horn Blows at Midnight ( 1945 ) is a comedy fantasy film directed by Raoul Walsh , and starring Jack Benny . [S1] Its biggest claim to fame , apart from its star , is its failure at the box office . [S2] In the two decades following its release , Benny often exploited the film 's failure for laughs in his popular radio and television comedy series The Jack Benny Program , making the film a well - known entity to his wide audience , even if they had never seen it . [S3] The Horn Blows At Midnight would prove to be Benny 's final starring feature , although he would continue as a radio and TV star ( as well as making cameo appearances in films ) for years afterwards . [S4] The Horn Blows At Midnight had the misfortune to be released only eight days after the death of U.S. President Franklin Delano Roosevelt . [S5] This may have contributed to its poor reception , although the film 's negative reviews ( often alluded in jokes mentioning the production ) might have also impacted it , as the classic Rodgers and Hammerstein musical Carousel , also dealing with the afterlife , opened on Broadway at roughly the same time and became a hit .

Document: [S0] Mavis Grind ( or , meaning " gate of the narrow isthmus " ) is a narrow isthmus joining the Northmavine peninsula to the rest of the island of Shetland Mainland in the Shetland Islands , UK . [S1] It is just wide at its narrowest point . [S2] It carries the main A970 road to Hillswick in the north west of Shetland and is about two miles west of the settlement of Brae . [S3] Mavis Grind is said to be the only place in the UK where you can toss a stone across land from the North Sea to the Atlantic Ocean . [S4] It is a regular crossing point for otters , which in Shetland are sea - dwelling . [S5] In 1999 , local volunteers successfully helped to demonstrate whether Viking ships could be carried across the isthmus , instead of sailing around the end of the island . [S6] Remains of a late Bronze Age settlement have been found close by .

Document: [S0] Between 2008 and 2011 , the Milton Friedman Institute for Research in Economics was an academic center established at the University of Chicago as a collaborative , cross - disciplinary site for research in economics . [S1] The Institute aimed to advance , refine , and share research that applied the tools of economic analysis to real - world issues . [S2] The institute was named in honor of former Chicago economics professor , Milton Friedman , who is widely recognized for his many enduring contributions to economic analysis . [S3] The institute was a collaboration of the University of Chicago Booth School of Business , Department of Economics , and Law School and fostered inquiry across a wide range of topics and subfields . [S4] The institute aimed to advance and preserve the unique University of Chicago economic tradition of combining theory and data in rigorous analysis -- an approach exemplified by Friedman and others . [S5] The Institute hosted visiting scholars working in subfields of economics , business , law , and related fields such as public policy and medicine . [S6] It hosted workshops , seminars , and lectures on fundamental questions across these fields . [S7] The Institute also supported advanced professional training for post - doctoral students , as well as expanded opportunities for University of Chicago graduate students . [S8] When announcing the creation of the institute in 2008 , University President Robert J. Zimmer said its goal was to create " a primary intellectual destination for economics by creating a robust forum for engagement of our faculty and students with scholars and policymakers from around the world . ” The university had initially planned to invest $ 200 million in the institute , with half of that in the form of an operating endowment ; though the majority of funds were to be raised through donations . [S9] The institute was an object of intense controversy at the university , as many faculty objected both to its objectives as originally framed and to the naming of an institute after Friedman , who was viewed as polarizing . [S10] The announcement of the institute drew a response from more than 170 of the faculty at the university , who argued that to found such an institute would constitute " a symbolic endorsement of his views by the University " and that the proposal reflected " a very narrow research scope even within the field of economics , not to speak of the complete disregard for other disciplines involved in the study of ' economy and society ' " . [S11] In June 2011 , the institute and the Becker Center on Chicago Price Theory were joined to form the new Becker Friedman Institute for Research in Economics .

[S2] Thus , the group reduced the third side to an extended play record entitled ' " Babyfingers ' " , and released it in 1979 to people who had been waiting for their copy of The Third Reich and Roll box sets . [S3] A second printing was made for members of the W.E.I.R.D. [S4] fan club in 1981 , and a last pressing , on pink vinyl , in 1985 . [S8] Of these , the Milk and the Kootenay cross the international border twice , the Milk leaving and then re - entering the United States , the Kootenay leaving and then re - entering Canada . [S9] The drainage basins of these nine rivers extend into both countries ; in addition , the drainage basins of six others — the Fraser , Assiniboine , South Saskatchewan , Saskatchewan , Nelson , and Winnipeg — extend into the United States even though their main stems flow entirely within Canada . [S10] Sources report hydrological quantities with varied precision . [S11] Biologist and author Ruth Patrick , describing a table of high - discharge rivers , wrote that data on discharge , drainage area , and length varied widely among authors whose works she consulted . [S12] " It seems , " she said , " that the wisest course is to regard data tables such as the present one as showing the general ranks of rivers , and not to place too much importance on minor ( 10–20 % ) differences in figures . Davis and a professor at the University of Massachusetts Amherst , sought to demonstrate and protest the ignorance of the state bureaucracy in Boston of the rural portions of the commonwealth . [S2] To do so , he invented the town of Ripton . [S3] He then proceeded to apply for various grants and other official assistance , and the town was allotted funds in the state budget . [S4] Several checks were issued , and deposited in an escrow account , before the hoax was uncovered . [S5] The funds were returned and the matter dropped . [S6] In 1985 , Representatives of the town of Ripton contacted the US Air Force and invited them to situate antennas for a post - nuclear war communication system in their town . [S7] Robbins Phillips , chairman of the Board of Selectmen of Ripton , stated that the antennas would make good nesting places for eagles . [S8] As a protest of the issue today , some signposts in the western portion of Massachusetts still contain " directions " to Ripton . [S9] Lawmakers in western Massachusetts continued to humorously reference the incident in proposed state budgets .

[S5] was recorded over two time periods at Track Record Studios in North Hollywood , California , during October – November 1980 and again in January 1981 . [S6] After the original recording sessions , drummer Jay Ziskrout left Bad Religion and was replaced by his friend and the band 's roadie Pete Finestone , who was brought in to complete the rest of the album . [S7] Though not yet credited as a member of the band , future guitarist Greg Hetson , who was in Circle Jerks during this time , provided a guitar solo on " Part III " . [S8] How Could Hell Be Any Worse ? [S9] was also Bad Religion 's last album featuring Jay Bentley on bass for six years , until 1988 's Suffer . [S10] The front cover photograph was taken by Edward Colver near the Hollywood Bowl , while the back cover featured one of Gustave Dore 's illustrations of Dante 's Divine Comedy .

Document: [S0] The Irish in the British Armed Forces refers to the history of Irish people serving in the British Armed Forces ( including the British Army , the Royal Navy , the Royal Air Force and other elements ) . [S1] Ireland was then as part of the United Kingdom from 1800 - 1922 and during this time in particular many Irishmen fought in the British Army . [S2] Different social classes joined the military for various reasons , including the Anglo - Irish officers who thoroughly identified with the British Empire , while others , typically poorer Irish Catholics did so to feed their families or seeking adventure . [S3] Many Irishmen and members of the Irish diaspora in Britain and also Ulster - Scots served in both World War I and World War II as part of the British forces . [S4] However , especially since the advent of Irish independence and The Troubles , the topic of enlistment in the British forces has been controversial for the Irish at home , but does still occur . [S5] Since partition , Irish citizens have continued to have the right to serve in the British Army . [S6] Since 2007 , when troops finally withdrew from the streets of Northern Ireland , the number of Irish citizens joining has increased , reaching its highest levels since World War II .

[S5] Throughout the summer , it features various street fairs and festivals . [S6] Among locals , Crescent Street is known better for its many clubs and bars . [S7] Saint - Laurent Boulevard and the surrounding Plateau Mont - Royal neighbourhood , are also well known for their nightlife , with many bars , nightclubs and restaurants . [S8] The main sectors that attract tourism in Montreal are Festivals drawing in 7.5 million tourists , museums accounting for 7 million visits and Old Montreal bringing in 2.5 million tourists in the year 2013 .

Document: [S0] Ferrous metallurgy is the metallurgy of iron and its alloys . [S1] It began far back in prehistory . [S2] The earliest surviving iron artifacts , from the 4th millennium BC in Egypt , were made from meteoritic iron - nickel . [S3] It is not known when or where the smelting of iron from ores began , but by the end of the 2nd millennium BC iron was being produced from iron ores from Sub - Saharan Africa to China . [S4] The use of wrought iron ( worked iron ) was known by the 1st millennium BC , and its spread marked the Iron Age . [S5] During the medieval period , means were found in Europe of producing wrought iron from cast iron ( in this context known as pig iron ) using finery forges . [S6] For all these processes , charcoal was required as fuel . [S7] Steel ( with a carbon content between pig iron and wrought iron ) was first produced in antiquity as an alloy . [S8] Its process of production , Wootz steel , was exported before the 4th century BC from India to ancient China , Africa , the Middle East and Europe . [S9] Archaeological evidence of cast iron appears in 5th - century BC China . [S10] New methods of producing it by carburizing bars of iron in the cementation process were devised in the 17th century . [S11] During the Industrial Revolution , new methods of producing bar iron by substituting coke for charcoal were devised and these were later applied to produce steel , creating a new era of greatly increased use of iron and steel that some contemporaries described as a new Iron Age . [S12] In the late 1850s , Henry Bessemer invented a new steelmaking process , that involved blowing air through molten pig iron to burn off carbon , and so to produce mild steel . [S13] This and other 19th - century and later steel making processes have displaced wrought iron . [S14] Today , wrought iron is no longer produced on a commercial scale , having been displaced by the functionally equivalent mild or low carbon steel . [S15] The largest and most modern underground iron ore mine in the world is located in Kiruna , Norrbotten County , Lapland . [S16] The mine which is owned by Luossavaara - Kiirunavaara AB , a large Swedish mining company , has an annual production capacity of over 26 million tonnes of iron ore .

[S3] All of Li Jiancheng 's sons were executed and excluded from imperial clan . [S4] After Li Shimin took the throne , Li Jiancheng was posthumously created the Prince of Xi ( 息隐王 ) . [S5] Later , he was buried with ceremonies due an imperial prince . [S6] In 642 , Li Jiancheng 's crown prince title was restored as the crown Prince of Yin ( 隐太子 ) .

Document: [S0] The Storming of the Winter Palace was a 1920 mass spectacle , based on historical events that took place in Petrograd during the 1917 October Revolution . [S1] Taking place on the third anniversary of the revolution , it was directed by Nikolai Evreinov and was subtitled a " mass action . " [S2] The sets were designed by Yuri Annenkov . [S3] The spectacle was staged outside the former Tsarist Winter Palace where the Provisional Government was meeting at the time of the Bolshevik revolution . [S4] Its performers included 125 ballet dancers , 100 circus people , 1,750 supernumeraries and students , 200 women , 260 secondary actors , and 150 assistants . [S5] There were also tanks and armoured cars involved . [S6] The mass spectacle form took the pre - revolutionary Symbolist utopias of " ritual theatre " ( whose formulation was largely a response to the abortive 1905 revolution ) , and recast their " people " as the proletariat . [S7] Performed on 7 November before 100,000 spectators , the action begins with the February Revolution , follows the gradual organization of the workers ( on a red stage to the left , with Kerensky and the Provisional Government on a white stage to the right ) , until they are illuminated fully by searchlights , and crying " Lenin , Lenin " charge over the arch which joins the two stages to do battle with the " Whites . " [S8] Kerensky leaps to a car for an escape , and is pursued along a path between the two large groups of spectators by trucks full of the Red Guard waving bayonets , to the Palace . [S9] Silhouettes struggle in the windows of the Palace , until the Red Army is finally successful , and red lights flash out . [S10] A cannon fired from the cruiser Aurora and fireworks herald the victory of the October Revolution .

Document: [S0] Matthew de Glendonwyn ( died 10 May 1408 ) was a late 14th and early 15th century bishop of Glasgow . [S1] He was elected to the see after the death of Cardinal Walter Wardlaw , his predecessor as bishop . [S2] He was elected sometime between Wardlaw 's death in September and Matthew 's first appearance as bishop - elect in December . [S3] Matthew was consecrated some months after his election , either in late 1387 or early 1388 . [S4] Matthew was a witness to charters of kings Robert II and Robert III , an occasional ambassador of the Scottish crown to England , and a frequent arbiter in disputes concerning various religious establishments . [S5] On 21 May 1401 , he introduced a tax in his diocese to improve the deficient ornamenta of the diocese ( i.e. [S6] chasubles , copes , dalmatics , etc . ) . [S7] According to the Martyrology of Glasgow , he died on 10 May 1408 .

Document: [S0] In the southwestern United States , a ramada is a temporary or permanent shelter equipped with a roof but no walls , or only partially enclosed . [S1] Ramadas have traditionally been constructed with branches or bushes by aboriginal Americans living in the region ( deriving from the Spanish rama , meaning " branch " ) . [S2] However , the term today is also applied to permanent concrete , wooden , or steel structures used to shelter objects or people from the sun . [S3] For example , public parks in desert areas of the United States may contain ramadas with picnic tables , restrooms , water sources , etc . [S4] Since sunlight is more of an environmental hazard than wind or snow or rain in this part of the world , a roof alone provides substantial shelter . [S5] And because there are no walls in the structure , airflow is unrestricted , helping to keep the temperature below the roof substantially cooler than ambient . [S6] An example of a large modern - day ramada can be seen at the Casa Grande Ruins National Monument in Arizona , where it is used to protect ancient ruins .

Document: [S0] Gennadii Vladimirovich Belyi ( 1951 – 2001 , , ) was a Soviet , Ukrainian , and Russian mathematician , known for Belyi 's theorem on the representation of algebraic curves as Riemann surfaces and for the Belyi functions arising in that theorem . [S1] Belyi was born on February 2 , 1951 , in Magnitogorsk , Russia , then part of the Soviet Union . [S2] His family moved from there to Ukraine , and he began his studies at the Kiev Physics and Mathematics School but moved from there to Moscow State University . [S3] After completing his studies in 1973 he returned to Ukraine , working in Kiev and then Lviv . [S4] He became a graduate student at the Steklov Institute of Mathematics in Moscow in 1975 , and studied there under the supervision of Igor Shafarevich , earning a candidate degree in 1979 . [S5] He then took a faculty position at Vladimir State University , in Vladimir , Russia , where he remained for the remainder of his career . [S6] He died on January 29 , 2001 , in Vladimir . [S7] Belyi won a prize of the Moscow Mathematical Society in 1981 , and was an invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians in 1986 .

Document: [S0] Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Martinsburg Shops is a historic industrial district in Martinsburg , West Virginia . [S1] It is significant both for its railroading architecture by Albert Fink and John Rudolph Niernsee and for its role in the Great Railroad Strike of 1877 . [S2] It consists of three contributing buildings , one of which is the oldest covered roundhouse in the United States . [S3] The presence of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad Company in Martinsburg dates back to the late 1840s , when the first engine and machine shops were erected for the expanding company . [S4] The shops were designated a National Historic Landmark and placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2003 . [S5] They are now managed by a local authority as an event venue .

Document: [S0] " Bombtrack " is a song by American rap metal band Rage Against the Machine that opens their self - titled debut album . [S1] Like most of Rage Against the Machine 's songs , the song 's lyrics discuss social inequality , proclaiming that " landlords and power whores " were going to " burn " . [S2] The riffs were composed by Rage Against the Machine bassist Tim Commerford . [S3] The song is one of three on the album in the key of F along with " Know Your Enemy " and " Fistful of Steel " . [S4] Impressed by their song , Rage Against the Machine named it Bombtrack in reference to hip hop terminology where the word ' bomb ' means ' the greatest ' , making the song title literally mean ' the greatest track ' . [S5] A music video was released , depicting support for the Peruvian Maoist terrorist organization , Sendero Luminoso and its leader Abimael Guzman . [S6] The video clip did not appear on the group 's first home video , citing Rage 's first altered political opinion . [S7] In 2003 , the video finally appeared as bonus material on their Live at the Grand Olympic Auditorium DVD . [S8] The single artwork features Cuban photographer Alberto Korda 's famous image of Che Guevara , Guerrillero Heroico . [S9] A mirrored version of the iconic two - tone portrait by Irish artist Jim Fitzpatrick ( T - shirt version ) . [S10] Perhaps the song 's most notable appearance outside of the music industry would be its appearance in Oliver Stone 's controversial film Natural Born Killers , when Mickey breaks out of his prison cell in search of Mallory .

[S5] Much of Boulainvilliers ' historical work and political life centered on the decline of the nobility .

Document: [S0] The Neue Bachgesellschaft , or New Bach Society , is an organisation based in Leipzig , Germany , devoted to the music of the composer Johann Sebastian Bach . [S1] It was founded in 1900 as the successor to the Bach Gesellschaft , which between 1850 and 1900 produced a complete edition of Bach 's works , publishing many pieces for the first time . [S2] On completion of these collected works ( the Bach - Ausgabe ) , the original Society dissolved itself . [S3] The new Society approved three enduring projects : [S4] the annual edition of a Bach - Jahrbuch ( Bach yearbook ) [S5] biannual ( today : annual ) Bachfeste ( Bach festivals ) . [S6] The venues of the Bachfest have mainly been in Germany , but the 2012 Festival had an international dimension , being held in Görlitz - Zgorzelec on the German - Polish border . [S7] the founding of a Bach museum . [S8] In 1907 the Society opened the first museum dedicated to Bach at Eisenach , the town where he was born . [S9] This Bachhaus is managed by the Bachhaus Eisenach gemeinnützige GmbH , a registered charitable company , with the New Bach Society as its sole associate . [S10] The Society has not been directly involved in publishing scores in the way that its predecessor was . [S11] However , in 1950 it recommended that the second complete edition of Bach 's music be undertaken , the Neue Bach - Ausgabe ( NBA , in English : New Bach Edition ) . [S12] The project was a joint venture of musicologists in Göttingen , then West Germany , and Leipzig , then East Germany , in order to stress that the common cultural heritage was undivisible .

St. Catharines Milling and Lumber Company was to have a long - lasting influence on the interpretation of First Nations land claims in Canada . [S3] Boyd was Chancellor of the High Court of Justice of the Province of Ontario . [S4] He was appointed a Knight Commander of the Order of St Michael and St George ( KCMG ) during the visit to Canada of TRH the Duke and Duchess of Cornwall and York ( later King George V and Queen Mary ) in October 1901 . [S5] In 1903 , Boyd and William Glenholme Falconbridge were appointed to a Royal Commission to investigate charges of bribery brought forward by Robert Roswell Gamey against the Liberal Government of the time . [S6] Although the commission found no proof for these allegations , the provincial Conservatives won the general election that followed two years later .

Document: [S0] The Piton des Neiges ( Snow Peak ) is a massive 3,069   m ( 10,069   ft ) shield volcano on Réunion , one of the French volcanic islands in the Mascarene Archipelago in the southwestern Indian Ocean . [S1] It is located about east of Madagascar . [S2] Piton des Neiges is the highest point on Réunion and is considered to be the highest point in the Indian Ocean . [S3] The volcano was formed by the Réunion hotspot and emerged from the sea about two million years ago . [S4] Now deeply eroded , the volcano has been inactive for 20,000   years and is surrounded by three massive crater valleys , the Cirques . [S5] Piton des Neiges forms the northwestern two thirds of Réunion , with the very active Piton de la Fournaise comprising the rest . [S6] As it name suggests , snow is occasionally seen on its summit in winter . [S7] The volcanic island is considered to be about three million years old ( Pliocene ) ; the other two islands in the archipelago , Mauritius and Rodrigues , are 7.8   million ( Miocene ) and 1 million ( Pleistocene ) years old , respectively . [S8] The island possesses a high endemism of flowering plants ( about 225 ) ; this has justified the creation of a biological reserve on the lower slopes of the Piton des Neiges .

[S4] It concerns a love triangle that develops between two good friends and a new girl who transfers to their high school from Tokyo . [S5] Ocean Waves was an attempt by Studio Ghibli to allow their younger staff members to make a film reasonably cheaply . [S6] However , it ended up going both over budget and over schedule . Document: [S0] João Paulo de Leiria e Silva ( born 13 November 1964 in Luanda ) is an Angolan sport shooter . [S1] He became the only sport shooter to represent Angola at the 2000 Summer Olympics , and the second from his country to do so in Olympic history ( the first being done by Paulo Morais in Atlanta 1996 ) . [S2] De Silva competed for the Angolan squad in the men 's trap at the 2000 Summer Olympics through a Tripartite Commission Invitation . [S3] He shuttered the lowest score in the qualifying round with 99 hits out of a possible 125 , placing him in last from a field of forty - one shooters . [S4] At the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro , he competed in the men 's trap competition thanks to another Tripartite Commission invitation . [S5] He finished 33rd in the qualification round and did not advance . [S6] He was the oldest member of Angola 's 2016 Olympic team .

Document: [S0] Assassin 's Creed Unity is an action - adventure video game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft . [S1] It was released in November 2014 for Microsoft Windows , PlayStation 4 and Xbox One . [S2] It is the eighth major installment in the Assassin 's Creed series , and the successor to 2013 's . [S3] It also has ties to Assassin 's Creed Rogue which was released for the previous generation consoles , the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 on the same date . [S4] The plot is set in a fictional history of real world events and follows the centuries - old struggle between the Assassins , who fight for peace with free will , and the Templars , who desire peace through control . [S5] The story is set in Paris during the French Revolution ; the single - player story follows Arno Victor Dorian in his efforts to expose the true powers behind the Revolution . [S6] The game retains the series ' third - person open world exploration as well as introducing a revamped combat , parkour and stealth system . [S7] The game also introduces cooperative multiplayer to the Assassin 's Creed series , letting up to four players engage in narrative - driven missions and explore the open world map . [S8] Assassin 's Creed Unity received mixed reviews upon its release . [S9] Praise was directed towards its visuals , improved gameplay , customization options , multiplayer - oriented format , mission design , setting , characterization , and narrative . [S10] However , the game was criticized for a lack of gameplay - innovation , unrefined controls , and numerous graphical issues and bugs upon release . [S11] Because of the game 's poor launch owing to the technical issues , Ubisoft issued an apology , and offered compensation . [S12] Assassin 's Creed Unity was followed by Assassin 's Creed Syndicate , which takes place in Victorian England , and was released in October 2015 .

Document: [S0] Briggs Terrace , also known as Evergreen Lane , is a nationally recognized historic district located in Nevada , Iowa , United States . [S1] It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1998 . [S2] At the time of its nomination it consisted of eight resources , which included six contributing buildings , one contributing site , and two non - contributing buildings . [S3] This estate was established and built by Otis Briggs , a local banker who founded Farmers Bank in Nevada . [S4] He arrived in town in 1857 from Des Moines , four years after Nevada and Story County were founded . [S5] He worked in a variety of commercial ventures before becoming a banker . [S6] Briggs invested heavily in real estate , and he became one of the largest land owners in the county . [S7] The two - story , brick , Italianate style house was completed in 1879 . [S8] It features floor - length windows , a wraparound porch , and a bay window . [S9] It is surrounded by an planted grounds , which contribute to the historic nature of the district . [S10] The other historic building located here are the carriage house ( c. 1879 ) , barn ( c. 1879 ) , and late 19th century out buildings .

Document: [S0] The Atlantic Charter was a pivotal policy statement issued during World War II on 14 August 1941 which defined the Allied goals for the post - war world . [S1] The leaders of the United Kingdom and the United States drafted the work and all the Allies of World War II later confirmed it . [S2] The Charter stated the ideal goals of the war : no territorial aggrandizement ; no territorial changes made against the wishes of the people ( self - determination ) ; restoration of self - government to those deprived of it ; reduction of trade restrictions ; global cooperation to secure better economic and social conditions for all ; freedom from fear and want ; freedom of the seas ; and abandonment of the use of force , as well as disarmament of aggressor nations . [S3] Adherents of the Atlantic Charter signed the Declaration by United Nations on 1 January 1942 , which became the basis for the modern United Nations . [S4] The Atlantic Charter set goals for the postwar world and inspired many of the international agreements that followed the war . [S5] The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade ( GATT ) , the postwar independence of European colonies , and much more are derived from the Atlantic Charter .

Document: [S0] Viscount Alanbrooke , of Brookeborough in the County of Fermanagh , was a title in the Peerage of the United Kingdom . [S1] It was created on 29 January 1946 for Field Marshal Alan Brooke , 1st Baron Alanbrooke . [S2] He had already been created Baron Alanbrooke , of Brookeborough in the County of Fermanagh , on 18 September 1945 , also in the Peerage of the United Kingdom . [S3] Brooke was the sixth son of Sir Victor Brooke , 3rd Baronet , and the uncle of Sir Basil Brooke , 5th Bt . [S4] ( created Viscount Brookeborough in 1952 ) , the Prime Minister of Northern Ireland from May 1943 until March 1963 . [S5] Field Marshal Lord Alanbrooke was succeeded by his elder son , Thomas , who was unmarried and had no children . [S6] The titles were then held by his half - brother , Alan Brooke 's younger son , also named Alan ( but popularly known as Victor ) . [S7] The 3rd Viscount died on 10 January 2018 and the viscountcy became extinct on his death .

Document: [S0] The House of Hanover ( ) , whose members are known as Hanoverians ( ) , is a German royal house that ruled Hanover , Great Britain , and Ireland at various times during the 17th through 20th centuries . [S1] The house originated in 1635 as a cadet branch of the House of Brunswick - Lüneburg , growing in prestige until Hanover became an Electorate in 1692 . [S2] George I became the first Hanoverian monarch of Great Britain and Ireland in 1714 . [S3] At Victoria 's death in 1901 , the throne of the United Kingdom passed to her eldest son Edward VII , a member of the House of Saxe - Coburg and Gotha . [S4] The last reigning members of the House lost the Duchy of Brunswick in 1918 when Germany became a republic . [S5] The formal name of the house was the House of Brunswick - Lüneburg , Hanover line . [S6] The senior line of Brunswick - Lüneburg , which ruled Brunswick - Wolfenbüttel , became extinct in 1884 . [S7] The House of Hanover is now the only surviving branch of the House of Welf , which is the senior branch of the House of Este . [S8] The current head of the House of Hanover is Ernst August , Prince of Hanover .

Document: [S0] Load is the sixth studio album by the American heavy metal band Metallica , released on June 4 , 1996 by Elektra Records in the United States and by Vertigo Records internationally . [S1] The album showed more of a hard rock side of Metallica than the band 's typical thrash metal style , which alienated much of the band 's fanbase . [S2] It also featured influences from genres such as Southern rock , blues rock , country rock and alternative rock . [S3] Drummer Lars Ulrich said about Load more exploratory nature , " This album and what we 're doing with it – that , to me , is what Metallica are all about : exploring different things . [S4] The minute you stop exploring , then just sit down and fucking die " . [S5] At 79 minutes , it is Metallica 's longest studio album . [S6] Load debuted and spent four consecutive weeks at number one on the US Billboard 200 chart . [S7] Load sold 680,000 units in its first week , making it the biggest opening week for Metallica as well as the biggest debut of 1996 . [S8] It was certified 5× platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America ( RIAA ) for shipping five million copies in the United States . [S9] Four singles—"Until It Sleeps " , " Hero of the Day " , " Mama Said " , and " King Nothing "— were released as part of the marketing campaign for the album .

Document: [S0] Raymond Hermantier ( 13 January 1924 – 11 February 2005 ) was a French actor , born in Lyon , France as Raymond Maroutian . [S1] Raymond Hermantier aspired to acting since the age of 17 . [S2] His training was interrupted by World War II during which he served in the Free French Forces , until the liberation of Paris . [S3] Decorated by General Charles de Gaulle , he resumed his acting career immediately after the end of the war . [S4] Supported by André Malraux and Albert Camus , he ascended to fame at the Festival de Nîmes , France , in his role of Julius Caesar . [S5] After several movies and theater successes , he was offered the Directorship of the fledgling Senegalese National Theater by the King who aspired to a world - class national theater . [S6] This culminated in the National Theater of Senegal being the first African Shakespearean to tour major European capitals in 1974 . [S7] This success was followed by many successful tours of Europe over the next 13 years .

Document: [S0] The Romanian Revolution of 1989 , which ended the Communist regime of Nicolae Ceauşescu in December 1989 , offered the 15 religious denominations then recognized in Romania the chance to regain the terrain lost after 1945 , the year when Dr. Petru Groza of the Ploughmen 's Front , a party closely associated with the Communists , became prime minister . [S1] From that time , the Communist Party started a campaign of secularisation , seeking to transform the country into an atheistic state along Marxist - Leninist lines . [S2] Beginning with the 1989 revolution , the legally recognized churches , especially the Romanian Orthodox Church , the country ’s largest religious group , pressured the post - communist authorities to introduce religious education in public schools , offer substantial financial support for theological institutions and allow denominations to resume their social role by posting clergy in hospitals , elderly care homes and prisons . [S3] Although education was an area where churches registered success in the early stages of post - communist transition , religious education remains a low priority in Romania .

Document: [S0] Leonessa is a town and comune in the far northeastern part of the Province of Rieti in the Lazio region of central Italy . [S1] Its population in 2008 was around 2,700 . [S2] Situated in a small plain at the foot of Mt. [S3] Terminillo , one of the highest mountains of the Apennine range , in the winter Leonessa is known mostly as a low - key staging center for the ski slopes of the Terminillo , and in the summer as a weekend vacation town frequented for the most part by Romans with local roots . [S4] Historically , the town is known mostly as the birthplace of St. Giuseppe di Leonessa . [S5] Until 1927 it was part of the province of L'Aquila . [S6] The town suffered one of the worst German reprisals during World War II when the Wehrmacht and the SS killed 51 inhabitants in early April 1944 . [S7] A monument dedicated to the dead was erected in 1959 . [S8] Typical food production include the local variety of potato , known as patata di Leonessa . [S9] Leonessa is twinned with the French town of Gonesse .

[S5] The team also one of the teams to participate in friendly match against football club that visited Hong Kong , along with Hong Kong national football team and Hong Kong League XI . Document: [S0] Pettigrew State Park is a North Carolina State Park in Tyrrell and Washington Counties , North Carolina in the United States . [S1] It covers around the shore lines of Lake Phelps and the Scuppernong River . [S2] The park 's developed facilities are south of U.S. Route 64 near Roper and Creswell , North Carolina . [S3] Pettigrew State Park is open for year - round recreation , including hiking , camping , fishing , boating and picnicking . [S4] Pettigrew State Park is named for Confederate General J. Johnston Pettigrew , who lived in a nearby home . [S5] It surrounds Somerset Place , a North Carolina state historic site that includes a restored 1830s plantation house and outbuildings that can be toured , including reconstructed slave quarters . [S6] Pettigrew State Park was established during the Great Depression after the land was leased from the Farm Security Administration , a New Deal program of U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt . [S7] Part of Pettigrew State Park surrounds Lake Phelps , one of the oldest lakes in the eastern United States and a former hunting and fishing ground for the Algonquian peoples . [S8] Archaeologists have found dugout canoes in the lake that are up to 4,400 years old , preserved by its unusually clean waters . [S9] Pettigrew is home to an abundance of wildlife : Lake Phelps is a primary wintering location for several types of waterfowl , including Canada geese and Tundra swans . [S10] The park is also home to the woodland creatures , such as raccoons and white - tailed deer , that are commonly found along the east coast of the United States . [S11] Lake Phelps contains several species of game fish including largemouth bass and catfish . [S12] The park also manages the Lake Phelps , which is a North Carolina State Lake . [S13] All together , the park manages .

Document: [S0] The Ålgård Line ( ) is a closed , but not abandoned , railway line between Ganddal and Ålgård in Rogaland , Norway . [S1] The line was built as a narrow gauge branch line of the Jæren Line by the Norwegian State Railways ( NSB ) and opened in 1924 . [S2] It runs through the villages of Foss - Eikeland and Figgjo in Sandnes to Ålgård in Gjesdal . [S3] Several proposals were made for the Ålgård Line to become the first part of the main line from Stavanger to Oslo , but instead the Sørlandet Line was connected to the Jæren Line in 1944 . [S4] At the same time , the Ålgård Line was upgraded to standard gauge . [S5] The line had up to ten daily round trips with diesel multiple units , until passenger traffic was terminated in 1955 . [S6] Freight traffic remained until 1988 , when most of the line was abandoned in 1988 , although was used until 2001 . [S7] The line is owned by the Norwegian National Rail Administration . [S8] The station at Figgjo has been converted to a museum , and the section from there to Ålgård is used for recreational draisines . [S9] There have been proposals to reopen the line either as part of the Jæren Commuter Rail or the planned light rail for Greater Stavanger .

Document: [S0] The Blue River is a tributary of the Colorado River , approximately long , in the U.S. state of Colorado . [S1] It rises in southern Summit County , on the western side of the continental divide in the Ten Mile Range , near Quandary Peak . [S2] It flows north past Blue River and Breckenridge , then through the Dillon Reservoir near Dillon . [S3] The West portal for the " Roberts Tunnel " is at the base of Dillon Reservoir . [S4] The Roberts Tunnel is a trans - basin diversion , built by Denver Water in 1962 , that diverts water under the Continental Divide from the Colorado River basin into the South Plate River Basin . [S5] The East portal is approximately one mile upstream of Grants , Colorado . [S6] North of Dillon the river flows NNW along the eastern slope of the Gore Range and joins the Colorado River at Kremmling . [S7] The Green Mountain Dam , upstream from Kremmling , forms the Green Mountain Reservoir , providing hydroelectric power and diversionary water for irrigation , as part of the Colorado - Big Thompson Project . [S8] The dam is a project of the United States Bureau of Reclamation .

Document: [S0] Joseph Reid Anderson ( February 16 , 1813 – September 7 , 1892 ) was an American civil engineer , industrialist , politician and soldier . [S1] During the American Civil War he served as a Confederate general , and his Tredegar Iron Company was a major source of munitions and ordnance for the Confederate States Army . [S2] Starting with a small forge and rolling mill in the mid-1830s , It was a flourishing operation by 1843 when he leased it . [S3] He eventually bought the company outright in 1848 and forcefully and aggressively built Tredegar Iron Works into the South 's largest and most significant iron works . [S4] When the Civil War broke out he entered the Army as a Brigadier General in 1861 . [S5] Shortly after he was wounded and then resigned from the Army returning to the iron works . [S6] It was the Confederacy 's major ( and for much of the war only ) source of cannons and munitions , employing some 900 workers , most of whom were slaves . [S7] His plant was confiscated by the Union army at the end of the war , but returned to him in 1867 and he remained president until his death . [S8] Anderson was very active in local civic and political affairs .

Document: [S0] Sycamore Canyon Wilderness is a 56,000-acre ( 22,662 ha ) wilderness area in the Coconino , Kaibab and Prescott national forests in the U.S. state of Arizona . [S1] Encompassing Sycamore Canyon and its surrounds from south of Williams to the confluence of Sycamore Creek with the Verde River , the wilderness is about 40 miles ( 64 km ) southwest of Flagstaff . [S2] The canyon is one of several in Arizona that cut through the Mogollon Rim . [S3] Relevant United States Geological Survey ( USGS ) map quadrangles are Davenport Hill , White Horse Lake , May Tank Pocket , Perkinsville , Sycamore Basin , and Clarkdale . [S4] Red Rock - Secret Mountain Wilderness borders Sycamore Canyon Wilderness on the east . [S5] Ring - tailed cats , black bears , mountain lions , elk , deer , rattlesnakes , scorpions , canyon wrens , hermit thrushes , and many other creatures frequent the wilderness . [S6] Vegetation , which varies with elevation and the availability of water , includes stands of pine , fir , sycamore , walnut , and cottonwood . [S7] The canyon walls include exposures of red sandstone , white limestone , and brown lava . [S8] Parts of the wilderness are open for dispersed camping ; many trails are open for horseback riding as well as hiking .

[S5] " , the words attributed to King Henry II which led to Becket 's death in 1170 , and embark on a mission to murder Edmund . [S7] The Catholic Church was to be satirized again in the second series , Blackadder II , in the 1986 episode " Money " .

Document: [S0] The Enterprise Objects Framework , or more commonly simply EOF , was introduced by NeXT in 1994 as a pioneering object - relational mapping product for its NeXTSTEP and OpenStep development platforms . [S1] EOF abstracts the process of interacting with a relational database by mapping database rows to Java or Objective - C objects . [S2] This largely relieves developers from writing low - level SQL code . [S3] EOF enjoyed some niche success in the mid-1990s among financial institutions who were attracted to the rapid application development advantages of NeXT 's object - oriented platform . [S4] Since Apple Inc 's merger with NeXT in 1996 , EOF has evolved into a fully integrated part of WebObjects , an application server also originally from NeXT . [S5] Many of the core concepts of EOF re - emerged as part of Core Data , which further abstracts the underlying data formats to allow it to be based on non - SQL stores .

Document: [S0] The Battle of Kashii ( 樫井の戦い ) was the very first battle of the Summer Campaign of the 1615 Siege of Osaka , near the beginning of the Edo period in Japan . [S1] It took place on the 26th day of the 4th month of the Keichō era . [S2] As the Shōgun 's Eastern Army prepared to renew , the siege begun the previous winter , the Ōsaka garrison sallied forth , ambushing Tokugawa forces in a number of skirmishes and sieges . [S3] In the battle of Kashii , a contingent of forces loyal to Toyotomi Hideyori , lord of Ōsaka , attempted to besiege Wakayama Castle , which was controlled by Asano Nagaakira , an ally of the shōgun . [S4] The attackers were led by Ōno Harunaga , Hanawa Naoyuki , and Okabe Noritsuna . [S5] Asano 's garrison realized that their attackers were far from support or reinforcements , and met them in battle at Kashii , a short distance from Wakayama . [S6] Okabe and Hanawa were killed in the battle , and Ōno was therefore forced to retreat back to Ōsaka .

[S1] Girls ideally wore them as an apotropaic amulet , the equivalent of the boy 's bulla . [S2] In the popular belief the Romans wore amulets usually as a talisman , to protect themselves against evil forces , demons and sorcery , but especially against the evil eye . [S3] In Plautus ' play , Epidicus asks the young girl Telestis : " Do n't you remember my bringing you a gold lunula on your birthday , and a little gold ring for your finger ? " [S4] An explicit definition is provided by Isidore of Seville : " Lunulae are female ornaments in the likeness of the moon , little hanging gold bullae . " [S5] But in Plautus ' play Rudens , Palaestra says her father gave her a golden bulla on the day of her birth . [S6] There is also some indication that babies of both sexes wore phallic amulets .

[S1] He is revered as being an ideal example of non - attachment to material possessions . [S2] As a king , he had access to luxuries and pleasures far beyond the ordinary , but his internal state was closer to that of a sadhu . [S3] He was intensely interested in spiritual discourse and considered himself free from worldly illusions . [S4] His interactions with sages and seekers such as Ashtavakra and Sulabha are recorded in ancient texts . [S5] His relationship with adopted daughter Sita led her to be called Janaki Mata . [S6] The Nepalese city of Janakpur is named for him and daughter Sita . [S7] The Videha ( or Mithila ) kingdom was located between east of Gandaki River , west of Mahananda River , north of Ganga river and south of Himalayas . [S8] The region is now divided between the present day Indian state of Bihar and a small part of Terai Region in Nepal .

Document: [S0] Ulysses is a modernist novel by Irish writer James Joyce . [S1] It was first serialised in parts in the American journal The Little Review from March 1918 to December 1920 and then published in its entirety in Paris by Sylvia Beach on 2 February 1922 , Joyce 's 40th birthday . [S2] It is considered to be one of the most important works of modernist literature and has been called " a demonstration and summation of the entire movement " . [S3] According to Declan Kiberd , " Before Joyce , no writer of fiction had so foregrounded the process of thinking " . [S4] Ulysses chronicles the peripatetic appointments and encounters of Leopold Bloom in Dublin in the course of an ordinary day , 16 June 1904 . [S5] Ulysses is the Latinised name of Odysseus , the hero of Homer 's epic poem the Odyssey , and the novel establishes a series of parallels between the poem and the novel , with structural correspondences between the characters and experiences of Leopold Bloom and Odysseus , Molly Bloom and Penelope , and Stephen Dedalus and Telemachus , in addition to events and themes of the early 20th - century context of modernism , Dublin , and Ireland 's relationship to Britain . [S6] The novel is highly allusive and also imitates the styles of different periods of English literature . [S7] Since its publication , the book has attracted controversy and scrutiny , ranging from an obscenity trial in the United States in 1921 , to protracted textual " Joyce Wars " . [S8] The novel 's stream - of - consciousness technique , careful structuring , and experimental prose — replete with puns , parodies , and allusions — as well as its rich characterisation and broad humour , have led it to be regarded as one of the greatest literary works in history ; Joyce fans worldwide now celebrate 16 June as Bloomsday .

Document: [S0] The National Turkey Federation ( NTF ) is the non - profit national trade association based in Washington , D.C. , United States , representing the turkey industry and its allies and affiliates . [S1] NTF advocates for all segments of the turkey industry , providing services and conducting activities which increase demand for its members ' products . [S2] The NTF represents its members before the U.S. Congress and the various regulatory agencies , such as the U.S. Department of Agriculture 's Food Safety and Inspection Service . [S3] Among members of the general public , NTF is best known for its role in the National Thanksgiving Turkey Presentation , an annual ceremony where a live domestic turkey is presented to the President of the United States just before Thanksgiving Day . [S4] NTF began presenting the National Thanksgiving Turkey during the presidency of Harry Truman . [S5] The custom of " pardoning " the turkey started with Bush I in 1989 , Two birds are brought to the White House for final selection and the President invariably grants a " pardon " to both birds . [S6] Its official website , EatTurkey.com , is home to thousands of turkey recipes , cooking and preparation tips , and educational information on the turkey industry .

Document: [S0] Henry Wager Halleck ( January 16 , 1815 – January 9 , 1872 ) was a United States Army officer , scholar , and lawyer . [S1] A noted expert in military studies , he was known by a nickname that became derogatory : " Old Brains . " [S2] He was an important participant in the admission of California as a state and became a successful lawyer and land developer . [S3] Halleck served as General - in - Chief of all Union armies during the American Civil War . [S4] Early in the Civil War , Halleck was a senior Union Army commander in the Western Theater . [S5] He commanded operations in the Western Theater from 1861 until 1862 , during which time , while the Union armies in the east were defeated and held back , the troops under Halleck 's command won many important victories . [S6] However , Halleck was not present at the battles , and his subordinates earned most of the recognition . [S7] The only operation in which Halleck exercised field command was the Siege of Corinth in the spring of 1862 , a Union victory which he conducted with extreme caution . [S8] Halleck also developed rivalries with many of his subordinate generals , such as Ulysses S. Grant and Don Carlos Buell . [S9] In July 1862 , following Major General George B. McClellan 's failed Peninsula Campaign in the Eastern Theater , Halleck was promoted to general - in - chief of all U.S. armies . [S10] Halleck served in this capacity for about a year and a half . [S11] Halleck was a cautious general who believed strongly in thorough preparations for battle and in the value of defensive fortifications over quick , aggressive action . [S12] He was a master of administration , logistics , and the politics necessary at the top of the military hierarchy , but exerted little effective control over field operations from his post in Washington , D.C. His subordinates frequently criticized him and at times ignored his instructions . [S13] President Abraham Lincoln once described him as " little more than a first rate clerk . " [S14] In March 1864 , Grant was promoted to general - in - chief , and Halleck was relegated to chief - of - staff . [S15] Without the pressure of having to control the movements of the armies , Halleck performed capably in this task , ensuring that the Union armies were well - equipped .

[S1] On Easter morning 1972 , Captain Ripley repeatedly exposed himself to intense enemy fire over a three - hour period as he prepared to blow up an essential bridge in Dong Ha . [S2] His actions significantly hampered the North Vietnamese Army 's advance into South Vietnam . [S3] The story of " Ripley at the Bridge " is legendary in the Marine Corps and is captured in a gripping diorama at the United States Naval Academy . [S4] On October 28 , 2009 , the first biography about Col . Ripley was published . [S5] It was written by Norman Fulkerson and is titled An American Knight , The Life of Col . John W. Ripley .

[S8] His father Antoine arranged for Henri to marry Anne Phélypeaux in 1613 . [S9] Her father and uncle were Raymond Phélypeaux and Paul Phélypeaux , both secretaries of state and highly influential men . [S10] His son , Louis de Buade , Compte de Frontenac at de Pulluau , was born in 1620 . [S11] King Louis XIII acted as godfather to the boy , who was named after him . [S12] Henri de Buade became a colonel in the Regiment of Navarre . [S13] He was killed in 1622 during a military campaign . [S14] His heart was removed , sealed in a lead box , and buried in the church at Palluau . [S15] Henri 's son Louis later became Lieutenant General of the colony of New France in North America .

Document: [S0] Zillebeke Churchyard Commonwealth War Graves Commission Cemetery forms part of the village churchyard located around the Catholic parish church of Zillebeke in Belgium . [S1] A section of the parish churchyard used by the inhabitants of Zillebeke is maintained as a war cemetery by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission as a burial ground for the dead of the First World War near Ypres ( now Ieper ) on the Western Front . [S2] The grounds of the war cemetery were assigned to the United Kingdom in perpetuity by King Albert I of Belgium in recognition of the sacrifices made by the British Empire in the defence and liberation of Belgium during the war . [S3] Within Zillebeke Churchyard CWGC Cemetery there is a section with war graves of soldiers from aristocratic backgrounds ; this plot is called The Aristocrat 's Cemetery .

Document: [S0] Souvlaki ( Greek : ) , plural souvlakia , is a popular Greek fast food consisting of small pieces of meat and sometimes vegetables grilled on a skewer . [S1] It is usually eaten straight off the skewer while still hot . [S2] It can be served with pita bread , fried potatoes , lemon , and sauces , but the souvlaki itself is eaten on its own , with the side dishes eaten subsequently . [S3] The meat usually used in Greece and Cyprus is pork , although chicken , beef , and lamb may also be used . [S4] In other countries ( and for tourists ) , souvlaki may be made with meats such as lamb , beef , chicken , and sometimes fish . [S5] The word souvlaki is a diminutive of the Medieval Greek σούβλα souvla ' skewer ' , itself borrowed from Latin subula . [S6] ' Souvlaki ' is the common term in Hellenic Macedonia and other regions of northern Greece , while in southern Greece around Athens it is commonly known as ' kalamaki ' , ' reed ' .

Document: [S0] " Amambanda " was the Dutch entry in the Eurovision Song Contest 2006 , performed predominantly in an imaginary language but with some words in English by Treble . [S1] This was the second occasion on which a song had been performed with lyrics in an invented language - Belgium having entered Sanomi by Urban Trad at the 2003 Contest . [S2] The song is an up - tempo number , with many influences from African and flamenco music . [S3] The lyrics explain that " There is a way / To understand without a language " , in keeping with the musical theme of exuberant joy in spite of an apparently insurmountable language barrier . [S4] The title was the cause of much confusion prior to the Contest , with the official CD of entries titling the track " Amanbanda " ( with an " n " instead of an " m " ) . [S5] BBC commentary referred to the song as " Amamdangda " briefly , as well as describing the group as " a mother and her two daughters " , which was also incorrect as Caroline Hoffman was not the mother of the two van Dijk sisters , though this comment was sarcastic and not taken as literal by listeners . [S6] As the Netherlands had not finished the 2005 Contest in the top 10 , the song was performed in the semi - final . [S7] Here , it was performed seventeenth , following Finland 's Lordi with " Hard Rock Hallelujah " and preceding Lithuania 's LT United with " We Are The Winners " . [S8] At the close of voting , it had received 22 points , placing 20th in a field of 23 and thus missing out on the final and requiring the Netherlands to qualify from the semi - final at the next Contest . [S9] Immediately following this result , rumours began to circulate that the Netherlands would opt out of the next Contest . [S10] These rumours were , however , proven to be untrue as the country began qualification for the 2007 Contest . [S11] It was succeeded as Dutch representative at the 2007 Contest by Edsilia Rombley with " On Top of the World " .

Document: [S0] In Sunni Islam , an imam khatib ( or just imam , ) is a leader , often the leader of prayers in the masjid , and the Muslim community . [S1] This compound title is merely a common combination of two elementary offices : leader ( imam ) of the congregational prayer , which in larger mosques is performed at the times of all daily prayers ; and preacher ( khatib ) of the sermon or khutba at the required congregational prayer on Friday . [S2] Although either duty can be performed by anyone who is regarded as qualified by the congregation , at most well - established mosques imam khatib is a permanent ( part - time or full - time ) position . [S3] He may be elected by the local community , or appointed by an outside authority — e . [S4] g. , the national government , or the waqf which sustains the mosque . [S5] There is no ordination as such ; the only requirement for appointment as an imam khatib is recognition as someone of sufficient learning and virtue to perform both duties on a regular basis , and to instruct the congregation in the basics of Islam . [S6] Similar to spiritual leaders , the imam khatib is the one who leads Islamic worship services . [S7] More often , the community turns to the mosque imam if they have a religious question . [S8] In smaller communities , an imam could also be the community leader . [S9] The term is not to be confused with the use of Imams of Shi'a Islam , where it has a meaning more central to belief , referring to main leaders of the Shi'a community . [S10] The term imam is also used for a recognized religious scholar or authority in Islam , often for the founding scholars of the four Sunni madhhabs , or schools of jurisprudence ( fiqh ) . [S11] It may also refer to the Muslim scholars who created the analytical sciences related to Hadith or it may refer to the heads of the Prophet Muhammad 's family in their generational times . [S12] In other words , Imam Ali , referring to Ali ibn Abi Talib , is a phrase commonly used by both Shi'a and Sunni Muslims , though with different connotations . Document: [S0] A life - size bronze statue of Jan Smuts by the British artist Jacob Epstein stands on the north side of Parliament Square in London , United Kingdom , between a statue of Lord Palmerston and a statue of David Lloyd George . [S1] Smuts served as an army general and as a member of the Imperial War Cabinet in the First World War , and then served as Prime Minister of South Africa twice , from 1919 to 1924 and from then 1939 to 1948 . [S2] The statue depicts him in his military uniform as a field marshal , leaning forward with his left leg advanced , as if walking forward . [S3] The statue stands on a pedestal of granite from South Africa , which bears the inscription . [S4] After Winston Churchill won the 1951 UK general election in October 1951 , he proposed erecting a statue in Parliament Square as a memorial to Smuts , who had died in September 1950 . [S5] Churchill retired as prime minister in 1955 , and was too ill to perform the unveiling in November 1956 ; it was unveiled instead by the Speaker of the House of Commons , William Morrison . [S6] The statue became a Grade II listed building in 1970 .

Document: [S0] Lucien L'Allier ( 1909 - 1978 ) was a Canadian engineer who is best known for having built the Montreal Metro , the city 's subway system . [S1] Born in the suburb of Saint - Laurent , Quebec he studied with the Frères des écoles chrétiennes , Collège Sainte - Marie de Montréal and McGill University , from which he graduated with a degree in electrical engineering . [S2] In 1935 , he took part in a three - year project working on the telephone networks of Bell Canada , and later worked for the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation as regional engineer until 1946 . [S3] In 1946 , he joined the staff of the city of Montreal , and became the city 's engineering director in 1954 . [S4] In 1961 the construction of the Montreal Metro began . [S5] He supervised a construction project with 5000 workers . [S6] McGill University awarded him an honorary doctorate in 1964 . [S7] The same year , he was appointed Chairman of the Montreal Transit Commission , a position he held until his retirement in 1974 . [S8] After his death in 1978 , a Metro station was renamed in his honor . [S9] Rue de l'Aqueduc , north of rue Saint - Jacques , became rue Lucien - L'Allier in 1979 . [S10] In 2001 , the Réseau de transport métropolitain railway Lucien - L'Allier station adjacent to the metro station was also renamed .

Document: [S0] Angry Candy is a 1988 collection of short stories by American writer Harlan Ellison , loosely organized around the theme of death . [S1] The title comes the last line of the poem " the Cambridge ladies who live in furnished souls " by E. E. Cummings , " ... the/ moon rattles like a fragment of angry candy . " [S2] The collection contains the short story " Eidolons " , which won the 1989 Locus poll award for best short story . [S3] It also contains the novelette " Paladin of the Lost Hour " , winmer of a Hugo award for best novelette and later converted by Ellison into an episode of the television series The New Twilight Zone , as well as the short story " Soft Monkey " , which won Ellison his second Edgar Award , in 1988 . [S4] Angry Candy was nominated for a Bram Stoker Award and won a World Fantasy award for best collection of short stories .

Document: [S0] " Extraordinary Merry Christmas " is the ninth episode and mid - season finale of the third season of the American musical television series Glee , and the fifty - third overall . [S1] Written by Marti Noxon and directed by Matthew Morrison , the episode aired on Fox in the United States on December   13 , 2011 , and features the members of New Directions starring in a black - and - white Christmas television special that is presented within the episode itself . [S2] Nine songs are performed over the course of the episode , eight of which come from the second Glee Christmas soundtrack album , . [S3] The episode has the same name as an original song on that album , " Extraordinary Merry Christmas " , which was written for Glee by the show 's executive music producer Adam Anders , song producer Peer Åström , and Shelly Peiken . [S4] The remaining eight songs are covers , and all nine were released as singles . [S5] Reviewers generally praised the music in the episode . [S6] Although reviewers were polarized in their views of the episode as a whole , the special within the episode received mostly favorable comments , though the rest of the episode was deemed light on plot . [S7] Some aspects of the framing sequences were criticized , such as Rachel 's excessive demands for Christmas presents despite the fact that she is Jewish . [S8] Upon its initial airing , this episode was viewed by 7.13   million American viewers and garnered a 3.0/8   Nielsen rating / share in the 18–49 demographic . [S9] The total viewership was up marginally from the previous episode , " Hold On to Sixteen " .

Document: [S0] The Faliero Coup was a failed 1355 coup designed to overthrow Venice 's established republican government . [S1] Strains between the Venetian commoners and the nobility , originally stemming from the catastrophic failure of the nobility in the Battle of Porto - Longo against Venice 's long - time rival , Genoa , are largely considered to be the main cause for the coup . [S2] However , traditional stories also point to the marriage of Doge Marino Faliero as a possible cause for the coup . [S3] Faliero , an 81 year old man , had recently taken a young bride , who was rumored to be engaged in multiple affairs , including with Michele Steno , a Venetian statesman and future Doge . [S4] The consistent rumors and apparent intense arrogance of the established Venetian elite seems to have gotten to Faliero in this explanation for a coup . [S5] A more reasonable one , however , is that Faliero wished to transform Venice into a dictatorship , mirroring those of Genoa and other northern Italian city - states . [S6] This view is , however , disputed by some historians , who cite Faliero 's apparent regret at his trial , and , his lack of mentioning his belief that a dictatorship would better suit Venice 's interests , a valid argument . [S7] These two actions are much more consistent with a man regretting a passionate crime , than one who had executed a calculated plan , some argue . [S8] The coup was poorly organized and abortive . [S9] Faliero convened with two popular , wealthy , public figures who also had quarlles with the noblility : Bertuccio Isarello and Filippo Calendario . [S10] After convincing them of the need for a coup , he laid out his plan : Faliero and Isarello would recruit 20 trusted men who would assist in the overthrow of the government , who would each in turn recruit 40 each . [S11] However , due to the incredible variability of any given individuals ' reaction to the plan , rumors of unrest quickly began to spread throughout the city and , the Venetian people , fearing the civil turmoil which was swelling up all around them in northern Italy and Byzantium , reported the rumors to the authorities . [S12] One of the most powerful governmental bodies of Republican Venice , the Council of Ten , soon convened to discuss the rumors . [S13] They became concerned about the Doge 's role in the plot and , exercising emergency powers , together with the Doge 's councillors , the Signori di Notte , and the six sestieri , ordered the immediate and unquestioned arrest of Calendario and Isarello , who , upon questioning , implicated the Doge . [S14] After a series of quick albeit somber trials , the conspirators were imprisoned and executed , including Calendario , Isarello , and Doge Faliero .

[S1] According to Ketel 's biography , written by his contemporary Karel van Mander , he seems to have wanted to concentrate on the most prestigious of the hierarchy of genres , history painting , which included mythological subjects , but after he left France he is known almost entirely as a portrait - painter . [S2] Neither England nor Holland had much demand for large history paintings during his lifetime , and none of Ketel 's histories or allegorical paintings are known to have survived intact , although drawings and prints survive . [S3] He did however significantly influence the development of the largest type of painting commonly produced in the United Provinces at this period , the civic group portrait .

[S1] It was the first of two Luxembourgish entry in the contest and was performed in French . [S2] In contrast to most of the other entries of this Contest , the song is an up - tempo number , with Arnaud telling a friend or lover that the fact that he looks good at the moment is largely meaningless . [S3] She tells him that his looks are due to his youth and that , as for the rest of humanity , he will lose his hair , gain weight and possibly lose his teeth as well . [S4] Thus , she tells him that he should " take advantage of it " , rather than simply enjoying his looks at the time . [S5] The song was performed sixth on the night ( following France 's Mathé Altéry with " Le temps perdu " and preceding Italy 's Franca Raimondi with " Aprite le finestre " ) . [S6] As the scoreboard of this Contest has never been released , definitive statements about scores and positions are impossible to make , however the song did not win . [S7] The song was accompanied at the 1956 contest by Arnaud with " Les amants de minuit " and was succeeded as Luxembourgish representative at the 1957 contest by Danièle Dupré with " Amours mortes ( tant de peine ) " .

Document: [S0] Panlongcheng ( ) or Panlong City is an archaeological site associated with the Erligang culture . [S1] The site is located just north of the Yangtze river in Huangpi , Wuhan , Hubei , China . [S2] Panlongcheng is the largest excavated Erligang site ( 1   km² at its peak ) , showing the southernmost reach of the Erligang culture at its peak . [S3] It was discovered in 1954 , and excavated in 1974 and 1976 . [S4] The site at Panlongcheng was sparsely inhabited during the Erlitou period , consisting mainly of several small settlements and occupying an area of around 200,000 m² . [S5] During the early Erligang period , the site suddenly grew rapidly , reaching an area of around with a walled center of 75,000 m² . [S6] Panlongcheng may have been an Erligang outpost used to control regional resources , such as copper mines . [S7] The construction and bronze casting techniques at Panlongcheng are identical with the techniques employed at Erligang and Zhengzhou ; however , the pottery style is different . [S8] The style of Erligang elite burials is almost an exact replica of the burials at Zhengzhou ; however , later layers show that the Erligang style disappeared during the later stages of the Erligang culture . [S9] The site declined until it was abandoned altogether at the end of the Erligang culture . [S10] Panlongcheng 's decline may have been affected in part by the growth of the site at Wucheng . [S11] In Hubei Province , other sites such as Jingnansi and Baimiaozhu also feature Erlitou or Late Erlitou – Early Erligang type of ceramics .

[S2] Keitt is notable for being involved in two separate acts of legislative violence in the Congressional chambers . [S3] In the first , Keitt assisted Representative Preston Brooks ( D - SC ) in his 1856 attack on Senator Charles Sumner ( R - MA ) in the Senate chamber by brandishing a pistol and cane to prevent other Senators from coming to Sumner 's aid . [S4] The second was in 1858 , when he attacked and attempted to choke Representative Galusha Grow ( R - PA ) during an argument on the floor of the U.S. House . [S5] When the Civil War began , he served as a deputy of the Provisional Confederate States Congress and later as a colonel in the Confederate States Army , until he was mortally wounded at the Battle of Cold Harbor in June 1864 .

Document: [S0] Ahmet Kaya ( 28 October 1957 – 16 November 2000 ) was a folk singer from Malatya , Turkey . [S1] He was of mixed Kurdish - Turkish origin and often identified himself as a " Kurd of Turkey " . [S2] Many of his albums broke sales records . [S4] An elegy " Ya beni sararsa memleket hasreti / What if I am homesick " tells the story of his agony , suffering , longing for the people and homeland he was torn away from . [S5] Many believe this led to his sudden death at a very young age . [S6] Ahmet Kaya paid a huge price announcing his wish " to sing in the Kurdish language " when he was invited to stage to receive award at an award ceremony live on TV in 1999 . [S7] He was declared a villain by authorities ; targeted with fabricated news as a " traitor " by newspapers and TV stations nationwide . [S8] Turkish Media portrayed Kaya as " Part of the Kurdistan Worker 's Party and " with Abdullah Ocalan " as a result of his declaration of him being Kurdish .

Document: [S0] The Georgi Dimitrov Mausoleum ( ) was a ceremonial tomb on Prince Alexander of Battenberg Square in Sofia , Bulgaria , from 1949 to 1999 . [S1] The white marble mausoleum was built in 1949 to contain the embalmed body of Bulgaria 's first Communist leader , Georgi Dimitrov ( 1882 – 1949 ) , construction beginning immediately after the news of Dimitrov 's death . [S2] It was completed in just six days , the time it took Dimitrov 's body to be returned to Sofia from the USSR . [S3] Dimitrov 's body remained in the mausoleum until August 1990 , when Dimitrov 's remains were cremated and the ashes buried in the Sofia 's Central Cemetery . [S4] The mausoleum itself was destroyed by Prime Minister Ivan Kostov 's UDF government in 1999 after a heated nationwide debate . [S5] The prime minister and his party claimed that retaining the mausoleum was inappropriate following the fall of Communism in 1989 because it represented Bulgaria 's repressive past . [S6] Even within the government there was opposition to destroying the building , and an opinion poll revealed that two - thirds of the population opposed the demolition . [S7] Proposals were made to turn the mausoleum into a museum or art gallery because it contributed to the unique atmosphere of the capital city . [S8] In August 1999 , the government made four attempts to demolish the building . [S9] The first three failed because they relied on a single powerful explosion . [S10] The building did not budge after the first two attempts and tilted only slightly after the third . [S11] The fourth ( and successful ) attempt was carried out using a series of consecutive , less powerful explosions .

Document: [S0] Mendenhall Glacier ( also Sitaantaagu ) is a glacier about long located in Mendenhall Valley , about from downtown Juneau in the southeast area of the U.S. state of Alaska . [S1] The glacier and surrounding landscape is protected as part of the Mendenhall Glacier Recreation Area , a federally designated unit of the Tongass National Forest . [S2] The Juneau Icefield Research Program has monitored the outlet glaciers of the Juneau Icefield since 1942 , including Mendenhall Glacier . [S3] The glacier has also retreated since 1929 , when Mendenhall Lake was created , and over since 1500 . [S4] The end of the glacier currently has a negative glacier mass balance and will continue to retreat in the foreseeable future . [S5] Given that average yearly temperatures are currently increasing , and the outlook is for this trend to continue , it is actually possible that the glacier might experience a period of stabilization or slight advance during its retreating march . [S6] This is because increasing amounts of warm , moist air will be carried up to the head of the icefield , where colder ambient temperatures will cause it to precipitate as snow . [S7] The increased amount of snow will feed the icefield , possibly enough to offset the continually increasing melting experienced at the glacier 's terminus . [S8] However , this interesting phenomenon will fade away if temperatures continue to climb , since the head of the glacier will no longer have cold enough ambient temperatures to cause snow to precipitate .

Document: [S0] In the New York metropolitan area , the Metropolitan Transportation Authority ( MTA ) runs the New York City Subway , which is mostly manually operated . [S1] The subway system currently uses Automatic Block Signaling with fixed wayside signals and automatic train stops . [S2] Many portions of the signaling system were installed between the 1930s and 1960s . [S3] Because of the age of the subway system , some replacement parts must be custom built for the MTA , as they are otherwise unavailable from signaling suppliers . [S4] Additionally , some subway services have reached their train capacity limits and can not operate extra trains with the current system . [S5] There are two different schemes of signaling in the system . [S6] The most used scheme is found on all of the B Division , which consists of lines originally built to the Brooklyn – Manhattan Transit Corporation ( BMT ) and Independent Subway System ( IND ) 's wider specifications , as well as on most of the A Division , which consists of lines built to the narrower specifications of the Interborough Rapid Transit Company ( IRT ) . [S7] An older system was used on all of the A Division , but with the conversion of the IRT Dyre Avenue Line signals to the B Division scheme , this system is no longer in use . [S8] As part of the modernization of the New York City Subway , the MTA has plans to upgrade much of the system with communications - based train control ( CBTC ) technology , which will control the speed and starting and stopping of subway trains . [S9] The CBTC system is mostly automated and uses a moving block system – which reduces headways between trains , increases train frequencies and capacities , and relays the trains ' positions to a control room – rather than a fixed block system . [S10] This will require new rolling stock to be built for the subway system , as only newer trains can use CBTC .
